## Phase 7 · Slice 27 — the design pass: Photos · 2026-09-05

The brief: *make the app look like `ConnectSuite.dc.html`* — layout, spacing, type scale, radii,
elevation, motion — measured against the design file rather than recalled, and breaking nothing.
Photos first, because its grid was reported unusable.

### The identity column, and three tokens that were wrong for the whole build

Before any pane, the design file's own colour literals were counted rather than reasoned about from
`tokens.css`'s prose. Four departures, three of them chromatic:

| Role | `tokens.css` had | The design file has | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| accent fill | `#8b6bff` = rgb(**139**,107,255) | `#7c6bff` = rgb(**124**,107,255) | `#7c6bff` **34** times, `rgba(124,107,255,…)` **59** times, `rgb(139,…)` **zero** |
| success / live | `#32e58a` | `#34d399` | **34** occurrences |
| destructive | `#ff5d5d` | `#ff6b81` | **17** occurrences |
| panel radius | `18px` | `20px` | **34** occurrences, the second-commonest radius after the pill |

**Nothing renders wrong when an accent is fifteen steps off in one channel.** A violet is a violet,
`stylesheets.test.ts` has no opinion about which one, and every screenshot comparison in
`docs/evidence/` was read for layout. The four alpha tints below `--accent` had all inherited the
wrong base as `rgba(139,107,255,…)`, and six hand-written literals in `shell.css` and `float.css`
had it too.

`--radius-media: 12px` was **missing entirely** — 40 occurrences in the design, its commonest
non-pill radius — so the photo grid drew `--radius-control` and a photograph had the shape of a
button.

The `--accent-on-fill` contrast note was recomputed rather than left standing: `#0b0b12` on the
corrected accent is **5.05:1** (was 5.27), white is **3.89:1** (was 3.72). Both moved; the argument
— near-black, not white, because white fails AA at 13.5px/600 — did not. That is why the ratio is
recorded and not the verdict.

### Defect 88 — the Photos grid drew every tile on top of the two below it

The report was *thumbnails stacked and overlapping vertically*. Three causes were named in advance
and are different bugs: no height constraint on the tiles, collapsing grid rows, or images
overflowing their containers. The measurement, in the running app at the real display size:

```
container  display:grid  cols: 116px x5  gap: 8px  max-height: 560px
           grid-template-rows: 32px x 24          <- 24 rows of 32px
tile       116 x 116, aspect-ratio 1/1, overflow hidden
img        114 x 114 inside it
worst vertical overlap between any two of 24 tiles: 79px
```

So: **the tiles were never unconstrained** (116px throughout, from `aspect-ratio`) and **the images
were never overflowing** (114px inside a 116px box that clips). The rows collapsed — pitch 40px
under a 116px tile — and two of the three candidates are ruled out by the same reading.

Which property, isolated one at a time in the live page:

| tried | rows resolved to |
|---|---|
| as shipped | `32px` |
| `max-height: none` | **`119px`** — correct |
| `overflow-y: visible` | `32px` |
| `align-content: start` | `32px` |
| `grid-auto-rows: auto` | `32px` |
| an explicit `height` on the tile | `116px` — correct |

**A grid container with a definite block size sizes its `auto` rows against the space it has rather
than against its items' transferred `aspect-ratio` height** — and `aspect-ratio` on the item then
wins anyway and overflows the track it was given. `align-content` does not reach it; neither does
`grid-auto-rows`. A control run in a clean container confirmed the ordinary case works — an empty
`aspect-ratio: 1` item in a `repeat(4,1fr)` grid with no height gives **144px** rows — so the item
was never the fault.

**The fix is structural.** `.photos-scroll` owns the height and the overflow; `.photos-grid` owns
the columns and no height at all. A property tweak would put both jobs back on one element for the
next person to re-merge — and `.apps-grid` is the proof that this happens, having met the same
collapse once already and answered it with `grid-auto-rows: max-content`, which survives only
because an apps tile's height comes from its content. That grid is split the same way now.

**After, same instrument, same window:**

```
cols: 131.25px x4   rows: 131.25px   gap: 10px   radius: 12px
tile 131 x 131, square                worst vertical overlap: 0px
5 day-groups: Yesterday, Thursday, Wednesday, Tuesday, Monday
scroller is a grid: false
```

The restructure also buys the design's date grouping — `Today`, `Yesterday`, `14 May 2024` — which
was impossible while the scroller *was* the grid, because a scroller holding several headed grids
needs the grids to be separate elements.

**Where the guard went, and why not where the defect was.** `photosView.test.ts` renders this pane
against a DOM double and **passed throughout**. A double has no layout, so a grid whose rows have
collapsed and one whose rows are correct produce the identical tree. Adding view tests would have
been `CLAUDE.md`'s defect-67 shape exactly: more assertions at the layer that was already right. The
fault is two CSS declarations in one rule, and `stylesheets.test.ts` is the only file in the repo
that can see one. The rule it now holds: **a scrolling grid never also carries its own height.**

Its own control caught two instrument faults while it was being written, both worth recording:

- **The first parser silently dropped every rule nested inside an `@media`** — a parser wrong in the
  *safe* direction, which is the variety this repo records as worse than no check at all. Its
  control (*the parser saw the real sheets*) is what found it.
- **The first predicate had only two conditions** — grid + definite height — and flagged **eight**
  rules of which **all eight were fine**: five `place-items: center` icon boxes on a fixed square,
  two single fixed-height rows, and `.apps-grid`. One true positive in nine is a guard that gets an
  exception list, and an exception list nobody prunes is how a guard stops guarding. The
  discriminator is that **the defect needs more than one row**, and what guarantees more than one
  row is that the grid is *also the scroller*. All eight are fixtures now.

Shown red by restoring the shipped rule verbatim; put back.

### Defect 89 — what the album rail is actually showing

The rail draws **150 albums**, including `1389444597` as a name and two rows both reading *WhatsApp
Images*. Read off the device rather than guessed at:

```
bucket_id=-1829889111  Android/media/com.whatsapp/WhatsApp/Media/WhatsApp Images/
bucket_id=318896427    Android/media/com.whatsapp/WhatsApp/Media/WhatsApp Images/
bucket_id=278607672    WhatsApp/Media/WhatsApp Images/          <- pre-scoped-storage
bucket_id=1432227631   Android/.Trash/com.sec.android.gallery3d/.../WhatsApp Images/
```

`BUCKET_DISPLAY_NAME` is the **leaf directory name only**, so distinct paths collide. The fourth row
is Samsung Gallery's **trash**: the pane is showing the user their deleted photographs as an
ordinary album. It is not flagged `is_trashed` — that column returns nothing on this device, because
Samsung Gallery manages its own `.Trash` directory instead of using `MediaStore`'s trash. **Only the
path separates them, and `media.buckets` does not carry one.**

The numeric names are the same class of thing and are *correct*: real directories some app created
and named with a Unix timestamp. Prettifying them would invent a name for a place a person can
navigate to.

**Two surface-only workarounds were built, drawn, and removed** — and both were true sentences that
answered nothing:

| tried | what appeared on screen |
|---|---|
| append the item count | `Instagram / 34 / 34 items` — the count **is already the row's second column** |
| append `newestMs` | `WhatsApp · Latest Sep 4, …` on **both** rows it was meant to separate, truncated in a 188px rail |

Neither was caught by a test, because in each case the assertion and the defect were the same
sentence. Both were caught by looking at the running app. Nothing is drawn now: the counts already
differ and are already on the row, which is the whole of what this wire supports.

### The three refusals in the Photos detail column

The design's Quick actions card draws four controls. `media.*` is four verbs — `buckets`, `list`,
`thumb`, `original` — checked against `docs/protocol.md`:

| Design's control | Verb it needs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Import to Mac | `media.original` | **kept**, gated on the phone advertising the bulk channel |
| Share | none | **removed** |
| Set as Mac wallpaper | none | **removed** |
| Delete from phone | none — `fs.delete` is a *SAF path* compare-and-delete and cannot address a `MediaStore` id | **removed** |

Removed rather than greyed: a disabled control is a promise that it might light up, and these three
are not waiting on a permission or a reconnect. One line replaces all three, and it is **new copy,
flagged unratified**: *"Sharing, wallpaper and deleting are on the phone. Nothing on the wire carries
them."* No sentence in `docs/empty-and-failure-states.md` fits; the closest is Calls' *"Mute, speaker
and keypad tones are on the phone. Nothing on the wire carries them."* — the right shape with the
wrong subject, so this is that shape rather than a fourth new grammar.

The design's metadata grid reads Taken / Camera / ISO / Size. `media.list` carries **no filename and
no EXIF**, so **Camera and ISO are not drawn** — a row labelled `ISO` over an empty value is worse
than its absence. Kind, Type and *Saved by* are real and the design has no row for them, so they get
one; `Saved by` resolves through `ownerAppName` and the package id never reaches the row.

### Two instruments, both new, both in the repo

`scripts/shot.mjs` had been **named in `docs/evidence/phase-7-panes-2026-09-04/README.md` since the
last design pass and did not exist** — the shots were taken by a scratchpad script that no longer
survives, which is the complaint `phase7-panes-probe.mjs` opens with about its own numbers. It
refuses rather than writing a file it cannot vouch for: it aborts on a zoomed window
(`innerWidth !== outerWidth`, which Chromium persists across relaunches) and on a route that did not
land, and writes a sidecar carrying every bound it imposed.

`scripts/design-shot.mjs` renders one artboard of the design canvas in a separate headless Chrome —
separate because the design loads a `_ds_bundle.js` and a Google Fonts stylesheet that the app's own
CSP blocks — clicks the nav row, waits for the pane, and clips to the `1440px` artboard. The page is
a **stimulus that reports its effect**: a typo in `--page` refuses and lists the artboard's real nav
ids rather than silently screenshotting Overview under another pane's filename.

Both grew a check from their own first failure. `--prep` (a set-up click before the shutter) ran
**before** the settle in its first version: the click landed, its `expect` went true, and the pane's
own in-flight `refresh()` then cleared the selection during the settle — so the shot showed an empty
detail column under a stimulus that had genuinely succeeded. A set-up is only a set-up if nothing
overwrites it before the shutter, so it runs after. `--ready` was added the same way, after a
`--prep` correctly refused because it had fired at a grid that had not loaded yet.

**Evidence:** `docs/evidence/phase-7-design-2026-09-05/` — `photos-before.png` (the smear),
`photos-build.png`, `photos-design.png`, each with a `.json` sidecar naming the window size, the DPR,
the scrollbar state and the settle.

## Phase 7 · Slice 28 — the design pass: Calls, and the motion that was never built · 2026-09-05

Calls was already structurally right from the last pass — three columns at the design's
`300px / 1fr / 300px`, the filter strip, the running clock, the 3×4 keypad. What was left was
surface, and one thing the whole app was missing.

### Measured against the design, then changed

| | Was | Design | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| call-row radius | `--radius-tile` 14px | 12px | `--radius-media` |
| dial key height | 46px | 52px | 52px |
| Call button | flat `--accent`, 44px | `linear-gradient(135deg, …)`, 48px | gradient, 48px, and it **keeps its word** |
| row avatar | one accent tint for every contact | a solid per-contact fill, `#0b0b12` initials | `hsl(var(--disc-hue) 62% 66%)` |
| foot-of-card note | a plain paragraph | a `#111219` strip with a phone glyph | the design's strip, in every state |

**The Call button keeps its label rather than becoming the design's bare phone glyph**, and that is
a deliberate refusal of the design rather than an omission: this button has a second state,
`is-confirming`, which is the only thing between a mistyped number and a real call. A state a
control can express *only* by changing colour is one a colour-blind user cannot read at all.

### The avatar discs, and why the colour is keyed on the name

Fifty call rows carried fifty identical violet circles — a mark with no information in it — and the
initials inside were `--accent-text` on `--accent-tint`, **2.4:1**, which is a decoration rather
than a label. The design gives each contact a solid individual fill with near-black initials.

**The hue is keyed on the name (or the number when there is none), never on the initials**, and this
handset is why. Its log has six consecutive `VENKY SIT` rows — correctly one colour — and an `SB`
that is a different person from another `SB` two rows below. Keying on the two letters in the circle
would give different people the same disc, which is exactly the confusion the colour exists to
break. The test carries its own control: it asserts the two names *do* share initials before
asserting their hues differ, so it cannot pass over a pair that was never ambiguous.

**Saturation and lightness stay in the stylesheet.** A per-contact *colour* is the design's intent;
a per-contact *contrast ratio* is not, and a hash that produced lightness too would give some
contacts black-on-dark initials with nothing reporting which.

### `hueOf` moved rather than being copied

`notifications.ts` already had this function, for app tiles. A second one in `calls.ts` would have
been wrong twice: every renderer file is loaded as a plain script into one global scope, so a second
top-level `hueOf` is a redeclaration the compiler catches and the browser would not — and, more
importantly, two hash functions mean one person is teal on Calls and amber on Notifications with
nothing ever reporting it. It is `src/shared/discHue.ts` now, one rule with one home.

**Moving it produced the export/CommonJS trap this file already records, twice in a row.** The pane
threw `ReferenceError: iconSvg is not defined`, and then — one fix later — `discHue is not defined`.
Both are the same shape: the page provides these by loading them as plain scripts *before* their
callers, and under `node --test` nothing does, so a view test mounting the pane dies on the first
row it draws. Both symbols had been green a moment earlier because neither had a caller yet. The
tests now import them in the page's own order, and `discHue.ts` hangs itself on the global the way
`icons.ts` does.

### Card stagger — the design's `float-in`, and the reason a route change read as a cut

The design animates each top-level column of a pane in separately: `float-in .3s
cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)`, then `.05s`, then `.1s`. **It was never built.** `page-in` moves the
whole page as one block, so every card landed at the same instant and the eye was given no order to
read them in.

Three decisions, each with a wrong version that is identical in a still:

- **It hangs off `.page.route-in`**, which `shell.ts` re-adds on every navigation. A bare
  `animation` on the cards would run once at first paint and never again, because panes are shown
  and hidden with `hidden` rather than created — and a stagger you see once is decoration.
- **The delay comes from `nth-child`**, not a class per column. The DOM already knows the order;
  asking each column to declare its own position is a second expression of one fact.
- **It is opt-in per pane** (`.stagger`), not `.page > * > *`. A list of fifty call rows is not a
  card, and a 0.3s entrance on things that redraw continuously — the notification list, a live call
  card whose clock ticks every second — would animate on every tick.

Applied to Overview, Calls, Photos, Clipboard and Settings. The reduced-motion block in `tokens.css`
already switches every animation off globally.

### The idle card's void, and a duplicate selector under the threshold

`.calls-stage` carries `min-height: 400px` so the three columns read as a row rather than as a wide
banner over two tall ones. With the idle copy pinned to the top that left a **170px void** beneath
it, which reads as something that failed to load. It is centred now — measured at **112px above and
112px below** in a 400px card.

Getting there needed the flex chain fixed: `.calls-stage` was a block, so the idle state's
`min-height: 100%` resolved against an indefinite height, came out `auto`, and `justify-content:
center` had nothing to centre within. The first version of this fix **looked identical in the
screenshot** and was measured rather than eyeballed.

`min-height` also turned out to live in its own `.calls-stage` block **ninety lines** above the
main one. `stylesheets.test.ts`'s dead-declaration check treats a same-sheet duplicate under 100
lines apart as a deliberate override, so it passed — correctly, by its own definition. The threshold
is left alone: it was derived from a real population (every deliberate override 5–19 lines, a dead
block 408 apart) and retuning it on one data point would be replacing evidence with a guess. The two
rules are merged into one instead.

### The three remaining refusals from the brief, checked against the wire rather than recalled

| Design draws | Verb it would need | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **Video call** (Messages aside) | none — `call.dial` is `ACTION_CALL` and there is no video verb | **refused**; a video call is another app's, not ours to place |
| **Block contact** | none — and `BlockedNumberContract` is restricted to the **default dialer or SMS app**, which this is not and will not be | **refused, and it is a platform wall** rather than a missing verb |
| **Shared media** (Messages aside) | none — there is no MMS-parts verb on this wire at all; `sms.messages` carries text | **refused** |

The whole `sms` / `call` / `contacts` surface is thirteen verbs — `sms.threads`, `sms.messages`,
`sms.send`, `sms.received`, `sms.sent`, `call.log`, `call.dial`, `call.answer`, `call.reject`,
`call.incoming`, `call.ended`, `contacts.list`, `contacts.get` — enumerated out of
`docs/protocol.md` rather than remembered. **None of the three is drawn today**, so this records why
they must not be added rather than a change.

The **End-to-end encrypted** badge on Calls and **Encrypted** on Messages stay cut, as they were:
the link is encrypted and an SMS is not, and a badge on the message pane claims the second.

**Evidence:** `docs/evidence/phase-7-design-2026-09-05/calls-build.png`, `calls-design.png`,
`calls-compare.png`. Measured after: stage `400px` with `112 / 112` above and below, rows `56px` at
`12px`, keys `52px`, six discs six distinct fills with the three `VENKY SIT` rows correctly sharing
one. Mac suite **539 → 545**.

## Phase 7 · Slice 29 — the design pass: Settings, and defect 90 · 2026-09-05

### Defect 90 — every control the design draws shorter than 32px has been drawing at 32px

`button, .button { min-height: 32px }` is the app's control floor. Its own comment reasons about one
direction only:

> *"32px is the design's control height and the floor everything sits on; anything that needs to be
> taller simply is."*

**Nothing considered a control that needs to be shorter**, and `min-height` beats `height` in the
cascade, always, silently. Measured in the running app, each routed to its own pane first:

| rule | declares | drew |
|---|---|---|
| `.switch` | `24px` | **32px** |
| `.calls-tab` | `28px` | **32px** |
| `.clip-tab` | `28px` | **32px** |
| `.clip-clear` | `28px` | **32px** |
| `.overview-disconnect` | `28px` | **32px** |
| `.icon-button` | `24px` | *not measurable — it draws at 0 height on every pane it appears on, which is a separate question and not this one* |

The switch is the sharpest of them. Its own comment reads *"a 42×24 track, an 18px knob at 3px
margin"*, its declared value is exactly that, and inside a 32px track the knob sat 3px from the top
and **11px from the bottom** — off-centre, on five panes, with the correct number written directly
above it.

**Nothing in the repo could have caught it.** `tsc` is clean, no selector collides,
`stylesheets.test.ts` had no opinion, and a screenshot of a toggle 8px too tall looks like a toggle.
It was not found by looking; it was found by asking a different question — *which rules declare a
height under the floor?* — of the loaded stylesheets in the running app.

**The fix is `min-height: 0` on each of the six**, and the guard is in `stylesheets.test.ts`, which
reads the floor **out of the base rule** rather than holding `32` as a literal: a threshold typed
from memory is a pass criterion quoting a value the code does not write, which is a failure this
file already records. Shown red by removing the `min-height: 0` from `.switch`; put back.

#### The scan that found it was wrong twice first, and both faults are the ones this repo names

**1. It saw 17 rules out of 760 and reported nothing wrong, confidently.** The walk asked
`if (r.cssRules)` to decide whether a rule was a container. In Chromium a `CSSStyleRule` has a
**truthy, empty** `cssRules` — CSS Nesting — so every ordinary rule was treated as a container,
iterated over its zero children, and never examined. The output was a clean `[]`, which is the
answer anyone would have hoped for.

**2. Its first run was against a pane that was not routed**, so `querySelectorAll('.switch')`
returned nothing and the scan reported no distorted controls. The control it was given —
`document.styleSheets.length` — came back `3` and was **true and irrelevant**: it proved the sheets
were readable and said nothing about whether the elements were there. Changing the control to
`document.querySelectorAll('.switch').length` is what turned the second empty result into a visible
contradiction (control `1`, findings `0`) and led to fault 1.

**3. Five of the six then reported `drawn: 0`**, because they sit on panes that were hidden at the
time. Zero is not a height; it is the instrument's own limit. Each was re-measured after routing to
its own pane, and `.icon-button` — the one that still reads 0 — is recorded as **not measured**
rather than folded into the table as a pass or a failure.

#### And the guard's first version had two false positives

It matched the control vocabulary as a **substring anywhere in the selector**:

| flagged | what it is |
|---|---|
| `.switch-knob` (18px) | the `<span>` **inside** the switch — matched on "switch" |
| `.pill-tab.unbuilt::after` (5px) | a 5px dot — matched on "tab" |

Neither is a button and neither inherits the floor. The test is on the **trailing token** now — the
last class in the selector, whole — and pseudo-elements are excluded outright. Both are fixtures.
This is the same discipline the grid guard in Slice 27 needed, one slice later: a substring match
over selector text finds the thing's children and its decorations.

### Settings, measured against the design

| | Was | Design | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| grid gap | 24px | 16px | 16px — it was the only three-column pane in the app not using `--space-7` |
| rail row | padded box, 34px, 10px radius | 38px, 11px radius, 12.5px | 38px / 11px / 12.5px |
| rail row selection | grew a 1px border when picked, with `calc(… − 1px)` padding to undo the shift | — | a transparent border always present, colour only |
| pane title | `--text-card-title`, 21px | 19px | 19px |
| pane sub | 6px above, 20px below | flush under the title, 18px below | `0 0 18px` |
| row hover | none | `.cs-row` hover | `rgba(255,255,255,.02)` |
| toggle | 42×**32** | 42×24 | 42×24 (defect 90) |

Columns were already the design's `200px / 1fr / 320px`, verified at **200 / 583 / 320**.

**The selected rail row's `calc(… − 1px)` padding is worth naming as a shape rather than a bug.** It
was compensation: the row grew a border on selection, every row below it shifted two pixels, and the
padding was reduced by one to cancel it. A transparent border that is always present cannot shift
anything and needs no compensation. Wherever a `calc(… − 1px)` appears next to a conditional border,
it is the same thing.

### What is *not* changed: the row copy

The build's Settings descriptions run to two and three lines where the design's run to one — *"There
is no update server. ConnectSuite has no account and talks to nothing but your phone, so there is
nowhere for it to check."* against the design's *"Check for new versions in the background."* That
makes the pane taller than the design's and pushes its last row below the fold.

It is left alone. Those sentences are the *reason* beside each **Not yet**, they were written
deliberately as rows G3/G4/G7 in `docs/design-departures.md`, and shortening them to match a
mockup's rhythm would trade a true explanation for a shorter one. The pane scrolls and the sweep
reports the rows **reachable, 0 stranded**; a long pane is allowed to be long.

### The sweep accused a pane it should have stayed silent about

`scripts/card-visibility-sweep.mjs` reported, for Photos:

```
undefined  (untitled)   top=0 onScreen=0   gone  (scroller none)
```

`gone` is the one verdict that file exists to raise the alarm on. It was not a stranded card — the
Photos `.pane-sub` (`#photos-note`) is **empty until the first page of the album lands**, and the
sweep's `(untitled)` fallback manufactured a name for a nameless node, which then could not be
resolved back by that name.

That is worse than the gap the file already documents. `files` reporting **NOT MEASURED** was an
honest silence; this was a **false accusation**, produced by a fallback whose whole job was to be
helpful. The fallback is removed; a heading with no text is not a card.

**Evidence:** `docs/evidence/phase-7-design-2026-09-05/settings-build.png`, `settings-design.png`,
`settings-compare.png` — shot on the **General** pane with `--prep`, because the build opens on
Connection and the design opens on General, and a comparison of two different panes is not a
comparison. Sweep after: **23 cards, 20 visible at rest, 3 reachable, 0 stranded.** Mac suite
**545 → 549**.

## Phase 7 · Slice 30 — the design pass: Overview · 2026-09-05

### Two truncation defects, both measured rather than eyeballed

`scrollWidth > clientWidth` over every text node in the pane, before and after:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `.quick-sub` truncated | **5 of 8** | **0 of 8** |
| `.recent-detail` truncated | **4 of 4** (`3819 byt…`, `Samsu…`, `ver…`, `a…`) | **0 of 5** |
| `.recent-text` truncated | 0 | 0 |

**The quick-tile captions.** `quickTileSub` reused the screen's page `subtitle`, and the reasoning
for that was sound and is preserved: *"a caption written in this file is a claim about a screen,
made somewhere the screen cannot correct it."* It was the right **source** and the wrong **length**
— a tile is half a 1fr column and a page subtitle is a sentence, so *"Control your phone from your
Mac…"*, *"View, organise and import photos …"*, *"Send and receive SMS and chat m…"*, *"Copy on
either machine, paste on …"* and *"Make and receive phone calls fro…"* all ended in an ellipsis. An
ellipsis is not a caption; it is a sentence the layout could not afford.

The fix keeps the ownership and changes the length: `tileCaption` is a **second field on
`NavScreen`**, in the same table, beside the subtitle. One owner, two lengths. Twelve screens plus
the pairing screen carry one; the compiler refuses a screen without it.

**The recent-activity detail column.** The tracks were `74px 26px minmax(0, 1fr) auto` with
`max-width: 45%` on the item, which is circular: the `1fr` label track takes the free space, the
`auto` track is squeezed toward min-content, and a percentage max-width on the item then resolves
against whatever is left of it. Four rows out of four showed two characters and an ellipsis where a
value belonged. A **percentage track** is measured against the grid rather than against the
leftovers, so `minmax(0, 38%)` gives the two text columns a fixed ratio and each truncates on its
own content. `3819 bytes, automatically` and `Samsung SM-S938B` now read in full.

### Device status moved to the column the design draws it in

O4's rings were `overview-wide`, so they sat below Recent activity and *What this phone can do*, off
the bottom of an 841px window. The design puts Device status in **column two, beside Recent
activity**, and that is where they are now — measured at `top=543` in a 841px viewport, visible at
rest.

This is the sweep's own sharper rule rather than a preference: a card carrying a **state** must be
visible at rest, not merely reachable, because a person asking *how is the battery* does not scroll
to find out whether an answer exists. It is the one card on the screen whose entire content is a
number about the phone right now.

### Two guards caught the change while it was being made

- **`stylesheets.test.ts`**: the `grid-column` went into `shell.css` beside the other Overview
  column rules, while `.device-status-card` already had a rule in `styles.css`. One selector, two
  sheets, resolved by load order, silently — caught on the first run. It is one rule in
  `styles.css` now, with a note saying why it is not next to its siblings.
- **`overviewView.test.ts`**: the Notifications tile's zero-state assertion was
  `assert.match(sub, /notification/i)`, which went red the moment the caption became *"Mirror &
  reply"* — **over a pane behaving exactly as specified.** That is a test asserting a second
  expression of its own rule: what the rule says is *the tile shows the screen's caption when there
  is no count*, so it reads `tileCaption` out of `SCREENS` and compares, with a control that the
  table carries one at all.

### `shot.mjs` grew two preconditions from its own bad images

**It captured Overview twice with the page heading and the top of the sidebar missing.** Nothing was
scrolled: `document.scrollingElement.scrollTop` and `#page.scrollTop` both read **0**, and
`.page-head` measured at **y = −121** — the whole window's content above the viewport. It did not
reproduce after a clean relaunch, so **the cause is not established and is not claimed**; what is
established is that a session's accumulated probing can leave the page in a state where every scroll
offset reads zero and the picture is still wrong.

So the shot now resets the scroll *and then checks the pane's head is where it should be*, refusing
otherwise — the difference between an intention and a measurement, which is this file's own
recurring lesson. The reset runs **after** `--prep`, because a set-up may legitimately scroll to
reach what it clicks.

### Not changed

The design's Recent activity stamps a clock (`09:42`); this build shows elapsed time (`1m ago`).
Left alone: a dashboard list that is minutes old reads better relatively, and the Activity pane
carries the absolute times.

The design's title is *"Good morning, Chetan"*. This build's is *"Good morning"* with no name, which
is not an omission — the handoff's literal greeted every user of this app by the author's name at
every hour of the day, which is defect D1 in `docs/phase-9-distribution-audit.md`. The time-of-day
half is real and is drawn.

**Evidence:** `docs/evidence/phase-7-design-2026-09-05/overview-build.png`, `overview-design.png`,
`overview-compare.png`. Sweep after: **22 cards, 18 visible at rest, 4 reachable, 0 stranded.** Mac
suite **549 → 551**.

## Phase 7 · Slice 31 — Clipboard re-diff, and defect 91: the frame was a scroll port · 2026-09-05

### Defect 91 — `.app-window` could be scrolled out of place, permanently and invisibly

`shot.mjs` refused a Clipboard screenshot with *"the page head sits at y=−199"*. The precondition
added one slice earlier had done its job, and this time the cause was chased rather than relaunched
away:

```
.app-window   scrollTop: 199.5      overflow: hidden
document.scrollingElement.scrollTop: 0
#page.scrollTop:                     0
.page-head top:                   −199
```

**`overflow: hidden` removes the scrollbars and still makes the element a scroll port.** It can be
scrolled by `scrollIntoView`, by the browser revealing a focused descendant, or by any script that
sets `scrollTop` — and once it is, there is no scrollbar to show it and no wheel target to undo it.
The app's own header and sidebar sit above the viewport and stay there, while every scroll offset a
person would think to read still says zero.

**Who moved it, established rather than assumed.** Two candidates and they were separated by
measurement, not by argument:

| candidate | reading |
|---|---|
| ordinary keyboard focus on a control below the fold | focusing the Overview *Disconnect* button at `top=1085` scrolled **`#page` by 354** and left `.app-window` at **0** — correct behaviour, **not** the cause |
| `probe.mjs`'s `__probe.onScreen` | `el.scrollIntoView({ block: 'center' })` scrolls **every** scrollable ancestor and it restored only `box`, the one `scroller()` had chosen |

So the trigger was our own instrument, and that is fixed where it belongs: `onScreen` now records
the scroll position of every ancestor before the call and restores all of them. **An instrument that
leaves the app in a state it did not find it in is a stimulus with an unreported side effect** — the
same shape as a probe reporting bytes queued as bytes delivered, one layer over.

**The frame is hardened anyway, because "only our tooling can do it" is a statement about today.**
`.app-window` is `overflow: clip` now. `clip` cuts identically — the rounded corners and the ambient
blobs at `inset: −10%` are unaffected — and creates **no scroll container**, so nothing can scroll
this element by any route. Proven after the change: `win.scrollTop = 200` reads back **0**, and
`scrollIntoView` on a below-fold control leaves it at **0** with `.page-head` at **0**.

This window has exactly one scroller by design, `#page`, and now that is enforced by the platform
rather than by nobody happening to call the wrong thing.

### Clipboard, re-diffed and already matching

| | design | build |
|---|---|---|
| grid | `1fr 340px`, gap 16 | `795px 340px`, gap 16 |
| panel | `#1c1f2b`, radius 20 | `rgb(28,31,43)`, radius 20 |
| row | 72px | 75px (the extra 3 is the selection border) |
| kind badge | 36×36, radius 10 | 36×36, radius 10 |
| filter pill | 28px, radius 999 | 28px, radius 999 |
| Clear all | 28px, radius 9 | 28px, radius 10 |

**Two of those were wrong an hour earlier and are fixed by defect 90**: the filter pills and *Clear
all* both declare 28px and were drawing at 32px under the button floor. The clipboard re-diff's real
finding is that its own numbers had been right all along and the cascade was overriding them.

### One design affordance deliberately not built

The design's clipboard rows carry two hover actions — a **Copy** button and a **Star**. Neither is
built:

- **Star is Favourites**, and Favourites is already cut (K1–K6): this history is memory-only by
  decision — 20 entries, cleared on disconnect, gone on restart — and a star that vanished when the
  phone went out of range would be a lie about the word.
- **Copy is real and is one click away already**, in the detail panel. It is not added *inside the
  row* because `.clip-row` is a `<button>`: a button inside a button is invalid HTML and gives one
  target two meanings. Making the row a `div[role=button]` to gain a hover affordance would trade
  working keyboard semantics for a shortcut, on a pane where the action is already reachable.

**Evidence:** `docs/evidence/phase-7-design-2026-09-05/clipboard-build.png`, `clipboard-design.png`,
`clipboard-compare.png`.

## Phase 7 · Slice 32 — the polish audit, and defect 92 · 2026-09-05

The brief's last item is polish: *hover states, the nav pill travelling from live offsetTop, route
transition and card stagger, progress rings, toggles*. Each was **measured** rather than assumed,
and the audit found one defect and corrected one of my own readings.

### The nav pill: correct, and my first reading of it was not

The rule the pill is supposed to follow is that its Y comes from the **live `offsetTop` of the
current row**, never from an assumed pitch — group headers and the notification badge change the
rhythm, so an assumed pitch desynchronises.

The first measurement clicked all twelve rows in one synchronous loop and read
`getComputedStyle(pill).transform` immediately. It reported **9 of 12 mismatched**, every one stuck
at `pillY: 258`. That is the transition being read **mid-flight**: the pill has
`transition: transform var(--dur-pill)`, and a computed transform during a transition is the
current animated value, not the target.

Re-taken one row at a time, each click reported through `act` (the row must actually have become
current) and each read settled with `until: pillY === offsetTop`:

```
rows: 12   pill Y === row offsetTop: 12
```

**The pill is correct on every row.** So is the 40px pill over a 38px row — the pill is `top: -1px`
with a 1px border, so its 38px interior sits exactly on the row and the border falls outside it.
That was very nearly written up as a two-pixel defect.

Both halves are worth recording: **an animated property read at the moment it is animating is not a
reading**, and *"the number does not match"* is one sentence away from a change nobody needed.

### Defect 92 — eleven uses of four custom properties that do not exist

`.ring-value` and `.ring-caption` referenced `var(--text-strong)` and `var(--text-muted)`. **Neither
token is declared anywhere.**

A custom property that has never been declared makes the whole declaration **invalid at
computed-value time** — the property is not skipped and it does not fall back to a sensible default;
it becomes `inherit`. So `color: var(--text-strong)` silently means *whatever my parent is*, with no
error, no warning, a clean `tsc` and no selector collision.

Measured in the running app before the fix, and the mixture is what makes this class survive:

| site | should be | drew | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.ring-value` | `--text-primary` `#f4f4f7` | `#f4f4f7` | **correct by accident**, inherited |
| `.ring-caption` | `--text-meta` `#5b5e6e` | `#f4f4f7` | **wrong** — the caption *Charging* set at the exact weight of the 13px/600 value directly above it, so the pair had no hierarchy at all |

After: `.ring-caption` reads `rgb(91, 94, 110)` against a parent of `rgb(244, 244, 247)`.

**Some of it looked right, some of it looked like a design decision, and one misspelling produced
both.**

### The guard found five sites I had not, and then forced a better discriminator

Written as *every `var(--x)` must be declared somewhere*, it came back with **six more references**
than the two I had found by hand:

| orphan | uses | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `--text-secondary` | **4**, all in the Apps pane | a real orphan; `--text-body` was meant |
| `--dock-tint` | 2, in `.dock-tile` | **not an orphan** — `shell.ts` sets it per tile from `navModel.DOCK` |

`--dock-tint` is the useful half. A check that read only the stylesheets would have called it a
defect, and the fix would have been an exception list — which is how a guard stops guarding. It
reads `setProperty('--x', …)` out of the TypeScript instead, so a property is declared if *something
in this app declares it*, wherever that is. `--disc-hue` from this morning's Calls work is covered by
the same clause.

**What is not claimed:** the four `--text-secondary` sites are `.apps-banner-detail`,
`.apps-banner-fix`, `.apps-tile-name.mono`, `.apps-toast-fix` and `.apps-empty-detail` — a refusal
banner, a fallback label for a package with no launcher name, a toast hint and an empty state. **None
of them renders on this device**: all 122 launcher packages resolve their names, the phone is
advertising `apps`, and there is nothing to be empty about. So the defect is established
**statically** — an undeclared property is invalid at computed-value time by specification, not by
inference — and its *visible* consequence in that pane is **unmeasured**, said here rather than
implied.

The guard is the natural sibling of *"only tokens.css declares a colour token"*: that one says where
a token may be **born**, and this one says a token must be born before it is **used**. Shown red by
restoring `var(--text-muted)` to `.ring-caption`; put back.

### The rest of the polish list, as measured

| | reading |
|---|---|
| hover states | **47** selectors carry a `:hover` rule across the three sheets |
| route transition | `page-in`, keyed to `.page.route-in`, re-added by `shell.ts` per navigation |
| card stagger | `float-in` — **built this sitting** (Slice 28); five panes opt in |
| progress rings | drawn as SVG with `transition: stroke-dashoffset 240ms`; a transition fires on a *change*, and the arc is created at its final offset, so **the rings do not sweep in** — the design toggles a `rings` flag 140ms after mount to make them. Left as is and recorded: it is a one-line addition that changes what the pane does on every redraw, and this pane redraws on every `battery.state` |
| toggles | 42×24 as of defect 90, three hours ago; they had drawn at 42×32 since they were written |
| keyframes present | `page-in`, `float-in`, `cmdk-in`, `toast-in`, `halo`, `drift`, `deep-reveal-flash` |
| keyframes in the design and not here | `win-in` (the mockup's own window entrance — this app *is* the window), `shimmer` (a loading skeleton; this build uses flat placeholders deliberately, because a grid of animated placeholders over a wait measured in milliseconds is a lot of motion) |

Mac suite **551 → 555**.

### A correction to a number this repo has published: the sweep was scrolling the app as it measured

`docs/RESUME.md` and Slice 25 carry **"23 blocks, 21 visible at rest, 2 reachable, 0 stranded"** at
1440×865. Today's run of the same script reads:

```
23 cards: 15 visible at rest, 8 reachable by scrolling, 0 stranded
```

**That is not a regression, and the earlier number should not be quoted again.** Defect 91 is the
reason: `__probe.onScreen` called `scrollIntoView`, which scrolls every scrollable ancestor, and
restored only the one scroller it had chosen — so `.app-window` accumulated scroll *during the
sweep*. The first pane measured was measured correctly and every pane after it was measured with the
frame progressively pushed up, which makes cards appear **higher** than they are and inflates
"visible at rest". The instrument's own error pointed in the flattering direction, which is the
variety this file records as the hardest to notice.

The evidence for the mechanism, rather than the story: individual cards read **~120px lower** today
than they did before the fix — Photos' state line at `top=247` against `top=127` — and after a full
sweep the frame now reads `.app-window { scrollTop: 0, overflow: clip }` with `.page-head` at `0`,
where before it was found at `199.5` and `−199`.

**What is not established is the split.** The window is also **841px** tall now rather than 865 —
the previous sitting's window-fit work (defect 87) — so 24 of the difference is a smaller viewport
and the rest is the scrolling instrument. Separating the two would need the old probe run against
the old window, and neither exists any more. Both causes are named; the arithmetic between them is
not claimed.

**0 stranded is the number that carries across both runs**, and it is the one the file exists to
report.

## Phase 7 · Slice 33 — the design pass: Messages · 2026-09-05

Messages was not in the previous sitting's brief and was never touched by it. It was the pane
furthest from the canvas: one column that swapped a thread list for a thread, on hand-written hex
colours predating the token file, with the contacts **directory** occupying the third column where
the design puts the open conversation's own person.

### Defect 93 — the preview has been on the wire since Phase 4 and had never once been drawn

The thread list showed sender ids and dates and no preview text. The first question was whether the
wire carries one, because the two answers are different work: `sms.threads` sends **`snippet`**, and
this pane had always rendered it.

Measured in the running app, before anything was changed:

```
.sms-thread   50 rows,  height 32px,  display: flex, flex-direction: column
.sms-snippet  50 elements, 50 with real text, 50 at height 0
              "(no preview)" count: 0        ← every one had something to say
```

**Fifty sentences, present, correct, and invisible.**

#### The mechanism, and the first answer was wrong

Varying the row's own properties in the live page looked decisive:

| tried | row | preview |
|---|---|---|
| as shipped | 32px | **0** |
| `min-height: 0` on the row | 18px | **0** |
| `height: auto` on the row | 32px | **0** |
| `flex-shrink: 0` on the preview | 32px | 18px, overflowing |
| `display: block` on the row | 32px | 18px |

The row never grew, so the conclusion written down was *a `<button>` does not grow to its flex
content*. **That was wrong**, and it was caught by insisting the new guard go red first: the fix was
reintroduced to prove the probe could see it, and **the row grew to 119px with its text intact**.

Rebuilt off-screen from the shipped rule, varying the **parent**:

| parent of the rows | row | preview |
|---|---|---|
| **as shipped** — `display: flex; flex-direction: column; max-height: 300px` | 32px | **0** |
| the same, but `display: block` | 52px | 18px |
| flex column, **no** `max-height` | 52px | 18px |

**A column flex container with a constrained height shrinks its children**, because a flex item
defaults to `flex-shrink: 1` — and inside each shrunken row the deficit came out of the text. Both
conditions are needed; neither alone does anything, and the row's own `display: flex` was
incidental, which is exactly why changing it appeared to help.

The lesson generalises past this pane: **the properties you can vary are not necessarily the ones
responsible.** Varying the row changed the symptom, so the row looked like the cause. Only rebuilding
the whole structure separated them — and nothing would have forced that step except a guard that had
to be shown failing.

#### Why nothing in the repo caught it, and where the guard went

- A **DOM double has no layout**. `smsView.test.ts` rendered the element, asserted its text, and
  passed — for months, over a line no user had ever read.
- A **stylesheet parser has no tags and no tree**. `display: flex` with no height is correct on a
  `div`; the fault needed a *parent*, a *child* and a *constraint* together.
- A **screenshot comparison** shows a missing line as a design difference, which is how this
  survived a design pass three days earlier.

`scripts/zero-height-text-probe.mjs` sweeps every pane for elements that carry text and draw at zero
height. It is deliberately aimed at the **symptom** rather than the mechanism — given how wrong the
first reading of the mechanism was, a net cast at "a sentence with no box" is worth more than one
shaped around a cause. It excludes what is *meant* to have no box: `display: none` subtrees, `hidden`
nodes, and the `visually-hidden` convention.

**Its control is built in, not a sibling file.** `--self-test` plants a `height: 0` text node in a
live pane, runs the sweep, asserts it was reported, and removes it. A `*.test.mjs` beside it would
need the running app and so could never run in the suite — and this repo has already shipped a file
that named an instrument which did not exist.

```
13 of 13 panes measured, 0 text nodes drawn at zero height.
self-test: the planted node was reported (1 found), and it has been removed.
```

### The rebuild, measured against the canvas

| | design | build |
|---|---|---|
| grid | `280px 1fr 300px`, gap 16 | `280 / 539 / 300`, gap 16 |
| thread row | 60px, radius 12 | 60px, radius 12, `display: grid` |
| row avatar | 34px | 34px |
| person avatar | 72px | 72px |
| filter pill | 26px, radius 999 | 26px, radius 999 |
| previews with text / at zero height | — | **50 / 0** |
| composer in the viewport | — | yes, bottom at 758 of 841 |

**The grid does not take the design's literal `height: 600px`.** The canvas is a 920px window with
about 200px of chrome above the grid; this app's window is **841px** after defect 87's fit, and the
page head plus the device strip take about 300 — so a literal 600 put the composer, the one control
on the screen, below the fold. The pane opts into the viewport-bounded screen the way Files does and
the grid is `height: 100%` of it.

**Single-word senders get two initials.** Most of this phone's list is machine sender ids —
`AD-SUJAMK-P`, `VM-TNSBIC-P`, `CP-INUTRA-P` — which are one word by any rule a computer can apply,
so first-letter-per-word drew a column of discs reading `A`, `V`, `C`. And `threadInitials` had to
learn that *Unknown number* is a placeholder rather than a name: taking initials from `threadWho`'s
own fallback gave an unidentified sender a confident `UN` disc, a placeholder promoted to a name one
function later. `#` now, which is the Calls pane's convention for the same situation.

### The two diagnostic strings, and why both are the same fault

Removed:

> *"50 conversations, 2 showing a contact name, 586 unread. Older conversations are not shown yet."*
>
> *"50 contacts, and more the phone did not send — narrow the search. Sorted by name, which is the
> only order a book can be read in."*

Every clause of both is a fact about **our implementation**: how many rows one page happens to hold,
how well contact resolution is working, that a pager exists, and what the sort order is. They were
written to satisfy hardware steps and they stayed on a screen a user reads.

**The denominator rule in `CLAUDE.md` is about logs and evidence**, where a count with no scale is
not evidence. It was never a licence to put the instrument's readout on screen, and the second
string does not even have that excuse — *"the only order a book can be read in"* is a justification
addressed to a reviewer.

What replaces them is nothing, in the state they occupied. A loaded list explains itself by being a
list, and the unread counts are already on the rows that have them. **The three states that survive
are the ones about the user's phone rather than about us**: still reading it, nothing on it, and a
filter that matched none of it — and each is a sentence that already existed.

**One of those three had never been reachable.** `setAdvertised` started the fetch and only rendered
when it returned, so *"Reading the phone's conversations…"* went from blank straight to a list and
was never once on screen. Found by a test asserting the state and getting an empty string; the pane
draws before it awaits now.

### Where Contacts belongs

The question was asked and it has a definite answer:

- **There is no `contacts` screen** in `navModel`. The directory existed only as the third column of
  Messages.
- **The design's sidebar has no Contacts row** — eleven rows, none of them contacts.
- **The design's Messages third column is the open conversation's person**: avatar, name, number,
  actions.
- **A directory already has a built home**: the Calls pane's Contacts tab, over the same
  `contacts.list`, where picking someone fills the dialler.

So the third column is the person now, and the directory moved into the **New conversation** panel,
which is where searching a person by name is what you are actually doing. Nothing is lost: the
capability moved to where the verb is.

The palette's `deep.contacts` row was pointed at `messages` / `contacts-card`. A palette row cannot
usefully reveal something that is only on screen while composing, so it points at **Calls** now.

**And the two views nearly ended up fighting over one element.** `ContactsView` toggles a `hidden`
*class* on its card for the unadvertised state while `SmsView` sets the `hidden` *attribute* on the
panel for the composing state — the same element, two mechanisms, and an unadvertised `contacts`
capability would have kept the New conversation panel shut for reasons nobody could see. They have
separate elements: `#contacts-card` is the panel, `#contacts-people` is the directory.

### What the design draws and this wire cannot serve

| Design draws | Verb it would need | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **SMS** and **Chat** filter tabs | a kind per *thread*; `kind` exists only per **message**, and *Chat* means RCS, which this app does not implement | **refused** — the strip is `All` / `Unread`, and `unread` is on every thread row |
| **Encrypted** badge in the chat header | — | stays cut: the link is encrypted, an SMS is not |
| attachment **card** with a file name and size | `hasAttachments` is a boolean and there is no MMS-parts verb | a marker, not a card — the name and size would both be invented |
| **Video call** | none | removed |
| **Block contact** | none, and `BlockedNumberContract` is restricted to the default dialer or SMS app | removed |
| **Shared media** | none | removed |
| **Mute notifications** | none — the phone does not tell the Mac what is muted | removed |
| **phone call** button | `call.dial` — **exists** | not drawn here: it lives on the Calls pane, and a second entry point that silently changes screens is worse than the one that says where it goes |

One line replaces the four removed controls, and it is **new copy, flagged unratified**: *"Calling
is on the Calls screen. Video, blocking and shared media are on the phone — nothing on the wire
carries them."* That is the **third** sentence of this shape in the app, after Calls' and Photos'.
Three uses is either a house style or a rut, and it is the designer's call rather than mine; it goes
on the vocabulary list with the others.

**Evidence:** `docs/evidence/phase-7-design-2026-09-05/messages-build.png`, `messages-design.png`,
`messages-compare.png`. Mac suite **555 → 565**.

## Phase 7 · Slice 34 — contact photographs on the Calls pane · 2026-09-05

The avatar disc has been a placeholder for a picture the phone already held. This puts the picture
in it, and the way the wire is already shaped meant **no contract change**: `docs/protocol.md` keeps
binary out of the control messages with `contacts.get` named as one of two bounded exceptions —
one contact, on demand, a base64 PNG capped at 64 KiB and downscaled by the phone rather than
refused. That verb has been implemented on both sides since Phase 4 and the Contacts pane already
used it. Calls simply never asked.

### The measurement, taken first

Two `adb` reads against `content://com.android.contacts`, both with a control, before any code was
written. The question is what a photograph *is* on this handset, because "the contact has a photo"
is two different columns with a 42× size difference between them.

| | contacts | share of the book | source size |
|---|---|---|---|
| rows total | **665** | — | — |
| `photo_id` not null — a **thumbnail**, in the provider's own database | **224** | 34% | 96 px |
| `photo_file_id` not null — a **display photo**, the full-size file | **17** | 2.6% | 720 px |
| no picture of any kind | **441** | 66% | — |

`content://com.android.contacts/photo_dimensions` reports `display_max_dim=720,
thumbnail_max_dim=96`, which is where the two sizes come from rather than from documentation.

**Controls, both directions.** The presence control is the matched rows and not the count — five
`photo_id=` rows printed verbatim, and five `photo_file_id=` rows printed to show that a count of 17
is not a count of zero misread. The absence control is the query itself: the same command with the
same projection returns 665 rows, so a zero in either column would have been a fact about the
column rather than about the query.

**One reading in that run is worth keeping on its own.** `grep -c '^Row: '` returns **664** and
`grep -o 'photo_id=' | wc -l` returns **665**. One contact's `display_name` contains a newline, so
the row-per-line assumption is false on this phone's real book. The larger number is the honest one,
and this is the `grep -c` failure from the control table in `CLAUDE.md` arriving one more time: the
count was of *lines*, and the thing being counted was *rows*.

### What was built

`ContactPhotos` (`desktop/src/shared/contactPhotos.ts`) — one store for the pane, keyed on number,
holding an image source or `null`. Consequences worth stating:

- **A miss is cached exactly as hard as a hit.** Two thirds of this book has no picture, so *there
  isn't one* is the ordinary answer, and a store that only remembered successes would re-ask the
  common case on every redraw.
- **A second caller joins the run in flight.** The live card and a log row are routinely the same
  person drawn in the same frame from two code paths — the race `CLAUDE.md` records from the Files
  pane, where two correct triggers assembled the one state the type was built to prevent.
- **A failure is counted and *not* cached.** A photograph that failed because the link dropped is a
  question that was never answered; caching it would mean the face never returns on a link that has.
- **It is dropped on disconnect**, for the same reason the main process drops its name cache.

`photoWorthAsking` decides whether to spend a request at all, and the middle row is an inference
rather than a fact, so it is written down: `call.log` carries **no photo field**, only whether the
phone resolved a `contactName`. A name and a photograph come from the *same* `PhoneLookup` match on
the *same* number, so a row the phone could not name has no contact behind it and cannot have a
picture. What that costs is one case — a contact with a photograph and no display name — and
`ContactsStore.list` already refuses to list those rows (`DISPLAY_NAME_PRIMARY IS NOT NULL`), so it
is a face this app has never been able to show anywhere.

The photograph is painted **over** a disc that is already correct: `background-image` plus
`color: transparent`, initials and hue intact underneath. There is no loading state, because the
thing a spinner would cover is the right answer already, and every refusal — no photo, no contact,
contacts not granted, link gone, an image that will not decode — degrades to the disc this pane has
always drawn.

### On hardware

`scripts/call-photos-probe.mjs`, through `probe.mjs` because these numbers are written down here.

```
route to calls → landed  [waited=11ms stopped=settled]
how many call-log rows are drawn → 50  [control=3 polls=1 stopped=settled]
call-log discs carrying a photograph → {"discs":53,"withPhoto":22,"paintedKeepingInitials":22,
                                        "sample":["SC → url(\"data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0…"]}
                                        [control=53 stopped=settled]
  PASS  at least one photograph is drawn — 22 of 53 discs
  PASS  every painted disc still carries its initials underneath — 22 of 22
  what the photo store says it did → "6 found / 11 none / 0 failed, 9 not asked,
                                      cache 52 hit / 50 missed, 17 held"
switch to Missed and back to All, which redraws every disc → landed
  the tally after a full redraw → "6 found / 11 none / 0 failed, 15 not asked, cache 104 hit …"
  PASS  a redraw fetched nothing new — found 6 → 6
```

**Two instruments on one fact, deliberately.** The DOM says 22 discs carry a photograph. The store
says 6 were found across 17 distinct numbers. Those disagree and both are right: 50 log rows are 17
distinct numbers, and one contact appears on many rows — so *photographs fetched* and *discs
painted* are counts of different things, which is the units rule from `CLAUDE.md` met head-on. The
number that would have been wrong is any ratio between them.

The pair is also what separates the two stories a picture cannot: a pane drawing six faces because
six contacts have pictures, and one drawing six because the fetch died after six, look identical.
`0 failed` is the discriminator, and `cache 52 hit / found 6 → 6` across a full redraw is the
evidence that the cache is the feature rather than an optimisation.

The live card was measured separately, because a ring cannot be scheduled: a **synthetic** call was
driven onto it from a real log row that has a photograph, giving `104x104`, `hasPhoto: true`,
`initialsUnderneath: "SC"`. It is synthetic and is labelled so; the pane was put back on the phone's
real state with `calls.refresh()` afterwards, verified by the idle card returning.

**Evidence:** `docs/evidence/phase-7-call-photos-2026-09-05/calls-with-photos.png` (the real log)
and `live-card-synthetic.png` (the driven card, and the only synthetic image in this slice).

### Defect 94 — a shared script with an `export` had never run, and worked anyway

The feature did not draw at all on its first run: `ContactPhotos` was `undefined` in the page while
`photoKey`, declared four lines from it in the same file, was a `function`.

`src/shared/*.ts` files are loaded two ways — `require`d by tests, and dropped into `index.html` as
classic `<script>` tags. A file carrying an `export` is a **module**, and tsc compiles a module to
CommonJS whose first emitted statement is `Object.defineProperty(exports, …)`. There is no `exports`
in a classic script, so the file throws on its first line and **every declaration below it is dead**
— including the `globalThis` block at the bottom that each of these files carries and that each
file's own comment credits for making it work.

**The part that makes this worth a defect number rather than a fix: `discHue.ts` had been in that
state for a phase, and the app was fine.** A `function` declaration is hoisted onto `globalThis`
before the body executes, so it survives the throw. A `class` is not. So the same mistake is
invisible for a file of functions and fatal for one with a class, and nothing in this repo could
report either:

| | |
|---|---|
| `tsc` | clean — it is valid TypeScript |
| `npm test` | green — tests `require` the file, where `exports` exists |
| the page | **works**, when the file exports only functions |

Eight of the ten renderer-loaded shared files already avoid `export`; nobody had written down why,
so the ninth did not. Fixed in both files, and the comment in `discHue.ts` that credited the wrong
mechanism now records what was actually happening.

**Enforcement**, because a rule this repo has now paid for twice is not a rule anyone remembers:
`scripts/check-renderer-scripts.mjs`, wired to `PreToolUse` on `git commit` as the **eighth** hook.
Scope comes from `index.html` rather than from the directory — `src/shared/` also holds modules the
main process imports normally, and those keep their exports. The matcher is anchored on a
*declaration*, so prose about the rule stays legal; that is defect 41's lesson and there are
fixtures in both directions, including the verbatim `export function discHue` that shipped. Its
control fails loudly on an empty scan, and a second test reads the **built** `dist/shared/*.js` for
a top-level `exports` reference, which is the backstop if the source matcher is ever wrong in the
permissive direction. Shown to deny with the defect reintroduced, and to fall silent with it
restored.

### Two instrument faults from this sitting, both caught before anything was written down

- **`probe.mjs`'s own `format()` printed `NOT REPORTABLE` over a stimulus that landed perfectly.**
  An `act` result carries `what`/`landed`; `format` reads `question`/`value`/`reportable`, so it
  printed `undefined → undefined … NOT REPORTABLE — the instrument gave up` twice in one run, beside
  readings that were correct. That is the instrument reporting a failure of its own that did not
  happen — the same family `probe.mjs` exists to stop, inside `probe.mjs`. `format` now refuses an
  act result outright and `formatAct` is its counterpart, with the fixture being the sentence that
  actually got printed.
- **A parallel-test race that a ninth test file exposed.** `check-debt-claims.test.mjs` patched
  `scripts/check-protocol-spec.mjs` **on disk** for the length of a run and restored it in a
  `finally`. `node --test` runs files in parallel, so `check-protocol-spec.test.mjs` read the patched
  copy and failed with an accurate message about a file that existed for forty milliseconds. It had
  been latent since the guard was written; adding an unrelated ninth file changed the scheduling and
  surfaced it, which is how a latent race always surfaces. The fixtures write a **copy** now and
  point the subprocess at it with `DEBT_SOURCE`; nothing shared is mutated. Verified by ten
  consecutive parallel runs at `fail 0`, and by a checksum of the real file before and after a run.

**Tests:** Mac **565 → 580** (nine for the store, six for the pane's drawing). Six mutations of the
store and six of the pane were each shown to go red on exactly the test named for them, with the
restored source green. Phone: `sync-module` compiles and its suite passes; two log lines were added
and no behaviour changed.

## Phase 7 · Slice 35 — naming a call the phone network is not hosting · 2026-09-05

### What was reachable, and what was not

Asked before building, because the brief asked for `"WhatsApp video call"` and only part of that
sentence is supportable. Each row says what backs it.

| | Reachable? | What backs it, or what does not |
|---|---|---|
| **The call exists at all** | **yes, already** | `CallWatcher` sees it: a 68-minute WhatsApp video call produced a full episode with correct timing (`docs/defects.md` → 47). This was never the missing half |
| **The caller's name** | **yes** | the app's own `notif.posted` `title`. It is WhatsApp's name for the person, from WhatsApp's address book — not ours, and not a number |
| **Which app** | **yes** | `package` plus `appName`, already resolved through `AppLabels.of` on the phone |
| **Audio or video** | **no** | `Notification.category` is `"call"` for both. The distinction lives in the app's own prose (*"Incoming video call"*), which is another app's copy in the user's locale and can change in any update; or in `CallStyle`'s `EXTRA_CALL_IS_VIDEO`, which is structured and which this phone does not put on the wire. **So the card says *"WhatsApp call"*, never *"WhatsApp video call"*** |
| **Ringing → answered** | **yes, already** | the telephony state transition, not the notification. `CallWatcher` reports it and always has |
| **The end of the call** | **yes, already** | `call.ended`, with a duration that agreed with telecom's own analytics to within the ringing period |
| **Answering / rejecting from the Mac** | **unmeasured** | `call.answer` is `TelecomManager.acceptRingingCall()` and `call.reject` is `endCall()`. Whether either reaches a self-managed call is a device question. **Not guessed into the UI in either direction** |

So four of the seven were already built, two are new, and one is a measurement nobody has taken.

### What the notification alone can honestly claim

A notification says *an app believes a call exists, and here is who it says it is with*. It does not
carry the platform's call state — but this app does not need it to, because `CallWatcher` already
has the real thing. The notification supplies **identity only**, and that is exactly the half that
was missing.

### The discriminator, and the reason it is not "there is a call notification"

The phone's own dialer posts a `category: "call"` notification for a cellular call too, so presence
does not separate them; the **package** does. `TELEPHONY_PACKAGES` in `src/shared/appCall.ts` is an
exclusion set, it is a list from one handset, and that is stated in the file rather than assumed
away — a dialer package not on it would have its call named after the dialer.

Which is why the rule **only ever adds a name**. It does not remove a control, gate an action or
change what any button does. The worst case for a wrong answer is a wrong label on a card whose
buttons behave exactly as before; the other direction would take Reject away from a real ringing
call, and this repo has already hung up one of those.

Two further guards, both asserted: the episode must have **no number** (a call with a number came
from the phone network whatever is on screen), and the notification must be **ongoing** (a
`category: "call"` notification that is dismissible is a *missed-call* summary, and naming a live
card from one would put an hour-old caller on screen).

### Control: the field is real on this device

Before relying on `category`, the live list was read through `probe.mjs`: **7 notifications,
categories `msg` 1 / `service` 1 / `status` 1 / none 4, ongoing 3**. So `category` is populated and
`ongoing` discriminates. There was no `call`-category row, which is correct with no call in
progress — and it is why the rule itself is still **unverified against a live WhatsApp call**. That
stimulus is one incoming WhatsApp call and it needs the user's phone.

### On the running app

Driven synthetically — there is no WhatsApp call happening — through the real pane and the real
render path, with the pane restored afterwards:

```
what the card says for an app-hosted call → {
  "who":"Sahil Chaudhary", "status":"Ringing · WhatsApp",
  "buttons":["Answer on phone","Reject"],
  "strips":["Audio stays on the phone — pair the Mac to it over Blu",
            "WhatsApp is hosting this call, not the phone network. "],
  "hostedFor":"com.whatsapp" }                       [control=2 stopped=immediate]
```

The `buttons` line is asserted in the test suite as well as read here: **naming a call must not
add, remove or relabel a control.**

**Evidence:** `docs/evidence/phase-7-app-call-2026-09-05/app-call-card-synthetic.png`, which is
synthetic and named so.

### Defect 95 — `__probe.onScreen` measured against the viewport, not against the scroller

Found by disbelieving it. The app-call note looked clipped in a screenshot; `onScreen` said
`visible`, `fraction: 1`. Per this repo's own rule a measurement beats an impression, so the
disagreement was taken to a third query — every clipping ancestor of the element:

```
noteBottom: 826,  viewportH: 841        → inside the viewport, which is what onScreen measured
#page  overflowY: auto  bottom: 795     → clipsNote: true
```

`#page` is the scroll port and its bottom sits ~46px above the viewport because the dock is under
it. `seen()` intersected the element's rect with `window.innerHeight` alone, so **anything ending in
that 46px band read as fully visible while its lower part was not drawn.** 31px of the sentence was
missing and the instrument reported the card as whole.

This is defect 85's own instrument carrying defect 85's bug, and it is the third time in this repo
an instrument has been wrong about the thing it was built for. `seen()` now intersects with every
ancestor whose overflow is not `visible`, and reports `clipTop` / `clipBottom` so the reader can see
what did the clipping. Three fixtures: the failure with its real numbers (841 / 826 / 795 → `0.68`,
`reachable`), a control with a port that contains the element (`1`, `visible`), and a control
proving an ancestor with `overflow: visible` does not clip however small its box. Shown red against
the viewport-only expression and green with it restored.

**Two published numbers are superseded and are corrected here rather than left standing.** Slice 29
recorded *23 blocks: 21 visible at rest, 2 reachable* and Slice 30 *23 cards, 20 visible at rest, 3
reachable, 0 stranded*. Both splits were computed from the viewport-only fraction, so **`visible`
was over-reported**, and — because the same fraction decides the second split — `stranded` could
have been under-reported too. The card totals are unaffected. Today's run with the corrected
instrument, on today's pane contents: **21 cards, 12 visible at rest, 9 reachable, 0 stranded.**
That is not the same population as either earlier run and is not a before/after comparison; it is
the first honest reading.

### The note is two strips, not three, and that is the measurement talking

The first build appended the hosted note as a **third** strip. Measured: `top: 728, bottom: 826`
against `#page` ending at 795 — `fraction: 0.69`, `reachable`. A card carrying a *state* has to be
visible at rest and not merely reachable, and nobody scrolls a card while a phone is ringing. So for
an app call the note **replaces** the mute/speaker strip and carries what that sentence said, which
is asserted in the test rather than trusted. After: `top: 642, bottom: 722, fraction: 1, visible`.

**Tests:** Mac **580 → 601**. Seven mutations of the naming rule and six of the pane were each shown
red on exactly the test named for them. Two of those pane tests **passed for the wrong reason first**
and were rewritten: one asserted a fetch that a second code path also performed, the other checked
for a strip after a call that had been nulled anyway, so the idle card satisfied it whatever the
field held. Both now go red.

The DOM double grew `[attr]` presence matching, which it asks for explicitly rather than being
worked around: presence only, never `[attr="value"]`, because a selector that matches the value is
asserting it twice and fails by matching nothing.
