## Phase 7 Slice 36 — the status island, rebuilt as current state (2026-09-08)

Reported by the user: *"It says random things while the phone is connected, and sometimes shows
errors that are not happening. I see it on almost every screen, with Connected and a live latency
drawn two inches away."* The rule they gave, which is what was built: **the island shows current
state and nothing else; a recorded event is history and history is what Activity is for.**

### The diagnosis, read from the source rather than recalled

The island had **five writers and two clocks**. Four of the five were ordinary. The fifth was
`startIsland`, a `setInterval(…, 5200)` that cycled a six-slot ring of strings, and one statement in
it is the whole defect:

```ts
this.setIsland(this.events[this.eventIndex]!, toneOf(this.status));   // shell.ts:491
```

**Text from history, tone from the live link.** A stale sentence painted in the live colour is a
claim that the sentence is current.

Three questions were asked of it and each has a file-and-line answer:

| | |
|---|---|
| **What replaces a line?** | the 5.2 s timer, unconditionally, and nothing else. Eviction from the ring was by count (6), FIFO, deduped only against the immediately preceding string |
| **How old can a line be?** | **unbounded.** `ActivityEvent` carries `at: Date.now()` (`main/activity.ts:112`) and `islandLineFor` took `{ category, kind, detail }` — **the timestamp was dropped at the boundary** and `note()` stored a bare `string`. The ring was never cleared: not on disconnect, not on reconnect, not on a pairing change. The oldest line survived the session and came round every ~31 s |
| **Which lines contradict the strip?** | a `lastError` or a phone refusal, cycling in **green** after recovery; `Connected · N ms` — pushed as a *history* entry at `shell.ts:762` — cycling in **amber** during a reconnect; any feature line (`Sent to phone · 57 bytes`) cycling in **red** during an outage, asserting a send that is not happening |

**Why the strip was not the authority: nothing ever made it one.** `setStatus`'s own comment claims
*"one function so the four cannot disagree"*, and the island is not one of the four. It got a seize
on transitions and was then handed to a timer that had never heard of `status`.

### The fourth contradiction, upstream of the island

`link.ts` held **two** failure fields, `lastError` (raw) and `lastFailure` (classified), and
`status()` returned `lastFailure?.message ?? lastError`. A successful handshake cleared the raw one
and **not the classified one** — assigned in four places, cleared in none — so after a single
failure **every** subsequent status carried that sentence forever, `phase: 'connected'` included.
The island was narrating a genuinely stale field.

Same field, sharper consequence: `status()` feeds `lastFailure` to `pairingHealth`, so one
certificate refusal left `pairing` at `repudiated` **through a successful re-pair**, and the shell's
`mustPair` then pins the user to the pairing screen while connected.

**The fix is one field, not the missing line.** Adding `this.lastFailure = null` would have fixed
the instance; two fields that must be cleared together, in a class with six assignment sites, is the
defect. `LinkFailure` already carries `raw` beside `message` and `kind`, so there is now one field
and exactly two things that write it — `failed(raw)` and `succeeded()`. Three of the six sites had
been setting only the raw field, producing a status whose `lastError` was an unclassified fragment
(`no pong in 15s`) with no kind beside it; they are classified like everything else now.

### The rule, and what the island says in each state

One pure function in `src/shared/islandState.ts`, one writer in `shell.ts` (`renderIsland`), no
ring, no timer, **no timestamp anywhere in the file** — the fix expressed as a type, since a
function with no clock cannot show a stale line.

| Live state | Island | Tone |
|---|---|---|
| no status yet | `Starting…` | idle |
| unpaired | `Not paired` | idle |
| repudiated | `Pairing was removed on the phone` | down |
| searching | `Looking for phone` | working |
| connecting / handshaking | `Connecting` | working |
| reconnecting | `Reconnecting`, or `Reconnecting · no answer on any known address` | working |
| failed | `Disconnected · the phone closed the connection` | down |
| connected, idle | `Connected · 12 ms`, or `Connected` before the first heartbeat | live |
| transfer in flight | `Copying clip_final.mp4` / `Sending report.pdf` / `Transferring 3 files` | live |
| clipboard sync | **nothing** — see below | live |

**A clipboard sync gets no island line, and that is the rule rather than an omission.** `clip-send`
is a request and its reply; `clip-arrived` is an instant. Neither has a duration, so under the
user's own rule both are history the moment they exist. They are recorded in Activity, which
timestamps and filters them, and acknowledged by the toast, which is what a moment gets. A transfer
is the one thing on this Mac that is genuinely *in flight*, and it is the only work the island shows.

### Why the reason is a `kind` and never the classified sentence

`ConnectionStatus` gained `lastFailureKind`. The island reads it and never `lastError`, because
`classifyLinkError`'s prose for a dropped socket is **"The connection to your phone dropped.
Reconnecting."** — a sentence that *names a connection state*. In a pill beside a strip reading
`Disconnected`, that is the island contradicting the strip while carrying a perfectly current fact.

This is the difference between a rule and a filter, and it was demonstrated rather than argued.
Mutating `islandState` to render the message instead of the kind produces:

```
AssertionError: “Disconnected · The connection to your phone dropped. Reconnecting.”
  names a connection state other than “Disconnected”
```

A filter testing the prose for connection words would pass until somebody wrote a new sentence. A
closed enum of five cannot express the wrong thing.

### The tests, and the second assertion a mutation forced

Two files, because a pure test alone is defect 67's shape — a correct decision and an untested
write, which is exactly what `islandRota.ts` was: nine tests, all correct, over a pill that
contradicted the strip daily.

- **`src/shared/islandState.test.ts`** — the decision, over a **cross-product** of 9 phases × 4
  pairing kinds × 2 `paired` × 4 latencies × 8 failure kinds = **2,304 states**, including a phase
  and a failure kind *"added after this test was written"*. The set of connection labels is
  **derived** from `linkToneLabel` and `pairingLabel` rather than typed, so a label added tomorrow
  joins the invariant automatically. Control: the product reaches all four tones.
- **`src/renderer/shellIsland.test.ts`** — the **write**, driving the real `ShellView` against the
  DOM double through an eleven-step session (connect, heartbeat, transfer, drop mid-transfer,
  nothing answers, recover, repudiate, re-pair, unpair), asserting after every step **and after
  firing every timer the shell has scheduled**.

**The second assertion exists because the first mutation caught the test being too weak, not the
code being wrong.** Reinstating the rota with a ring holding `Sent to phone · 57 bytes,
automatically` **passed** the contradiction check: it names no connection state, and the old code
always painted the dot from the live link, which was the one thing it got right. Yet the pill was
asserting a send over a socket that was gone.

So the check is not *does the text avoid the wrong words* but **is the text the one the current
state produces** — `assert.equal(islandText, islandState(status, work).text)`, calling the
production rule rather than restating it. Any second writer fails it on its first tick, whatever it
says.

Red-first, three mutations, each on the tests named for it:

| Mutation | What went red |
|---|---|
| reinstate the 5.2 s rota | `the island never contradicts the strip…` — *“TIMEOUT: the phone stopped answering” where the live state produces “Looking for phone” — something other than the state wrote the pill*; and `the island holds no timer of its own` — *the shell scheduled 1 interval(s): 5200ms* |
| render `lastError` instead of `lastFailureKind` | 5 of 13 in `islandState.test.ts`, including the `Reconnecting.` sentence quoted above |
| draw a failure while the tone is `live` | `a stale failure left on a connected status is not drawn`, in both files |

`ShellView` came **off** `scripts/check-renderer-views.mjs`'s debt list — 11 covered / 2 outstanding
→ **12 / 1**. Its debt reason was *"the window frame; its rules live in shell.css"*, which was true
of the frame and false of this file's other job: it owns the island **and** the strip, two surfaces
that must agree about one fact, and no test could see either being written. The DOM double grew
`getElementById` (auto-vivifying, with the cost of that stated), `removeAttribute`, a small
`document.querySelector`, and recorded window listeners.

Suite: **616 pass, 0 fail** (from 598).

### On hardware, 2026-09-08 — SM-S938B, `scripts/target-device.sh` not needed (no device writes)

Read through `scripts/probe.mjs`. The strip is `display: none` on `overview` and `pairing`
(`shell.css:664`), so **the first run was refused** with `PROBE_NOT_VISIBLE: #strip-state-label
(hidden=false, height=0)` rather than reporting what an unlaid-out element says about itself — the
refusal working. Routed to Notifications by pressing the nav row by name, route confirmed landed
before anything was read.

| Reading | Value |
|---|---|
| island / strip, same instant | `Connected · 7 ms` · `Samsung SM-S938B` `Connected` `7 ms` |
| tones | `live` / `live` — agree |
| island's text begins with the strip's state | **true** |
| 15 samples over 30 s | **5 distinct readings, all `Connected · N ms`** with the card reading `Connected` in every one. The only thing that varied was the measured latency |
| transfer in flight | `{"island":"Copying inbox-probe.bin","tone":"live","strip":"Connected","stripTone":"live"}` — the work line landed **2 ms** after the click |
| after the copy | settled back to `Connected · 6 ms` |

The instrument's bound is stated: a small copy can finish inside one poll interval, so the sighting
was taken with `probe.act`'s `expect` (100 ms poll, explicit deadline, `landed` reported either
way). A `landed: false` would have been *not seen in this run*, never *does not work*.

Screenshot: `docs/evidence/island-2026-09-08/island-and-strip.png`, clipped to the two elements'
real bounding boxes read from the page rather than to coordinates guessed off an image.

### Defect 96 — the status island had no clock, and drew history in the live tone

Recorded above. Fixed and proven on hardware 2026-09-08.

### Defect 97 — `lastFailure` was assigned in four places and cleared in none

Recorded above. Fixed 2026-09-08; the stale-error half is proven on hardware by 30 s of samples
carrying no failure text, and the **repudiation** half is *unproven* — reproducing it needs a
certificate refusal followed by a successful re-pair, which needs the phone's Mac tab tapped
twice. The stimulus is named rather than the fix claimed: `Forget` on the phone, re-scan, then read
`pairing.kind` on a connected status.

### Slice 36, second sitting — the states the first window could not reach

The first 30-second sample had a healthy link throughout, so every non-`live` state was carried by
2,304 cross-product cases and the DOM session test and **not** by a sighting. That was recorded as a
named gap with its stimulus. The phone then went away on its own — `ECONNREFUSED` on the last-known
address, the phone's app not listening — which supplied the stimulus for free.

**It found a defect neither test layer could see.** The pill read:

```
Connecting · no answer on any known address
```

Both halves true. The reason describes the **last completed** attempt and the label describes the
one **in flight**, and joining them in one sentence presents two moments as one — it is dialling
something while saying nothing answered. It contradicts nothing: the strip said `Connecting` too, so
the invariant passed, and `assert.equal(text, islandState(status, work).text)` passed because the
island was faithfully rendering what the rule said. **A rule can be self-consistent and wrong**, and
the only instrument that sees that is a person looking at the screen. Same way defect 67 was found.

Fixed by `DIALLING = {searching, connecting, handshaking}`: a reason accompanies a **settled** state
— `Disconnected · …`, and `Reconnecting · …`, which by construction means *the last attempt failed
and I am waiting to try again* — and is withheld while a socket attempt is actually open. The pill
alternates as the discovery order sweeps candidates, and both readings are true when drawn.

Red-first: emptying `DIALLING` fails with *`searching` drew a reason for the previous attempt:
"Looking for phone · no answer on any known address"*. The test carries the control that makes it
mean something — the same failure in `reconnecting` and `disconnected` **does** render its reason,
so it is not passing because the reason never draws.

**On hardware, on the fixed build — 330 samples at 120 ms through a real outage:**

| | Reading |
|---|---|
| 283× | `Reconnecting · no answer on any known address` [working] · card `Reconnecting` [working] |
| 47× | `Connecting` [working] · card `Connecting` [working] |
| **0** | readings where the island disagreed with the card |

Two distinct readings, both led by the card's own state, tones agreeing in every sample. Screenshot:
`docs/evidence/island-2026-09-08/island-reconnecting.png`.

**And a second, independent healthy-link sample was recovered**, from a run whose output had been
read as empty: 15 samples over 30 s, `{"island":"Connected · 6 ms","card":"Connected"}`, three
distinct readings, all `Connected · N ms`, tones agreeing throughout. So the healthy-link claim
rests on **30 samples across two runs** taken hours apart, not 15.

That recovery is itself a lookalike worth the line. The output file was read while the process was
still running and came back **0 bytes**, and the conclusion drawn was *the process was killed*. It
had not been: node buffers stdout when it is a pipe rather than a TTY, and flushed the whole thing on
exit. **An empty file is not an empty result when nothing has flushed yet** — the same shape as the
263 ms window, one layer down: a reading that did not exist *yet*, read as one that did not exist. It
cost nothing because the run was repeated, and the repeat is why there are two samples instead of one.

### A safety finding, established before the stimulus rather than after

The plan for reaching the non-`live` states without the user's hands was the product's own
Disconnect button, then Retry to restore. Reading `link.ts` first:

```ts
stop(reason)  { this.running = false; … }
retryNow(why) { if (!this.running || this.isConnected()) return; … }   // ← returns immediately
```

**Retry cannot undo Disconnect.** Only `start()` can, behind `ipcMain.handle('connect')`. A script
that had reached for the obviously-named recovery would have left the user's phone link down and
reported a clean pass — `CLAUDE.md`'s decoration rule exactly: the check that matters is the one that
gates the action, and here the gate was knowing which call actually restores the state.

In the event the induced outage was never needed, and the restore ran in a `finally` regardless. The
link's final state is `running = true` with `Retrying in 30000ms` in the log — recovering on its own
whenever the phone comes back, which is the state it was in before any of this.

### Defect 98 — a reason for the last attempt, drawn beside the label for the next one

Recorded above. Fixed and proven on hardware 2026-09-08, 330 samples.

### Slice 36, third sitting — defect 97 proven through a real failure → recovery cycle

The user reconnected the phone, which closed the last reading that mattered. **The earlier hardware
runs could not test defect 97 at all**: the first had a healthy link for its whole window, so there
was no failure to fail to clear, and the second had a failure that never recovered. What was needed
was one process containing both, and this is it.

**The branch under test actually ran with something to do**, which is the precondition `CLAUDE.md`
requires — a no-op branch is not a pass. In one process (`/tmp/cs-app2.log`):

| | |
|---|---|
| `ECONNREFUSED` failures, 15:33:58 → 15:34:45 | **13**, backing off 1s → 30s |
| successful connects | **2**, first at 15:37:28 (`Paired with Samsung SM-S938B`) |

So `succeeded()` was reached with a real `LinkFailure` set. Four minutes later, read from **the
status object the renderer holds** rather than from the pill:

```json
{ "phase": "connected", "rttMs": 11, "lastError": null, "lastErrorRaw": null,
  "lastFailureKind": null, "pairing": "paired", "deviceName": "Samsung SM-S938B" }
```

| Claim | |
|---|---|
| `lastError` retired after recovery | **true** |
| `lastErrorRaw` retired with it | **true** |
| `lastFailureKind` retired with it | **true** |
| `pairing` recomputed to `paired` | **true** |

Before the fix all four were impossible: `status()` returned `lastFailure?.message ?? lastError`,
`lastFailure` was assigned in four places and cleared in none, and this exact sequence — thirteen
`unreachable` failures then a successful handshake — would have left *"Could not reach your phone.
Check that both are on the same Wi-Fi…"* on **every** connected status for the rest of the session.

**Read from the status object and not from the pill, deliberately.** The island is now structurally
incapable of drawing an error while the tone is `live`, so reading the pill would measure the
island's rule and say nothing about whether the field underneath it was retired — `CLAUDE.md`'s rule
about measuring from the end that can tell the difference. The control is that a status actually
arrived and is the connected one; without it a `null` `lastError` is indistinguishable from *no
status has been delivered yet*.

**The pill, in the same window — 330 samples at 120 ms:**

| | Reading |
|---|---|
| 161× | `Connected · 8 ms` |
| 72× | `Connected · 9 ms` |
| 40× | `Connected · 7 ms` |
| 40× | `Connected · 11 ms` |
| 17× | `Connected · 10 ms` |
| **0** | readings where the island disagreed with the card |

Five distinct readings, one sentence, the only variation being the measured latency — which is what
a surface showing current state is supposed to look like. Island against the strip at the same
instant: `Connected · 8 ms` [live] against `Samsung SM-S938B` `Connected` `8 ms` [live].
Screenshot: `docs/evidence/island-2026-09-08/island-after-recovery.png`.

**Running total across the three sittings: 990 samples, 0 disagreements**, spanning a healthy link,
a real outage with its retry sweep, and the recovery between them.

**Still unproven, and the stimulus unchanged:** defect 97's *repudiation* half and the island's
`Pairing was removed on the phone` state. Both need a **certificate refusal**, which needs `Forget`
on the phone's Mac tab followed by a re-scan. This session's outage was `unreachable`, not
`certificate-refused`, so it exercised neither. (Incidentally the log shows `Paired with Samsung
SM-S938B` at 15:37:28 — the Mac's store had no pairing and paired fresh, so the app also passed
through `Not paired` → `Connected` in this process without incident.)

## Phase 7 Slice 37 — the mirror takes the shape of the stream (2026-09-10)

**Why this slice exists.** Four mirror problems were reported together, in priority order, after a
floating window hung during an investor demo. The diagnosis is `docs/mirror-diagnosis-2026-09-09.md`
and the agreed order is **§3 (fit) → §1 (float start) → §4 (latency anchor) → §2 (float input)**.
This is §3, and it lands the box and the coordinate mapping **together**, because they are one
assumption written in three places rather than two bugs that happen to be adjacent.

### Defect 99 — the stage asserted a 9:19.5 phone, and the tap mapping believed it

The three places, and the third is the one that mattered:

| | Where | What it asserted |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `styles.css` `.pane-mirror .mirror-stage` | `width: 268px; aspect-ratio: 9 / 19.5` |
| 2 | `shared/floatGeometry.ts` | `RATIO = 19.5 / 9` — **still live, see below** |
| 3 | `mirror.ts` `pointAt`'s doc comment | *"there is no letterboxing inside the element to account for"* |

Numbers 1 and 2 draw black bars. Number 3 **moves the user's finger**, and it is the reason this was
not a cosmetic ticket. It was *true when it was written*: the Phase 2 canvas was sized by
`max-width`/`max-height` alone, so the element really was the picture. The design pass then gave the
canvas `object-fit: contain` inside a fixed stage, and the sentence stayed — correct about a layout
that no longer existed. This is `CLAUDE.md`'s *a true sentence about the wrong one of two paths*,
except the second path replaced the first rather than sitting beside it.

**CORRECTED 2026-09-10 — and the correction makes the "one device hid it" story stronger, not
weaker.** This slice first said *the reference device was already wrong (~20:9, 1.6px bars a side,
invisible)*. That was inferred from a **stale canvas backing store** of 480×1070 read off an app
instance that had been running since 2026-09-08, and it is **wrong**. The phone's own log, from a
live session the same day, is authoritative:

```
[mirror] Display 1440x3120 @600dpi -> capture 480x1040 @200dpi (cap 480)
1440 × 3120  →  2.16667   and   19.5 / 9 = 2.16667
```

**The SM-S938B is exactly 19.5:9.** The design's hard-coded box matched the reference handset
*perfectly*, so in portrait there were **no bars at all** on it — which is a cleaner reason for a
phase of invisibility than bars too small to see. Every other phone, and every rotation on every
phone, was wrong.

(Where 480×1070 came from is unresolved: 1070 is what a 480-capped capture of a **1080×2408** panel
gives, which is not this handset's geometry. It was a stale canvas from an unknown earlier session,
and using it to infer a phone's aspect was the error — a decoded frame is evidence about whatever
produced it, and nothing said what that was.)

**Measured before the fix**, in the 266 × 569.4 element the pane actually had:

| stream | picture inside the element | bars | worst-case tap error |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1080×2340 — SM-S938B, **exactly 19.5:9** | 266 × 569.4 | **none** | **none, in portrait** |
| 720×1600 — moto g34 **and** g45 | 256.2 × 569.4 | 4.9px a side | ~20 capture px |
| 1080×2160 — an 18:9 phone | 266 × 532 | 18.7px top and bottom | 71 px |
| 2340×1080 — **any phone turned** | 266 × 122.8 | **223px top and bottom** | **424 px of 1080** |

The last row is the one to keep: the picture was **21% of the box's height**, and to tap the top of
the phone you had to click in the black bar *above* the picture.

**Underneath both, a specificity collision inside one file.** `#mirror-canvas { max-height: 60vh }`
is an id — (1,0,0) — and beat the design pass's `.pane-mirror .mirror-stage canvas` — (0,2,1). So
the canvas was clamped to 569.4px inside a stage the design sized at 580.7px, and **the element was
not even the ratio the stage asserted**. Two selectors sizing one canvas, resolved by specificity
rather than by anyone's intent: the same shape as the three collisions of 2026-08-30 that
`stylesheets.test.ts` was written for — and invisible to it, because that guard compares selectors
*across* the three sheets and both of these live in `styles.css`.

### What changed

- **The stage is the shape of the stream.** `--capture-aspect` (width over height) is set on
  `#mirror-stage` by `mirror.ts` from the geometry the phone **already** announces — `mirror.state`
  at `running` and `mirror.rotate` on every turn both carry `width`, `height`, `dpi`, `rotation`,
  `geometryId`. Nothing new is on the wire. What was missing was any code that used it for layout:
  `this.capture` fed the HUD and the coordinate mapper and nothing else.
- **Landscape makes the box landscape.** Width comes from a height budget through the aspect
  (`min(560px, calc(580px * var(--capture-aspect)))`), so portrait still lands on the design's 268pt
  (580 × 0.4615 = 267.7) and a landscape stream grows wide instead of shrinking to a strip.
- **`pointAt` maps against the picture**, through `captureFit.ts` — `captureAspect`,
  `containedPicture`, `pointInCapture`. It no longer depends on the bars being zero, which is the
  point: the previous version was correct only by a coincidence nobody was checking.
- **The hairline moved from `border` to `box-shadow: inset`.** `aspect-ratio` sizes the *border*
  box; a 1px border makes the content box 2px smaller in each axis, which is a different ratio —
  measured at **1.2px** of residual letterbox in a stage that was otherwise exactly right.
- **Both legacy rules deleted.** The stage owns its size, the canvas fills it, one rule each.

`captureFit.ts` is a file rather than two methods because `docs/design-departures.md` M13 names the
shared input seam as what the float window's pointer input waits on, and this is its first half.

### The readings

**Red-first**, as the rule requires: `pointInCapture` was reverted to dividing by the element — the
defect exactly — and `captureFit.test.ts` went **2 of 6 red**. Restored: 6 of 6 green. Worth
recording *which* two, because it says where the evidence is: the two that fail are the letterbox
mapping and `outsideBy`. The corner-mapping test **stayed green under the mutation**, correctly —
on a box that is already the right ratio the two mappings agree, which is exactly why the old code
survived on one device.

**The box, measured through the real stylesheet in the packaged app** (`ConnectSuite.app`, relaunched,
1440×841 @2x, not zoomed):

| geometry | stage box | stage aspect | stream aspect | bars X | bars Y |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a 1080×2408 panel, portrait | 260.1 × 580 | 0.4485 | 0.4485 | **0** | **0** |
| moto g34 / g45 portrait 720×1600 | 261 × 580 | 0.4500 | 0.4500 | **0** | **0** |
| the same panel, landscape | 560 × 251.2 | 2.2297 | 2.2296 | 0.01 | **0** |
| moto landscape 1600×720 | 560 × 252 | 2.2222 | 2.2222 | **0** | **0** |

`max-height` on the canvas reads `none` — the specificity collision is gone. Control: 13
`section[data-screen]` elements on the page in every row; the probe **refused** one run outright when
the app had not finished loading and the control came back 0, which is that guard doing its job.
Screenshots: `docs/evidence/mirror-fit-2026-09-10/`.

### What this run does NOT reach, stated rather than left to be assumed

**The probe sets `--capture-aspect` by hand.** That is what `mirror.ts` does from the phone's
announced geometry, so this proves the **box rule** and the **mapping**, and it proves nothing about
whether `mirror.ts` writes the property when a real `mirror.state` or `mirror.rotate` arrives. That
write has three call sites and no test — `MirrorView` is the one class on
`check-renderer-views.mjs`'s debt list — so **only a phone can prove it.**

Three things are therefore owed and none of them is a Mac-side run:

1. a real session on **each of the three handsets**, with the box measured against the announced
   geometry — the 1440×3120 Samsung (19.5:9), the 720×1600 Motorolas (2.2222) and the 1080×2408
   vivo (2.2296) are three different ratios and this
   is the exact bug one device hid;
2. a **physical rotation** of the phone, watching the box turn rather than the picture turn inside
   it — the `mirror.rotate` path, which no Mac-side stimulus can produce;
3. a **tap near an edge** on a non-19.5:9 phone, which is the half that was moving fingers.

**And the float window's `RATIO = 19.5 / 9` is still live.** It is the same defect in a third place,
left deliberately: the float window cannot learn the stream's shape until §1 plumbs the geometry
through to it, and half-plumbing it now would mean writing that path twice. It is named in defect
99's row rather than left for someone to find.

## Phase 7 Slice 38 — the mirror has never run, and the control that said it had (2026-09-10)

**How this slice opened.** §3's Mac-side work landed (Slice 37) and the next step was its hardware
debt: prove `mirror.ts` writes `--capture-aspect` when a real `mirror.state` or `mirror.rotate`
arrives, on three handsets. The S25 was connected, `input` was enabled, `Start mirroring` was
pressed — and mirroring failed, repeatedly, in a way that turned out to predate everything done
today.

### Defect 100 — the mirror has never survived its own start

**The chain, in the platform's own words**, from a single deliberate attempt at 10:31:06 with the
buffers read seconds later:

```
06.372  ActivityManager: Background started FGS: Allowed [com.chetan.connectsuite.debug; uidState: TOP]
06.387  am_foreground_service_start: [MirrorService, PROC_STATE_TOP, …, count=7, UNKNOWN, type=32]
06.389  MediaProjectionManagerService: Start the token instance
06.390  [mirror] Display 1440x3120 @600dpi -> capture 480x1040 @200dpi (cap 480)
06.465  DisplayManagerService: Virtual Display: successfully set up virtual display 11
06.465  MediaProjectionMetricsLogger: logInProgress
06.494  am_foreground_service_stop:  [MirrorService, …, 107ms, count=7, STOP_FOREGROUND, type=32]
06.496  MediaProjectionManagerService: Stopped MediaProjection due to foreground service change
06.496  MediaProjectionMetricsLogger: logStopped: wasCaptureInProgress=true stopReason=7
06.496  VirtualDisplayAdapter: Virtual display device released because media projection stopped
```

**107 milliseconds.** Consent, token, display and encoder are all fine; the foreground service that
authorises the projection stops being foreground, and Android revokes it.

**The `type=32` at both ends is what kills the tempting explanation.** 32 is
`FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_MEDIA_PROJECTION`, so the service had the right type throughout, and the
`ForegroundServiceTypeLoggerModule: Foreground service start for UID: 11011 does not have any types`
line seen earlier is **the API-type logger** (camera/microphone/location), not the FGS type. It was
flagged as unresolved rather than concluded, and it would have sent a fix at a manifest that was
already correct — verified **in the installed APK**, not in source: `foregroundServiceType=0x20` on
the `<service>`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PROJECTION` in the permission list.

**What is not established, and why more log reading cannot settle it.** AOSP records
`STOP_FOREGROUND` for the branch where a service is *taken out of the foreground*, which is what
`Service.stopForeground()` does — and there is **no `stopForeground` call anywhere in the phone
codebase**. Every foreground-service call we make is: `ServiceCompat.startForeground` and `stopSelf`
in `LinkService`, the same two in `ConnectionService`, and `startForeground` / `stopSelf` (no-consent
branch) / `stopService` in `MirrorService`. The demotion is not logged with a caller at default
verbosity. The next step is therefore an instrument and not a fix — see the pre-registration below.

### The control was wrong, and it is the fourth of its shape

Asked for the phone's account, this run reported a passing control: **7 `Mirror session started`,
the most recent that morning.** That was a *registration line standing in for an execution line*.
`Mirror session started` is written at the end of `onServiceReady` — it means *we got this far*, not
*frames flowed*.

The execution line is the 2-second stats ticker, which only runs while a session is live:

| | `link.log` (09-09 20:22 → 09-10) | `link.log.1` (09-06 → 09-09 20:22) |
|---|---|---|
| `Mirror session started` | 7 | **0** |
| `Encoded +N frames` | **0** | **0** |

**Not one session in 4,720 lines of surviving log has ever produced a frame tick.** The rotated file
holds no mirror activity at all, so "it worked yesterday" cannot be supported *or* refuted from what
the phone still holds — the honest statement is that the failure is present in the oldest attempt
that survives, and predates the accessibility toggle, the §3 build and the packaged relaunch, all of
which happened on 09-10.

This is the fourth sighting of the shape `CLAUDE.md` already names, and the first where the wrong
control was **offered as a pass** rather than merely relied on. It is recorded in the rule's own
section there.

### Defect 101 — the app's own noise ate the evidence

The `am_foreground_service_*` records for the *first* set of attempts were gone by the time they
were asked for, because `ConnectionService` re-posts notification `1001` **twice every eight
seconds**, forever, each enqueue waking `NotificationManagerService` and taking two partial wake
locks. Five consecutive ticks from the events buffer:

```
10:26:36.295 / .301    notification_enqueue [11011,8229,…,1001,…]
10:26:44.301 / .306
10:26:52.307 / .311
10:27:00.305 / .307
10:27:08.315 / .319
```

Nobody was looking for it. It was found because it destroyed an instrument — the second time in this
project that the app's own output has eaten the evidence about the app.

### Pre-registered: the instrument, and what each outcome means

Written before the build so neither answer can be rationalised afterwards. `stopForeground` is
overridable; `MirrorService` gets an override that logs a stack and calls through, and **nothing
else changes in that build** — no fix, so the reading is clean.

| Outcome | What it means | What is fixed |
|---|---|---|
| the line **appears** | our process calls `stopForeground`, and the stack names the caller | a code fix at that call site |
| the line **never appears** | nothing in our process calls it; the demotion is the platform's | a different repair entirely — how the service is started, or a One UI behaviour — and every hour spent reading our own code would have been wasted |

**Blocked behind this:** §3's three-handset hardware verification. No session survives long enough
to announce a geometry, so there is nothing for the stage to take its shape from.

### The appop experiment — prediction, and what came back

Pre-registered before the flip: *if the FGS survives past 116 ms and the stats ticker emits
`Encoded +N frames`, this was never a code defect and the fix is onboarding plus a capability check.
If it does not, the op is a red herring.*

Original value recorded first (`RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND: ignore`), then set to `allow`, then one tap.

```
am_foreground_service_start  MirrorService  17:41:40.341   ← and NO matching stop
                                                              still foreground at 17:45:08
dumpsys                      MirrorService  isForeground=true  types=0x00000020
link.log                     94 × "Encoded +N frames"
                             +203 frames (101.5/s)  +227 (113.5/s)  +193 (96.5/s)
```

**116 ms before, 3½ minutes and counting after, with real frames.** The prediction is met on both
clauses. **Defect 100 is not a code defect.** The mirror was never broken; the app was
background-restricted and could not hold the foreground service the projection requires.

### It fixed one service and not the other, and that is the second finding

```
MirrorService       isForeground=true    types=0x00000020
ConnectionService   isForeground=false   types=0x00000000
LinkService         isForeground=false   types=0x00000000
```

`MirrorService` calls `startForeground` unconditionally in `onStartCommand` and re-claimed the state
by itself on the next tap. `LinkService` guards that call behind a field that is set once and never
reset — **defect 103** — so it stayed demoted after the restriction was lifted and
`scripts/link-up.sh` check 1 still fails. Lifting the restriction is necessary and not sufficient.

### Defect 99 — verified on hardware, on the S25, through a real rotation

The write that no test could reach, taken from the running app on a live session. The phone rotated
during the run, which supplied the `mirror.rotate` stimulus without anyone arranging it:

```
phone announces      Capturing 2340×1080 · cap 1080 on the short edge
rotation readout     90°
--capture-aspect     inline=2.1666666666666665     ← INLINE: only applyCaptureAspect() writes it
matches announcement YES  (expected 2.166667)
stage box            560 × 258.5   aspect 2.1667   ← the BOX is landscape
canvas element       560 × 258.5   backing 2340 × 1080
LETTERBOX            barX 0px   barY 0px
frames               8425 frames · 119 fps
```

Read as an **inline** style property rather than the computed value, because the stylesheet's `var()`
fallback would supply a number whether the app wrote one or not — and because a stale inline value
left by this morning's own probe had to be cleared first, which would otherwise have certified the
app for a write the instrument made. Screenshot:
`docs/evidence/mirror-fit-2026-09-10/s25-live-landscape.png`.

**One handset of three.** The moto g34, moto g45 and the vivo are still owed, and they are the point
of the exercise — 720×1600 is a third ratio and the vivo's is unread.

## Phase 7 Slice 39 — the restriction gets a name, and the mirror gets nine (2026-09-11)

Defects **102** and **104**, both from a keyboard. No device was touched in this slice and that is
stated up front, because the one thing it does not establish is the one a device would.

### 1 · What was built

| | |
|---|---|
| `core/.../link/BackgroundRestriction.kt` | the copy (pure, no Android symbol) **and** `BackgroundRestrictionReading`, the single home for `ActivityManager.isBackgroundRestricted()` |
| `CapabilityContract` | `Contract.needsForegroundService`, true for `mirror`; `blockedByBackgroundRestriction`; `advertisable` takes `backgroundRestricted` with **no default** |
| `Capabilities.kt` | `CapabilityStatus.backgroundRestricted`, the fourth gate on `advertised`, the reason branch, and `CapabilityHold` / `heldBackSummary` |
| `app/.../LinkRoute.kt` | the card, **at rest** above Advanced, with a deep link to App info |
| `mirror-module/.../MirrorStopReason.kt` | nine reasons, each with an `Actor`; `stop()` takes one instead of a `String` |

### 2 · The measurement that decided the shape, and it is a negative one

**The restriction is not blanket.** With `RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND: ignore` set on the S25 for twelve
hours on 2026-09-10, `sms`, `contacts`, `notifications`, `files` and the rest answered normally; the
only thing that failed was the only thing that needs a foreground service. So the gate is declared
per capability by `Contract.needsForegroundService`, and the test asserts the **whole** reached set
— `assertEquals(listOf(mirror), reached)` — rather than mirror's membership of it, because
`assertTrue(mirror in reached)` passes just as well when the restriction blankets everything, which
is the tempting wrong fix.

### 3 · Two readings of one fact, deliberately

`CapabilityDetector` reads the restriction on every `refresh()`; `MirrorEngine` reads it again at
the instant a projection is revoked. That is not redundancy. One UI can set the op while the app is
backgrounded, which is the exact window no refresh covers, and the revoke is the moment the answer
buys something. There is no watcher: `AppOpsManager.startWatchingMode` is public, the op string
`android:run_any_in_background` is **not** (no `OPSTR_` constant in `android.jar` 36.1), and
hardcoding an undocumented string to depend on it firing is worse than re-reading.

### 4 · What the platform does not supply, checked rather than recalled

```
$ javap -classpath <android.jar 36.1> android.media.projection.MediaProjection\$Callback
  public void onCapturedContentResize(int, int);
  public void onCapturedContentVisibilityChanged(boolean);
  public void onStop();                                   ← no reason, at 36.1
$ javap … android.media.projection.MediaProjection
  public void stop();                                     ← and none to give
```

Both `android-36` and `android-36.1` were read. So the stop reason is **derived**, and
`AndroidRevoked` names the two causes it cannot separate rather than picking the likelier one.

### 5 · Red-first: 12 mutations, 12 red

Each reintroduces the defect its test is named for. The harness prints the gradle exit code beside
every verdict and refuses a verdict from a build that did not compile — the stale-XML row in
`CLAUDE.md`.

| | mutation | went red |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | `mirror` stops declaring `needsForegroundService` | withholds-mirror-and-nothing-else; not-advertisable |
| M2 | `advertisable` stops applying the fourth gate | not-advertisable |
| M3 | the restriction blankets every capability | withholds-mirror-and-nothing-else; sms-and-contacts-go-on-working |
| M4 | `advertised` stops consulting the restriction | the reason; the summary; the 16-combination enumeration |
| M5 | the hold buckets revert to the two the phone used to count | the summary; the enumeration |
| M6 | the two revoke sentences collapse into one | a-revoke-on-a-restricted-phone |
| **M7** | **the platform revoke goes back to `"Screen capture was stopped on the phone."`** | **names-Android-and-never-the-person** |
| M8 | the restricted revoke drops its fix hint | names-the-restriction; only-stop-that-sends-anyone-to-a-setting |
| M9 | the unrestricted revoke claims the user tapped Stop | claims-neither-cause |
| M10 | the copy offers a retry (wrong fix 1) | no-copy-offers-a-retry |
| M11 | the copy points at battery optimisation (wrong fix 2) | no-copy-sends-to-battery-optimisation |
| M12 | the button claims to reach the Battery page | names-the-two-taps |

**M7 is the one worth the row, because it was green first.** The original test asserted that no two
sentences were *too alike*, by word-set overlap — a proxy for the rule, and a proxy that passed with
the **exact defect sentence restored**, because the sibling sentence had been reworded in the same
change so the pair was no longer close while the defect was back. The rule is **attribution**, not
similarity. `Actor` is now a field on the type and the test asserts the sentence agrees with it; M7
goes red on the first clause, whatever the other eight sentences say.

That is this project's third-variety test failure — *the test calls the rule correctly, at a layer
the defect is not in* — caught by mutation rather than by review, which is the only thing that
catches it.

### 6 · Counts, with the artifact age beside them

```
core 126 · mirror-module 49 · input-module 44 · app 11 · sync-module 212   =  442, 0 failures
results files written 12s ago; gradle exit 0
```

Up from 431 at the start of the slice, of which **one was failing**: `ProtocolNamespaceTest > every
feature message names a real capability` had been red on this branch since O4 added
`MessageType.STORAGE_STATE` without its system-set exemption. It is fixed here, and the reason it
survived is the module-blindness of defect 65 with the modules the other way round — the commit that
added the type ran `npm test` in `desktop/` and not the phone's suite. Two new classes:
`BackgroundRestrictionTest` (12) and `MirrorStopReasonTest` (11).

### 7 · What this slice does **not** establish

**`isBackgroundRestricted()` has never returned `true` on any device in this project.** The op was
restored to `allow` on the S25 at the owner's instruction and is unset on both Motorolas and the
vivo. So the *decision* is proven and the *write* is not — which is the `LinkWaitStatus` split
stated in advance instead of discovered in six weeks: eleven green tests over a decision, and a
feature that had never once worked, because no test could reach the line that filled the field in.

The stimulus, one command, with its control:

```
scripts/adb-pinned.sh samsung shell cmd appops set com.chetan.connectsuite.debug RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND ignore
#  expect: the phone's Mac screen draws the restriction card at rest;
#          `mirror` leaves the advertised set; the Mac's Mirror pane greys with CAPABILITY_REASON;
#          a mirror.start refused, and the stop sentence naming Android and the restriction
scripts/adb-pinned.sh samsung shell cmd appops set com.chetan.connectsuite.debug RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND allow
#  control: the card must GO AWAY and `mirror` must come back. A card that draws in both
#           states is a card that is reading nothing.
```

The control is the second half and it is the half that matters: without it the reading is a card
that might be drawn unconditionally, which is the hidden-grid failure in a new pane.

**Written as a script on 2026-09-11 — `scripts/defect102-read.sh` — before the phone was on the
bus.** Three phases (BEFORE / DURING / AFTER), the op restored by a trap on every exit path
including a mid-run failure, the pass criterion **read out of `BackgroundRestriction.kt`** rather
than typed from memory, and every UI dump checked for an anchor known to be on that screen so an
empty dump reports `NO READING` instead of an absence.

It also carries a **precondition that refuses**, found statically while writing it and worth more
than the script: `LinkRoute` holds its diagnostics as `remember(capabilities) { … }`, keyed on the
**advertised set**. The card therefore moves only when `mirror` enters or leaves that set — and
`mirror` needs the video channel served, which needs a Mac connected. On a phone with no Mac,
`mirror` is already withheld, the set does not change when the op is set, and **the card never
appears**. That would read as *"detection does not work"*; it is the different sentence *this
reading cannot be taken in this state*, and confusing the two is the entire subject of this defect.
So the script checks the advertised set first and exits 2 with that explanation rather than
producing a false negative.

**And `MirrorEngine.onStop` itself is unreached by any test**, because it is a platform callback
inside a class needing a `Context`, a live `MediaProjection` and an encoder. The decision was
extracted to `MirrorStopReason.revoked` so a JVM test can call it; what remains in the callback is
taking the reading and passing it in, and the honest status of that line is **unproven**, by the
same stimulus above.

## Phase 7 Slice 40 — the fit on a second ratio: **pre-registered, STILL NOT RUN** (2026-09-11)

> **2026-09-12: still owed.** The moto g34, the moto g45 and the vivo are all away. Slice 43 took
> the readings the Samsung can give — including the landscape half, which is the falsifiable one on
> that handset — and **none of it discharges this slice.** This is a pre-registration; its six
> outcomes have had no device pointed at them.

**Written before the phone was on the bus, and that is the point.** Slice 37 proved the box rule
against `--capture-aspect` values a probe set by hand. What it could not reach is whether `mirror.ts`
*writes* that property when a real `mirror.state` or `mirror.rotate` arrives — three call sites, no
test, `MirrorView` on `check-renderer-views.mjs`'s debt list. Only a phone settles it, and the swap
costs the S25's pairing (defect 17), so the expectations go down first.

### The instrument

`scripts/mirror-fit-probe.mjs <label>`, against a **live** session. It reads the stream's shape
**twice, by two different routes**:

| | route | written from |
|---|---|---|
| `announcedAspect` | `--capture-aspect` on `#mirror-stage` | `this.capture` — what the phone announced on the **control** channel |
| `decodedAspect` | the canvas's intrinsic `width`/`height` | `frame.displayWidth/Height` — a **decoded frame** off the video socket |

Agreement between them is the thing that says the announcement path and the pixel path describe one
phone. Disagreement is a finding and is reported as one.

**The lookalike it refuses.** An untouched canvas is **300×150** — aspect **2.000** — which sits one
decimal place from the moto's 2.2222 and the vivo's 2.2296 and would be read as a successful
landscape reading by anyone rounding to two figures. The probe exits 3 and prints `NOT A READING`
rather than reporting it.

### The device

```
moto g45 5G   ZN4222NSN6   Android 15 / sdk 35   720x1600 @280dpi
label: moto45        (`moto` is the g34 and must not be merged with it)
```

720 / 1600 = **0.45** portrait, 1600 / 720 = **2.22222** landscape. The vivo is **2.22963** and the
two are 0.3% apart, so one of the pair answers the ratio for now; the vivo is not thereby proven and
is not to be recorded as if it were.

### Pre-registered outcomes

| # | reading | what it means | what happens next |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | portrait stage aspect **0.4500 ± 0.005**, bars 0, and `announcementAgreesWithPixels` | the write happens on `mirror.state`; Slice 37's box rule holds on a second ratio | rotate the phone and take row 2 |
| 2 | after a **physical** rotation the stage aspect becomes **2.2222 ± 0.005** and the box turns | the `mirror.rotate` write happens too — the half no Mac-side stimulus can produce | take row 3 |
| 3 | a tap near a **short edge** lands within a few capture px of the intended point, per `input.ts`'s aimed-at line and the phone's own receipt | `pointInCapture` maps against the picture on a non-19.5:9 phone — the half that was moving fingers | defect 99's hardware half is discharged for two ratios of three |
| 4 | `announcedAspect` is **null** with a live session | `mirror.ts` never wrote the property; Slice 37 proved a stylesheet over a path that does not run | defect 99 **reopens**, and the box rule is unproven on every device including the S25 |
| 5 | the two aspects **disagree** | the phone announces one geometry and sends frames of another — a *new* defect, and it would make the S25's clean run a coincidence of that phone's cap | file it before touching the fit; the fit reading is not takeable until it is understood |
| 6 | stage matches `announcedAspect` but bars are non-zero | the stage is right and the canvas is not filling it — a CSS fault, not a geometry one | the specificity collision is back; check `maxHeightOnCanvas` in the same output |

Rows **4 and 5 are the ones that cost something**, and they are written down here because they are
the two a person who has just fixed this bug would least like to read. Row 4 in particular would mean
Slice 37's four green rows measured the stylesheet correctly and the feature not at all — which is
the third-variety test failure with a probe in the place of a unit test.

### What this run will **not** establish, whatever it returns

- **The vivo.** 2.22963 is near-identical and is *not* covered by a moto reading; it stays owed.
- **The S25.** It must be re-scanned after the swap, and until it is, this project has **one** paired
  handset at a time — defect 17.
- **The float window.** `RATIO = 19.5 / 9` in `shared/floatGeometry.ts` is still live and is the same
  defect in a third place, deliberately left until §1 plumbs the geometry through.

## Phase 7 Slice 41 — the half that was never asked (2026-09-11)

Two records from the 102/104 sitting, both of them about instruments rather than features.

### 1 · A green is a statement about the suite that ran

`ProtocolNamespaceTest > every feature message names a real capability` was committed **red** and
lived on this branch for days. The commit that broke it added `MessageType.STORAGE_STATE` without
its system-set exemption, ran `npm test` in `desktop/`, saw **623 green**, and committed. The
phone's suite was never asked.

**Nine commit hooks existed and not one read a test result.** All nine read documents — the defect
register, the protocol spec, the renderer views, the version scheme. The practice that was supposed
to cover the rest was *run the suite*, which is a rule enforced by someone remembering, in the file
that says what that is worth.

`scripts/check-suites-run.mjs` + `scripts/hooks/suites-were-run.sh`, the **ninth** enforcement point:

| | |
|---|---|
| what it reads | Gradle's `*.xml` per module, and `desktop/.test-run.json` |
| where the Mac record comes from | `desktop/scripts/run-tests.mjs`, now behind `npm test`, writing **on every run, pass or fail** |
| what it denies | a touched half that is `RED`, `UNRUN` or `STALE` |
| what it always says | **which half it did not check**, as `NOT CHECKED`, rather than by silence |

**It does not run the suites.** Both halves on every commit is ~15 s warm and minutes cold, and a
hook that slow is routed around inside a week — which is the failure mode the enforcement section is
about. It reads the artifacts and prints their age, which is the repo's own stale-XML rule turned
into a check: *an artifact older than the run is a memory, not a result.*

**Three verdicts, not two.** `UNRUN` (this half has said nothing), `STALE` (it said something about
different bytes) and `RED` (it answered, and the answer was no) are different findings needing
different sentences. Collapsing them is the empty-versus-failed mistake.

**Its instrument is `mtime`, and it says so in its own output.** An operation that restores old
mtimes — a `git stash pop`, a checkout of an older revision — can leave a source looking older than
an artifact that never tested it. So it prints the two timestamps it compared and states that it
checks *whether you ran it*, not that the artifact is of these exact bytes.

#### The readings

Red-first against the **verbatim** historical case, which is the only case it is known to have
missed:

```
C · RED    exemption for MessageType.STORAGE_STATE removed — the defect exactly
           gradle exit: 1
           phone: RED — 442 tests, 0s old, 1 failing            CHECKER EXIT: 1
D · CONTROL restored
           phone: NOT CHECKED — this commit does not touch it   CHECKER EXIT: 0

A · STALE  a staged Kotlin change with older artifacts
           phone: STALE — 442 tests, 2040s old                  EXIT: 1
B · CONTROL the same change, Gradle re-run in the same shell
           phone: GREEN — 442 tests, 0s old                     EXIT: 0
```

The hook itself was driven with a staged change and returned `deny` with the report in the reason.
14 fixtures, each carrying its opposite, including *a docs-only commit touches neither half* — the
control that keeps this from firing on every documentation edit and being switched off.

#### And it caught a regression of its own author, immediately

Moving the test glob out of `desktop/package.json` and into the new wrapper made **all 53** Mac test
files read as orphans on the first run of `check-orphan-tests.mjs`. The guard was right: it reads
the discovery rule out of that script, so the glob stays there and reaches the wrapper as argv.
**A guard that reads a rule out of one file is a reason not to move the rule.**

### 2 · A test that asserted a likeness, and the mutation that found it

The first guard for defect 104 asserted that no two stop sentences were **too alike**, by word-set
overlap. It is not a silly check — it went red against the original pair and against several
mutations. It **passed with the exact defect sentence restored**.

```
M7   AndroidRevoked.sentence := "Screen capture was stopped on the phone."
     → 46 tests completed, 0 failed          NO TEST WENT RED
```

The sibling had been reworded in the same change, from *"Stopped on the phone."* to *"You stopped
mirroring on the phone."*, so the pair was no longer close while the defect was fully back.

**A distance is a claim about two things, and either of them can move.** The rule constrains one
sentence; the test constrained a gap, and a gap is satisfiable by moving the thing that was never
wrong. `MirrorStopReason.Actor` is the fix — a closed enum on the type, and an assertion that *a
reason whose actor is `ANDROID` names Android and never says "you"*, which is one sentence
constrained by itself. M7 then goes red on the first clause whatever the other eight say.

Recorded in `CLAUDE.md` twice: as the **fourth variety** of test that cannot fail (beside the test
that restates the rule, the rule a test cannot reach, and the test at the wrong layer), and as a row
in the control table. Its relatives there are both **queries** — step 49's shared button label, and
the `/drop|upload|send to phone/` regex that matched the banner apologising for the absent
affordance. This is the first time the shape got into the suite, where no reading and no control can
see it and only mutation can.

## Phase 7 Slice 42 — defect 102's write, taken (2026-09-12)

Slice 39 built the detection, proved the **decision** with 23 tests and 12 mutations, and said
plainly that `ActivityManager.isBackgroundRestricted()` had **never once returned `true`** on any
device in this project. This is that reading, run against the pre-registered table in Slice 39 §7.
`scripts/defect102-read.sh samsung`, and `scripts/caps-reason-probe.mjs mirror` for the far end.

### The phone

```
                      card   dump bytes   advertised set
0 · BEFORE  allow       0      18,248     apps,calls,clipboard,contacts,files,mirror,notifications,photos,remote,sms
1 · DURING  ignore      1      20,798     apps,calls,clipboard,contacts,files,        notifications,photos,remote,sms
2 · AFTER   allow       0      18,248     apps,calls,clipboard,contacts,files,mirror,notifications,photos,remote,sms
```

**The restore is the reading that matters and it is the third row.** A card that appears is one bit;
a card that appears *and leaves* is that bit plus the proof that something is reading a live value
rather than drawing unconditionally. The dump byte count is an independent second signal and it is
the sharper one: **18,248 before and 18,248 after, byte for byte**, with +2,550 in between. That is
the card's own node tree arriving and going away.

`mirror` leaves the advertised set and comes back, and **nothing else moves** — nine capabilities
identical across all three rows. The measurement that the gate is not blanket, taken on the device
rather than argued from the twelve-hour observation it was designed against.

### The far end

`scripts/caps-reason-probe.mjs` reads the Overview chip's **accessible sentence**, not its colour —
the chip was a name and a background colour until defect 26, so the visually-hidden span is the
primary channel. Both routes to the fact are read, and they agree:

| | advertised | spoken | title |
|---|---|---|---|
| BEFORE | `true` | `: available` | `null` |
| **DURING** | `false` | `: unavailable, the phone has restricted this app's background activity, so it cannot hold the foreground service screen capture needs — open ConnectSuite on the phone to fix it` | the same sentence |
| AFTER | `true` | `: available` | `null` |

Control: **12 chips on the page** in every reading, all twelve named in the output. The sentence is
`BackgroundRestriction.CAPABILITY_REASON` verbatim, over the existing `unavailable` map, with no
protocol change.

### Three instrument faults, all caught by their controls, none reaching a finding

Recorded because every one of them produced a confident wrong answer first:

| | the instrument | reported | actually |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `strings` over 21 dex files, 25 MB | every count **empty** — including `ConnectSuite`, the positive control | `grep` gives no output at all on that blob. The **positive control returning empty is what refused the run**; the APK was fine, and Gradle's `packageDebug UP-TO-DATE` (content-hashed, not mtime) answered the question instead |
| 2 | `run-as PKG sh -c 'tail … link.log'` | `<none logged>` → *"no Mac connected"* | the `sh -c` form returns **nothing** on this handset; the direct `run-as PKG tail …` returns 3,720 lines. The script then **gave wrong advice** — connect a Mac that was already connected |
| 3 | a tag histogram over the log | `[samsung]` as a log tag | my own `2>&1` merging `adb-pinned.sh`'s stderr banner into the stream — the **exact failure that script exists to prevent**, committed by its author two days later |

Fault 2 is now a control in the script: `wc -l` on the log must return non-zero before anything is
concluded from its contents, and a dead query reports `NO READING` rather than a negative. Fault 3
is the standing rule and needs no new machinery — it needs the `2>&1` not to be typed.

### Two things this run did not set out to find

- **The accessibility service is off on this device.** `enabled_accessibility_services` is `null`
  and `accessibility_enabled` is `0`, so `input` is absent from every advertised set above.
  **Unattributable**: no before-reading was taken across the reinstall, and `CLAUDE.md` records that
  a force-stop removes this grant permanently while `install -r` preserves it. Stated as an observed
  state, not as a consequence of anything done here.
- **The three bottom-nav cells carry no `content-desc` and no text of their own**, so there is no
  named target for the Mac tab and the script reaches it by coordinates derived from a dump taken
  seconds earlier, announced in its output. That is the coordinate rule's last resort with both its
  conditions met; the right fix is a `contentDescription` on those three cells and it is owed.

**Defect 102 is closed.** The detection is built, the reading is taken on hardware with its control,
and the sentence reaches the Mac.

## Phase 7 Slice 43 — the fit on hardware, and the float A/B (2026-09-12)

Live session on the SM-S938B, physical rotations by the owner. Three devices were expected for this
slice; **only the Samsung was available** — see §3 for what that costs.

### 1 · The box, measured in both orientations

| | portrait | **landscape** |
|---|---|---|
| stage box | 267.69 × 579.98 | **560 × 258.46** |
| stage aspect | 0.46154 | **2.16667** |
| announced aspect (control channel) | 0.46154 | **2.16667** |
| decoded aspect (video socket) | 0.46154 — canvas 1080×2340 | **2.16667 — canvas 2340×1080** |
| letterbox | 0, 0 | **0, 0** |
| rotation readout | 0° | **270°** |
| `max-height` on canvas | `none` | `none` |

Control: 13 `section[data-screen]` on the page in every reading.

**Both routes to the stream's shape agree**, which is the half Slice 37 could not reach — that run
set `--capture-aspect` by hand and said so. Here it is written by `mirror.ts` from a real
`mirror.state`/`mirror.rotate`, and the canvas's intrinsic size comes off decoded frames. Two
independent paths, one answer.

### 2 · The tap, with its prediction written first

| | portrait | **landscape** |
|---|---|---|
| clicked | viewport (764, 291) | viewport (764, 285) |
| fraction of picture | (0.5, 0.02) | (0.5, 0.02) |
| **predicted** | (542, 45) | **(1172, 21)** |
| **measured** | (542, 45) | **(1172, 21)** |
| error | **0, 0** | **0, 0** |
| resolution | 4.03 capture px per viewport px | 4.18 |

Measured from the Mac's own `[input] input.tap delivered (x,y on #id WxH)` line — the log that did
not exist while defect 99 was live, and whose absence is why the defect could not have been found
from a log.

**A correction to what this slice originally claimed it would prove.** The plan said the landscape
tap would separate the fixed mapping from the pre-fix one by ~400 capture px. It does not, and the
first run proved it: both predictions came out **identical**. The discriminator was the *letterbox*,
and the box fix removes the letterbox — so once the box is right, a tap can no longer falsify the
old bug. What the landscape tap does still test is that the mapping uses the **announced**
2340×1080 rather than the canvas's intrinsic size, which lags a frame behind on a just-rotated
phone. That is the claim it is recorded against.

### 3 · Coverage, stated honestly

**Fit verified on 1 of 3 ratios — and on this handset portrait cannot falsify the bug at all.**

The SM-S938B is exactly 19.5:9, which is the ratio the pre-fix stylesheet hard-coded. In portrait the
old code drew no bars and the old `pointAt` agreed with the new one to the pixel, so a clean portrait
reading is **consistent with the bug being fully present**. Landscape is the falsifiable half on this
device, and landscape passed.

What is still owed, and it is the point of the exercise:

| device | ratio | state |
|---|---|---|
| moto g34 | 720×1600 → 2.22222 | **away** — not measured |
| moto g45 | 720×1600 → 2.22222 | **away** — not measured |
| vivo | 1080×2408 → 2.22963 | **away** — not measured |

**Slice 40 stays owed.** It is a pre-registration, not a result, and the two Motorolas and the vivo
have contributed nothing to it. The g34 and g45 share a build fingerprint and are one reading of that
image; the vivo is a genuinely third ratio.

### 4 · The float A/B — **STATE A**

Taken before any code, because the state it measures disappears the moment the float's start path
changes.

```
                      frames   fps    median total   link   decode   peak
A (float closed)       3349    115        8 ms       7 ms    2 ms    35.8 ms
B (float open)         3099    117        9 ms       7 ms    2 ms    34.6 ms
                    load ratio 0.93x
```

Against the rule written before the run — degrade at ≥1.5× latency or ≥30% fps loss, unchanged
within ±15% — this is **STATE A: the float is an independent consumer. Symptoms §1 and §4 are
separate bugs and want separate fixes.**

#### The run before it said STATE B, and it was wrong

```
A  102 frames @ 2 fps    median 5 ms
B  532 frames @ 18 fps   median 8 ms      ratio 1.6  ->  "STATE B — degrades"
```

Phase B did **five times the work**. A latency that rises with throughput is what more frames in
flight looks like **with or without contention**, so the comparison could not separate the hypothesis
from the load. It would have sent the float and the latency drift down a single-fix path on a number
that meant nothing.

**The A/B was missing a comparability precondition, and nothing in an A/B checks one.** An A/B is a
claim that only one variable moved; the guard is now `loadRatio` within 1.4× either way, and the run
above reports **0.93×** beside its verdict. This is the units rule one level up — that rule says two
numbers must be *of the same thing* before a ratio means anything, this says the two *conditions*
must be alike in every way but the one under test.

The first attempt before that one was refused outright by the frames-advanced guard: phase A decoded
**0** frames on a static screen, and its "13 ms" was the median of *retained* samples — a memory, not
a measurement of that window. Motion for both phases is gentle scrolling inside ConnectSuite's own
Mac tab, announced before it ran.

### 5 · Two instrument faults, both now fixed in the shared tooling

- **`openProbe` took the first page target, whichever it was.** The float window opened during a
  latency run, sorted ahead of the main window in `/json`, and the next probe attached to **it** and
  died on a null nav element. It died loudly this time; a probe whose selectors exist in both windows
  would not have. That is the control table's "you are looking at a different machine" one scale
  down, so the fix is the same: the caller names the window, matched on its URL, and an ambiguous
  match **refuses** rather than guessing.
- **The float button is not a toggle.** Its two states are *"Floating window"* and *"Show floating
  window"* — the second focuses the window, it does not close it. Using it as cleanup left the float
  open across two runs, and the next run then refused its own phase A. Closing the float's CDP target
  is what closes it; the main window's label flipping back is the confirmation. **This is a product
  observation, not a bug**: the design says show, and the button does what it says. It is recorded
  because every script that opens the float will otherwise leak one.

## Phase 7 Slice 44 — the keyframe path gets a voice, before it gets a fix (2026-09-12)

The float A/B came back **STATE A** (Slice 43), so §1 is its own bug and is built as one. This slice
is the observability and the state vocabulary. **The start contract is deliberately not in it** —
the request path had no measurement at all, so a fix would have had no before to be compared against.

### 1 · Defect 105 — the diagnosis, confirmed by reading

`H264Canvas.push` returns at `if (!decoder || decoder.state !== 'configured')`, and the branch that
calls `hooks.requestKeyframe()` is **below** it. A float with no decoder drops every access unit,
IDRs included, and asks for nothing: unreachable from its own recovery path.

It is intermittent rather than constant, and the reason matters for the fix. `main.ts`'s `onReady`
replays the retained config to the new window; when that wins the race against the float's listeners
being registered, the decoder configures and all is well — **observed today**, `1 asked / 1 answered`,
decoding. When it loses, nothing ever configures. **The race is the defect**, so the fix is the start
contract and not a retry.

### 2 · Defect 106 — six discards, three a side

| end | what was silent |
|---|---|
| Mac · IPC handler | `link.request('mirror.keyframe', …).catch(() => undefined)` |
| Mac · float onReady | the same line again |
| Mac · float renderer | `floatBridge.mirrorKeyframe().catch(() => undefined)` |
| phone · `MirrorFeature` | handler logged nothing at all |
| phone · `MirrorEngine` | `encoder.get()?.requestKeyframe()` — a null encoder swallowed the request whole |
| phone · `ScreenEncoder` | logged **only** its failure |

All three Mac callers now go through one traced path and each names its reason. `KeyframeTrace`
counts **requested / acked / answered-by-IDR** as three separate numbers, and the phone logs the
request arriving, whether a codec existed, and whether a keyframe followed and how long it took.

#### What the first run found, in nine milliseconds

```
15:25:12.278 [float]  decoder configured from retained parameter sets; asking for a keyframe
15:25:12.278 [float]  asking the phone for a keyframe (1 asked / 0 answered)
15:25:12.279 [mirror] keyframe requested — 1 requested / 0 acked / 0 answered by an IDR
15:25:12.287 [float]  keyframe reached the decoder; arming it and decoding from here
15:25:12.288 [mirror] keyframe request acked — …; an ack is not a frame
```

**The frame beat the ack by a millisecond.** That IDR was already in flight when the request went
out, so the request had nothing to do with it. A cruder instrument would have counted it and
reported the keyframe path as working on its very first run — the confirming-reading failure, and
it would have arrived as good news about a feature under suspicion.

`KeyframeTrace.onKeyframe()` returns null unless a request is outstanding, for exactly this reason:
an idle stream emits periodic IDRs, and counting those makes "answered" say yes forever.

#### And a counter of mine that could only ever read zero

`answered by an IDR` was tallied on the Mac and **nothing called `onKeyframe()` from the video
path**, so the line would have read `N requested / N acked / 0 answered` for the life of the
project. A counter that cannot move is worse than no counter: it reads as a finding rather than as
an absence, and the finding it reads as is the exact one under investigation. Caught by looking at
the first output rather than by any test.

### 3 · Defect 107 — the two states

`renderer/floatWait.ts`, a closed set of four, each with its own sentence and a `blocking` flag:

| kind | blocking | what it means |
|---|---|---|
| `no-parameter-sets` | **yes** | no decoder; the code that would ask is unreachable |
| `awaiting-keyframe` | no | armed, request out, clears when the phone answers |
| `unanswered` | **yes** | ≥3 **outstanding**, so the phone is answering nothing |
| `running` | no | decoding; say nothing |

**`blocking` is the load-bearing part, not the wording**, and the tests assert it rather than the
sentence — the word-overlap lesson from defect 104, applied in advance this time. The `unanswered`
threshold counts **outstanding** requests, not total, so a float answered twenty times out of twenty
stays healthy; the control test asserts exactly that.

### 4 · Two guards widened, both latent the moment the app grew a second window

- **`check-renderer-scripts.mjs` read `index.html` only.** `float.html` loads classic scripts too, so
  a `src/shared/` file added there with an `export` would throw on its first line in the float window
  — defect 94 exactly, in the window the guard does not open. It now reads **every** `.html` under
  `src/renderer` and prints which pages it scanned. The discriminator is unchanged: scope still comes
  from what a page *loads*, never from the directory.
- **`openProbe` took the first page target** (fixed in Slice 43) — and the audit asked for afterwards
  found the same expression in `design-shot.mjs` and `compare-shot.mjs`. Neither is at risk today:
  each spawns its own headless Chrome with one page on its own port. Both now match the URL they
  launched anyway, because the guard is one line and "safe today" is what the renderer-scripts guard
  was too.

### 5 · What is observed, and what is not

| | |
|---|---|
| **observed** | the request → ack path on both ends; the float configuring from a retained config, arming, and decoding; the frame-before-ack ordering |
| **not observed** | `droppedWithNoDecoder` above zero — it needs the onReady race to **lose**, and today it won |
| **not observed** | `answered by an IDR` above zero — it needs a request that actually *causes* an IDR, which the one measurement available says did not happen |

The second row is the honest status of defect 105's own symptom: the code path is read and the
counter is in place, and the state has **not** been reproduced on this machine. The third is the
question the whole slice was built to make answerable, and it is still unanswered — which is a much
better position than the one this started from, where it was unaskable.

## Phase 7 Slice 45 — the start contract, and the race watched losing (2026-09-13)

Defect 105. The float A/B said STATE A, so §1 is its own bug; Slice 44 gave the path a voice; this
is the fix, and **both halves of it are proven on hardware rather than reasoned about**.

### 1 · The contract

| | |
|---|---|
| who asks | **the float**, immediately after its own `floatBridge.on…` registrations, in the same synchronous run — the only participant that knows the handlers exist |
| who answers | **main**, to `event.sender` rather than by broadcast: by construction the window that just said it is ready |
| the answer | the retained config, **or `null` plainly**. `sessionRunning` comes from `video.isOpen()` |
| the limit | one request in flight; a 1 s floor between attempts; the in-flight gate releases after 5 s |
| what was removed | the push on `onReady`. Not narrowed — **removed**. There is no window event in the path |

`sessionRunning` is deliberately **not** derived from `config !== null`. That fallback was written
first and would have made `actionFor`'s `ask-again` branch structurally unreachable — a state drawn
beside states that can happen, which is the Folders-screen lesson. `video.isOpen()` is the real
signal.

### 2 · Proof — `answered by an IDR` above zero, ack **before** frame

Slice 44's one measurement had the frame beating the ack by a millisecond, so the request got credit
for an IDR already in flight. Taken again on a **quiet** stream (0.5–1 fps, phone screen static):

```
00:52:26.945 I [mirror] keyframe requested (PROOF 2: deliberate request on a quiet stream)
                        — 11 requested / 10 acked / 3 answered by an IDR
00:52:26.953 I [mirror] keyframe request acked (+8 ms)          ← the ack precedes the frame
00:52:29.025 I [mirror] keyframe ARRIVED after 2080 ms — 11 requested / 11 acked / 4 answered
```

Corroborated from the phone's own end, by a number nothing on the Mac writes: `last keyframe` in the
encoder's 2-second ticker changed **123968B → 277290B** at 00:52:30.808, against the Mac's ARRIVED
at 00:52:29.025.

Reproduced a second time inside the Reading A run below — ack at `.269`, frame at `+930 ms`,
`4 → 5 answered`.

**The quiet stream is the control, not a convenience.** At 115 fps a request is answered by whatever
IDR was coming anyway and the ordering proves nothing; at 0.5 fps a 2-second gap with an ack inside
it is attributable.

### 3 · Proof — `droppedWithNoDecoder` above zero, and what recovers from it

`delayFloatListeners` (a debug switch, off by default, announced at warning level when on) holds the
float's ask for 3 s, making the losing side of the race deterministic. It was never observed losing
before: on every machine tried here the push won.

**Reading A — the contract, delay ON, live session:**

```
00:54:26.253 [float]  delayFloatListeners is ON — holding the stream-start ask for 3000ms on purpose
00:54:27.141 [float]  dropped 1 access unit(s) with no configured decoder (delta)
                      — nothing has been asked for, because the request path is below this return
00:54:29.255 [float]  stream-start asking (listeners registered (delayed)), attempt 1
00:54:29.256 [float]  stream-start asked: replaying 31B of parameter sets, sessionRunning=true
00:54:29.259 [float]  decoder configured from retained parameter sets; asking for a keyframe
00:54:29.269 [mirror] keyframe request acked — 12 requested / 12 acked / 4 answered
00:54:30.189 [mirror] keyframe ARRIVED after 930 ms — 12 requested / 12 acked / 5 answered
00:54:30.190 [float]  keyframe reached the decoder; arming it and decoding from here
```

**The drop happened and the contract recovered from it.** That is the whole claim, and the first line
is the first time `droppedWithNoDecoder` has been above zero in this project.

**Reading B — the ask disabled, same delay, same session:**

```
droppedWithNoDecoder: 730        hasDecoder: false     decoding: false
requested: 0   answered: 0       ← nothing was ever asked
overlay: SHOWING, "The floating window has not been told how to decode this stream yet. …"
```

**730 against 1.** `requested: 0` is defect 105's mechanism read directly off the running window: the
recovery path is below the return, so nothing asks, so nothing ever arrives.

**What Reading B is and is not.** It reproduces the **losing branch** of the old race
deterministically — no config, no ask, dropping forever — which is the state a user was in whenever
the push lost. It is **not** a byte-for-byte run of the old code, because the old main also pushed on
`onReady` and therefore sometimes won. The push is what made the defect *intermittent*; Reading B
removes the luck and shows what remains. The faithful old-code run would additionally restore that
push, and it costs an Electron restart and a fresh consent tap for no additional information about
the mechanism.

The experiment patched the working tree and reverted it; `TEMPORARY EXPERIMENT` markers are asserted
absent in both `src/` and `dist/` afterwards.

### 4 · What is NOT proven, and what it would cost

**The phone-side instrumentation from defect 106 has never run.** `lastUpdateTime=2026-09-12
13:11:14` — the APK on the device predates it, and a grep for its three new lines
(`mirror.keyframe from …`, `Keyframe requested of the codec`, `Keyframe EMITTED`) returns **0** over
600 lines. Everything in §2 and §3 is Mac-side counting; the phone corroborates only through the
`last keyframe` byte size, which is older instrumentation.

To prove it: `adb install -r` the current debug APK, restart `MainActivity` by name, confirm with
`scripts/link-up.sh`, and take §2's reading again — one reinstall and **one consent tap**, because
the reinstall drops the session and MediaProjection consent cannot be cached.

Also unproven: the 1 s floor and the 5 s in-flight release are unit-tested and have not been seen
firing on hardware, because the contract succeeds on its first attempt every time so far.
