### Found while measuring — four product faults, four instrument faults

Product:
- The ⌘K input drew a boxed control inside the field: styles.css's `input[type='text']` (0,1,1)
  loads later and won at equal specificity. The shell rule is `.palette .palette-field input`.
- The active nav glyph used the lime *fill* in light, faint on the pale pill; it takes
  `--nav-active-glyph` now.
- **The sidebar was 233px to make its content 232**, which moved the whole content column to
  x = 261. The hairline is an inset shadow now; both numbers are Figma's.
- **Reduced transparency drew every card as a selected one**: all translucent surfaces went to
  `--elev-3`, the raised grey, and the palette, toast and tooltips were never listed at all.

Instrument (none became a finding):
- **`head_logo.png`'s alpha > 0 bounds include an invisible haze.** At alpha > 0 the mask is
  1719 × 799 (2.15 : 1, the handoff §13 figure); above alpha 4 it is **1515 × 797 (1.90 : 1)**,
  unchanged to alpha 128. Read at > 0, the correct 114 × 60 mark looked horizontally squashed and
  was nearly "fixed" into a stretched one. The derive script and the test use the visible bounds.
- The island read olive (`rgba(158,214,0,0.12)`, the light value) in dark: read inside the 180ms
  cross-fade straight after a theme switch. Settled on **both** the theme and the colour, it is
  lime. The two-clock rule, again.
- `querySelector('.card')` returned the **hidden** pairing card (`#1C1C1C`, primary). The visible
  panes' cards are `#161616`.
- The packaged app read as an **empty document** (39 bytes of HTML, 0 nav rows) 6–10 s after a
  first launch of the freshly ad-hoc-signed bundle, and complete at 20 s. A missing reading, not a
  broken package.
- `shellPalette.test.ts`'s first harness required `shell.ts` cached and then constructed a second
  `ShellView`: the first mount had two shells on one document and "focused the input twice".

### The packaged app's icon — 2026-09-19

`desktop/build/icon.icns`, derived by `scripts/derive-brand.mjs` from `LOGOS/main_logo.png`: cropped
to its visible tile (alpha > 4, 1100 × 1076), scaled **uniformly** to 824 on the long side — not
stretched square — and centred on a transparent 1024 canvas (Apple's 824-in-1024 grid; used as-is
the tile fills ~88% and sits larger than every other Dock icon). Unpacked with `iconutil -c iconset`:
all ten sizes 16–1024, every corner alpha 0, body at 80%. Re-running the script left the committed
renderer PNGs byte-identical. `mac.icon: build/icon.icns` in `electron-builder.yml`; `dist:dir` no
longer logs *default Electron icon is used*. In `release/mac-arm64/Sidekick.app`: `CFBundleIconFile`
= `icon.icns`, `Resources/icon.icns` sha1 `d4c293d3…` = `build/icon.icns`, `codesign --verify
--deep --strict` OK. `NSWorkspace.icon(forFile:)` on the bundle returns the Sidekick tile.

**What macOS 26 does with it, measured rather than assumed:** it draws the tile **inside a grey
plate** — Tahoe's treatment of a legacy `.icns`. Three geometries were tried in throwaway bundles
(the 824 uniform one shipped, an 824 square, and full-bleed); **all three were plated**, so it is
not the geometry. An un-plated icon needs an Icon Composer `.icon` compiled by `actool` into
`Assets.car`, and this Mac has Command Line Tools only — no Xcode, no `actool`. On macOS 11–15 the
`.icns` is the whole mechanism. The dev build (`npm start`) still shows Electron's icon: nothing
calls `app.dock.setIcon`, and the bundle there is Electron's.

## Sidekick Batch 6a — pairing's *No network*, and the code it used to draw instead — 2026-09-20

Frames `34:11219` (Ready) and `34:12152` (No network). **Neither rendered** — the Figma MCP is not
connected on this account, so both are *built to the handoff*, which is the weaker claim and is what
every row below says.

### Defect 125 — with no network the pairing screen drew a QR code of `0.0.0.0`

`localAddress()` walked `os.networkInterfaces()` for a non-internal IPv4 address and, finding none,
returned the string `'0.0.0.0'`. That value went into the pairing payload, was encoded into a real
QR image, and was drawn under *"Scan this with your phone"* beside `<name> at 0.0.0.0 — valid while
this code is on screen.` `0.0.0.0` is the unspecified address; nothing can connect to it.

**Every layer was truthful about a different thing.** The QR encoded the payload it was given, the
payload carried the address the function returned, and the function returned the platform's value
for *no address at all*. `grep` for the literal found it in **one** place in the whole desktop tree —
the fallback — and **no** reader anywhere. It is the silent-no-op shape decision 6 rules out: a
person photographs a code and nothing ever happens, with nothing on screen able to say why.

The handoff already had the answer drawn: *"No network replaces the code with an explanation,
because a code carries an address and there is none to put in one."*

- `shared/pairReach.ts` — `localPairAddress(interfaces)` returns `{ address, reachable }`; `main.ts`
  is a one-line caller and passes `reachable` back with the payload. **The renderer is never asked
  to infer it from the string**: a `host === '0.0.0.0'` test in the renderer would be two homes for
  one rule in two files, and the process that enumerated the interfaces is the one that knows.
- **Deliberately not claimed:** a link-local `169.254.x.x` reads **reachable**. A phone on the same
  link self-assigns from the same range, so refusing it would be a guess dressed as a reading, and
  wrong in the worse direction — refusing to draw a code that would have worked.
- `pairReach.test.ts`, 7 tests. **Red-first:** the old behaviour (no address treated as usable) →
  **3 red**; `family` compared only as the string `'IPv4'` (Node has reported it as `4`) → **1 red**.
  Its last test runs the rule against this machine's **real** `networkInterfaces()`, because every
  other case is a hand-built list and none of them asks whether the shape being read is the shape
  that arrives.
- `pairing` log line now carries both halves: `QR armed for <host> — scannable=<bool>`. A count of
  armed codes with no reachability beside it read as the good story for a phase.

### The card's two shapes, and the three surfaces that had to agree

`renderer/pairCard.ts` holds the decision and the write; `applyPairShape(reachable)` in
`renderer.ts` is the one call that moves **all three** surfaces — the card, the steps column and the
page subtitle.

- `pairCard.test.ts`, 5 tests through the DOM double. **Red-first, four mutations:** the QR drawn
  anyway (the defect) → **2 red**; the explanation never cleared, so the state is one-way → **2
  red**; the title still reads *scan* → **1 red**; both controls drawn at once → **1 red**.
- **The transition is asserted in both directions over the same nodes.** A screen that enters a
  state correctly and never leaves it looks perfect in every screenshot anybody takes of it.
- `pairSteps.ts` gains `scannable`. *Waiting for a scan* beside a card saying there is nothing to
  scan is the status island's two-writers failure across two surfaces two inches apart. **The
  module's standing rule is preserved and tested**: a later fact still outranks a stale reachability
  reading, so a sighted or paired Mac keeps its `done` step. Red-first: the column ignoring the
  network → **1 red**; a stale reading retracting a later fact → **1 red**.
- `navModel.pairingSubtitle` + `ShellView.subtitleFor` — the header read *"Scan this code once"*
  two lines above the card. This is verbatim the defect `overviewSubtitle` was written for, on the
  screen a stranger sees first. `#page-sub` now has **one writer**.

### Measured in the browser, because the DOM double cannot see a cascade

`scripts/pair-nonetwork-probe.mjs` drives `applyPairShape` — the production function, the real
nodes, the real stylesheet — and reads **`getComputedStyle(...).display`**, not attributes. 9 of 9
readings OK: the QR, its note and the standing copy are all `display: none`; the explanation is one
`state-block` at `tone=warning`; one control, not two; the title no longer says *scan*; and the code
comes back with its own title and button.

**Two things this run is recorded for, and neither is the pass:**

1. **A hypothesis of mine, refuted by its own control.** `.pair-card #qr { display: block }` is an
   author `display` on an id and would beat the user agent's `[hidden]`, so a `[hidden]` companion
   was added to `styles.css` and the comment beside it said the code would otherwise stay on screen.
   The probe was then re-run **with the companion removed** and read `qrDisplay: "none"` anyway:
   `shell.css` line 41 already declares `[hidden] { display: none !important }` globally, added for
   the palette backdrop that did exactly this. The line came back out and the comment now records
   the reading rather than the guess. *The control was only run because the answer had already come
   back the way I wanted it.*
2. **The probe's first run reported a failure that was its own.** It drove `applyPairCard` alone,
   the steps column did not move, and *"the steps column agrees with the card"* read FAIL over
   working code. `applyPairShape` exists because of that reading — one call, three surfaces.
3. **One row reports `NO READING` rather than a verdict.** This Mac is paired, so step 1 is `done`
   before reachability is consulted and the label is *correct* to stay put. Asserting the blocked
   label here would assert that `pairSteps`' own rule is broken. The unpaired combination is
   unreachable on any machine that can run the probe, and `pairSteps.test.ts` covers it.

### Pairing's three inline notices were three geometries

A rename, a refusal and a sighting — three facts of the same weight on one card, carrying
`12px 14px` on `--radius-tile` at 13.5px, against `--space-5 --space-6` on `--radius-control` at
13px. One `.pair-notice` with a `data-tone` of `neutral` / `warning` / `live`; the ids and the
`role="status"` are unchanged, so nothing that reads them moved. This is the five-vocabularies
problem `stateBlock.ts` settled for the panes, surviving on the one screen a stranger sees first.

| File | What |

| `pairing-code-1440x920.png` | the code shape, dark, at the demo size |
| `pairing-code-light-1440x920.png` | the same in light |
| `pairing-code-1100x700.png` | the same at the minimum supported size |
| `pairing-no-network-SYNTHETIC-1440x920.png` | `34:12152`, dark |
| `pairing-no-network-light-SYNTHETIC-1440x920.png` | `34:12152`, light |
| `pairing-no-network-SYNTHETIC-1100x700.png` | `34:12152` at 1100 × 700 |

**The no-network captures are SYNTHETIC and the label is load-bearing.** This Mac is on the network
that carries the session being measured; the state is produced by calling `applyPairShape(false)`,

## Sidekick Batch 6b — the shell's cross-cutting surfaces, measured — 2026-09-20

The last group in the full-app pass: palette, island, header, sidebar, toasts, menus, dialogs,
tooltips, focus rings, keyboard shortcuts, both themes, reduced transparency and reduced motion.

**Every one of these is invisible in a pane screenshot.** A focus ring exists only while a control
is focused by keyboard; a tooltip only while a pointer rests; a reduced-transparency rule only on a
machine with the setting on. Twelve routes photographed at rest, mouse elsewhere, cannot show any
of them — so this group is a sweep, `scripts/shell-parity-sweep.mjs`, not a look.

### What the sweep found, and three of the four findings were my own instrument

| Reading | First answer | What it was |
|---|---|---|
| focus rings | **0 of 17** | `el.focus()` from a script does not fire the user agent's `:focus-visible` heuristic. Zero rings on a fully ringed app |
| Photos' rings | **14 of 166** | `rawForcePseudo` stalled at 152 nodes and returned partial. `DOM`/`CSS` are **per-target** domains whose node map outlives the websocket, so an interrupted run poisons the next one — measured: after one, a selector matching **7** elements timed out; after restarting the app, instant |
| the whole sweep | **`OK — 0 of 0`** | every route refused to draw, and `0 === 0` is true. A sweep that measured nothing certified everything |
| the New-conversation panel | **not a dialog** | **real** — see defect 128 |

The first two were fixed in `scripts/probe.mjs`: `rawForcePseudo` forces the pseudo-class through
CDP, in parallel, with a **reported** node cap, and disables the `DOM`/`CSS` domains before
enabling them so a reading does not depend on how the previous one ended. `rawEmulateMedia` was
added for the same reason — an accessibility setting cannot be produced from page script.

**The third is the one worth carrying forward.** `0 of 0` passing is this repo's page-cap row
arriving *inside a sweep written in the same sitting as a probe that has the same guard*. The
denominator is the verdict's own control, and it is now checked before the ratio: an empty one is
**NO READING** and counts as a failure, and the routes that refused are named rather than summed
away. The committed artifact is that run —
`docs/evidence/sidekick-batch6/shell-parity-sweep-BLOCKED.txt` — because it is what the guard
looks like when it fires.

### The reading with the link up, taken at 17:15 the same sitting

| | |
|---|---|
| focus rings | **816 of 816** across all twelve routes, with the control at **0 of 816 outlined at rest** |
| translucent at rest | island, sidebar, palette, toast, pair notice — the control that makes the next row mean something |
| reduced transparency | **0** surfaces still blurred |
| reduced motion | **0** surfaces still transitioning |
| palette | `role=dialog`, `aria-modal=true`, labelled |
| toast | `role=status`, `aria-live=polite` |

**That run is not the committed artifact and the reason is a device condition, not a choice.** The
phone began refusing this Mac's certificate mid-sitting — `SSLV3_ALERT_CERTIFICATE_UNKNOWN`, SSL
alert 46, on every retry — so the app correctly forces the pairing screen and every other route is
a no-op. Re-pairing is a scan on the owner's phone and their trust store, so it was not done. The
numbers above were read live and displayed; the file beside them is the blocked run.

### Defect 126 — the menu bar named the app by its npm package and offered devtools to users

With no `Menu.setApplicationMenu`, Electron installs its own. Read live through `System Events`:

```
menu bar       : Apple, Electron, File, Edit, View, Window
the app menu   : About sidekick-desktop … Hide sidekick-desktop … Quit sidekick-desktop
View           : Reload, Force Reload, Toggle Developer Tools, …
```

Three separate things, none cosmetic. The app is called **Electron** in the one place macOS always
shows a name. About / Hide / Quit read **`sidekick-desktop`** — the npm package name, never meant
to be read by anyone. And **Force Reload and Toggle Developer Tools were offered to users**: a
person exploring the menu bar can throw away the renderer's state, or open a devtools pane over a
window specified to the half-pixel.

`main/appMenu.ts` builds a real one. **The routes come from the renderer**, which already owns
`navModel.SCREENS` for the sidebar and the palette — one list, three surfaces, so a route added
appears in all three or in none. `navModel` is a renderer module, so main importing it would be the
coupling pointed the wrong way.

- The accelerators become the menu's, which means ⌘1…⌘0 no longer reach the page. They route
  through the same `shell.route` the sidebar calls, over one IPC message — **not a second
  navigation path**. What it buys is the thing a palette cannot: the shortcuts become
  **discoverable**, printed beside their destinations where a Mac user looks.
- **Edit is not furniture.** Without it macOS has nowhere to send ⌘C / ⌘V / ⌘X / ⌘A and copy and
  paste are dead in every text field in the app. A minimal menu carrying Edit is installed at
  `whenReady`, before the renderer's list arrives.
- Reload is dropped and zoom is kept, and they are not alike: zoom is a preference (`shot.mjs`
  already refuses to photograph a zoomed window), a reload throws away the open thread, the loaded
  album and an unsent message with no warning and no undo.
- `appMenu.test.ts`, 9 tests. **Red-first:** devtools shipped → 1 red; no Edit menu → 2 red; an
  empty accelerator instead of none → 2 red; the package name in the menu bar → 1 red.

**Proven end to end, and stopping exactly where the evidence stops.** Clicking *Go → Photos* and
*Go → Search…* through `System Events` asked `shell.route('photos')` and `openPalette()` — recorded
by wrapping the two methods and reading what they were **asked** for. The routes did not *take*,
because the repudiated link forces the pairing screen, and that is stated rather than papered over:
the control is that `shell.route('files')` called **directly** is equally a no-op right now.

**Two things the menu reading does not show**, in the evidence file rather than left to be inferred:
the app menu still reads `Electron` because on macOS that title comes from the bundle's
`CFBundleName` — read from the plist, `Electron`, against `productName: Sidekick` in
`electron-builder.yml` — and **no packaged build was made, so the packaged title is unread**; and
View still lists the developer items because this is a development run, with the packaged branch
covered by a test and read from no packaged build.

### Defect 127 — nine Activity rows put their own visible text under the pointer

The sweep counted **203** `title` attributes. The useful number was not the total: nine
`activity-detail` tooltips carried a string **identical to the element's own text**, 9 of 9. The
intent was right — the class is `text-overflow: ellipsis`, so a clipped detail needs somewhere to
reveal the rest — but it was set on every row, including the ones that fit. A tooltip that repeats
what is on screen teaches a person that tooltips here say nothing, which costs the ones that do.

`renderer/overflowTitle.ts` sets it only where the layout clipped, measured after the rows are in
the document, one pass over the drawn rows so the layout flushes once. `overflowTitle.test.ts`, 4
tests. **Red-first:** set unconditionally → 3 red; a tie counted as clipped → 1 red; never cleared,
so a tooltip outlives the clipping that earned it → 1 red.

Beside it, `activity-time` carried `new Date(at).toString()` —
`Sun Sep 20 2026 17:10:22 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)`, a runtime's debug representation with
the timezone spelled twice, under the pointer on nine rows. `activityExactWhen` writes it for a
person. Same rule as a package id: a machine string may be a handle and may not be the thing
somebody reads.

**The double had to be fixed first, and that is the finding under the finding.** `FakeElement.title`
was a plain property while `getAttribute`/`removeAttribute` used the attribute map — two stores for
one thing, which the DOM keeps in sync. So a test asserting `getAttribute('title') === null` passed
for **every** implementation, including one that set a tooltip on every row: the third test variety
in `CLAUDE.md`, the test calling the right function at a layer where the defect cannot show. The
first mutation run proved it — *set unconditionally* left the suite green. `title` is reflected
through the attribute map now, and the same mutation goes red on three tests.

### Defect 128 — the New-conversation panel was a modal surface that said nothing

The sweep read it as `{ role: null, modal: null, label: null }` beside the palette's
`{ role: 'dialog', modal: 'true', label: 'Command palette' }`. One app, two modal surfaces, one
done properly and one done by un-hiding a div — and nothing in the build could tell them apart.

Three things it owed: it says what it is (without `role="dialog"` a screen reader announces fields
appearing from nowhere, with the pane behind them still in the reading order); **Escape closes it**
(every other dismissable surface in this app does, so a person who has learned that will press it
here and have nothing happen); and **focus goes back where it came from** (cancelling left focus on
a button inside a `hidden` subtree, which drops it to the document, so the next Tab restarts at the
top of the window).

`smsView.test.ts` +3. **Red-first:** any key dismisses → 1 red; focus not restored → 2 red; a closed
panel still acting on Escape → 1 red. The `role`, `aria-modal` and `aria-labelledby` are attributes
on static markup and are asserted by the **sweep against the real page** — a unit test asserting
them would be asserting its own fixture.

### Tooltips: what was NOT changed, and why

194 `title` attributes remain — 128 Apps tiles carrying a package id, 50 call rows naming what the
row does, the Camera nav row's explanation, 9 absolute times. They stay native, and that is a
recorded departure rather than an oversight: **the handoff specifies 18 components and none of them
is a tooltip**, so building one would be inventing design rather than matching it. A native tooltip
is OS-drawn, ignores the theme, waits about a second and is invisible to keyboard and touch — all
true, all worth fixing, and all a decision for the designer's hour rather than for this pass.

### 900 tests, from 869 at the start of the sitting. All twelve commit guards exit 0.

## Sidekick Batch 6c — the sweep re-run on a live link, and what it found about itself — 2026-09-20

The phone was re-paired by the owner. Confirmed before anything was read: `phase=connected`,
`paired=true`, `Samsung SM-S938B`, **10 ms**, 11 capabilities, and **13 of 13 routes open** — the
twelve sidebar rows plus pairing, each asserted by routing to it and reading back the `data-screen`
of the section that is actually visible.

### Defect 127, second instance — found by a column, not by looking

The sweep's tooltip reading was changed from a total to a **breakdown by kind with a
`duplicatesVisibleText` column**, and it immediately named a second instance of a defect fixed
earlier the same day: Overview's `recent-when`, **2 of 4** rows with a tooltip repeating the text
under the pointer. The row draws `activityClock` and its tooltip was `activityWhen` — and **past an
hour `activityWhen` returns `activityClock`**, so a row older than an hour repeated itself and a
newer one did not.

**194 would never have shown it.** Nine duplicates inside two hundred tooltips is invisible in a
total, and the two on Overview are invisible even in the nine. The column is the denominator rule
applied to a count that already had one: a total needs to be *of the right thing*.

`titleIfItAdds` in `renderer/overflowTitle.ts`, beside `titleWhenClipped` — and they are genuinely
different rules rather than one with a flag. For a clipped element a title equal to its text is
exactly right, because the text is *visually* cut and `textContent` still holds all of it; here
nothing is clipped and the two strings are simply the same. 5 tests. **Red-first:** set
unconditionally → 4 red; an untrimmed comparison → 1 red.

### Three answers to one question, and the second one was the dangerous shape

The focus-ring sweep gave **three** different readings of an app that did not change:

| Reading | Stable across runs? | What it actually was |
|---|---|---|
| `825 / 824 / 553` of 825 | **no** | the forced pseudo-state's style recalc lands on the renderer's own schedule; `getComputedStyle` could resolve against the pre-recalc style |
| `557 of 829`, twice | **yes** | Photos streams thumbnails in and **replaces** its elements. The node count is unchanged — so a settle predicate on the count is satisfied — while every forced state now sits on a node no longer in the document |
| **`835 of 835`**, three consecutive runs | **yes** | force and read as one **atomic pair**, repeated until two consecutive pairs agree |

**The middle row is the one to carry forward: a stable wrong answer.** Everything this repo has
written about flaky instruments is about readings that *vary*; the fix for those is a settle
predicate. This one settled perfectly, repeated exactly, and reported 272 photo tiles as having no
focus ring — which is precisely the shape a pane that styles its own controls would produce, and
would have been written up as a real defect in a pane that does not have one.

What separated them was **not** deciding which run to trust. It was asking what each was measuring:
one read a settled pane, the other read dead nodes. The stimulus is now re-applied immediately
before every sample, so the nodes carrying the state are the nodes being read.

**And a fourth attempt is recorded because it fails in a way nobody would predict.** The obvious
fix for a late style recalc is two `requestAnimationFrame`s before reading. **rAF does not fire in
an occluded window** — Electron behind another window never ran the callback and the sweep hung
with no output at all. An instrument that works only while somebody is looking at the app is not an
instrument, and the settle lives in a `setTimeout` loop for that reason.

### Two more instrument faults fixed in `probe.mjs` on the way

- **`DOM.getDocument` with `depth: -1` never answered** on a populated page: it serialises the
  whole tree. It was first diagnosed as stale per-target domain state on the strength of
  *"restarting the app fixed it"* — **a correlation, not a mechanism**: a freshly restarted app has
  a small tree until its content arrives, so the restart was shrinking the dump rather than
  resetting anything. `depth: 0` is the fix; nothing here needs a serialised tree.
- **A 30-second timeout on every CDP command**, because a promise that never settles is the worst
  failure an instrument can have: the process hangs and node prints `Detected unsettled top-level
  await` at a line number in the *caller*. It is what named `DOM.getDocument` as the culprit.
- `CSS.forcePseudoState` on a node that has gone is tolerated and **counted** — `forced` against
  `matched`, with `stopped: 'tree moved'` — rather than throwing, because a live app redrawing is
  not an instrument failure and a partial force must not read as a complete one.

### The green artifact

`docs/evidence/sidekick-batch6/shell-parity-sweep-GREEN.txt`, with the three-readings table at its
head so the number cannot be quoted without it. **835 of 835** controls ringed across twelve routes,
control **0 of 835** outlined at rest; **0** surfaces still blurred under reduced transparency and
**0** still transitioning under reduced motion, against **5** translucent at rest; palette and
New-conversation both labelled `role=dialog`; toast `role=status` / `aria-live=polite`.

905 tests, from 900. Typecheck clean, `probe.test.mjs` 24/24, all twelve commit guards exit 0.
**Nothing in this batch is within reach of pairing, identity, TLS, certificates or the trust
store** — the changed files are two renderer rules, one pane, two tests and two instruments.

## Sidekick Batch 6d — Files' and Photos' five uncaptured states, and what capturing them found

Inventory §5 row 4: *Sending*, *no folders* and *couldn't open* on Files, *partial* and *permission*
on Photos, none re-captured after the surface change. All five now exist in
`docs/evidence/sidekick-batch6/`.

### The states are driven through the production path, not painted

`scripts/files-photos-states.mjs` replaces each view's **bridge** — the async functions it calls —
and then calls the view's own public `refresh()`. The code that runs is the real failure path, the
same one the pane takes when the phone actually refuses. *Sending* is driven through `sendFiles()`
with a bridge that stays **in flight**, so the pane sits in the state a transfer occupies rather
than in a rendering of what that state would look like.

**TypeScript's `private` is erased at runtime**, so setting `view.failure` and calling `render()`
was available and is deliberately ruled out: it photographs a field, not a state. The one place the
script does write a private field is the *cleanup* — `lastPush` is not cleared by `refresh()`, so
without it the pane would be left showing a sentence about a transfer that never happened.

### Three faults in the script, and the second one poisoned the next run

| | What happened |
|---|---|
| 1 | `--prep` with a top-level `await` is a syntax error outside an async function. The prep without one worked, so only the awaiting captures failed |
| 2 | **A failed shot exited the process before the restore, leaving the app holding an invented permission refusal.** The *next* run's partial-notice capture then could not draw — a failure outranks a partial notice — and refused with `--prep did not land`, for a reason with nothing to do with the prep |
| 3 | *Sending* ran **after** a capture that faked `fs.roots` to empty, so `selectedRoot` was null, `sendFiles` returned immediately, and the prep did nothing while reporting nothing |

The second is the one worth the entry. A probe that edits the thing it measures is a known fault;
one that edits it *for the next run* is worse, because by then nothing connects the symptom to the
cause. `restoreLive()` is called **before** the run as well as after it, and the shots are wrapped
so the restore happens on a failure too. The control is at both ends: **152 albums before, 152
after**.

### Defect-shaped finding: seven state vocabularies, not one

`docs/design-departures.md`'s Batch 4a section is headed **"One vocabulary for states"**. One
private vocabulary was deleted — Notifications' — and that sentence is true. **Six survive**,
counted in `styles.css`: `files-state*` (16 rules), `apps-banner*` (6), `photos-banner*` (5),
`activity-state*` (4), `files-banner*` (2), `call-state` (1).

They are not near-duplicates. Measured as computed style on the same fact, component 11's `error`
is transparent, centred, `0px` radius, `24px` padding, 600/15px in `#F2F3F5`; Files' M4 card is
`rgba(255,92,92,.14)`, left-aligned, `14px` radius, `14px` padding, 500/13px in `#FF5C5C`.

**Two of the five captures show both at once**, which is what turns this from a code observation
into a visible defect: `files-couldnt-open` has the red left-aligned card in one column and a
centred `state-block` in the other; `photos-permission` has the amber bar above the same centred
block. One pane, one screenshot, two languages for *there is nothing here*.

**Not converted in this batch, and the reason is a boundary rather than a budget.** Component 11's
default is specified *centred in a pane-sized region*; all six of these live in a narrow column or
a full-width bar. `stateBlock` has a `compact` variant for that case and **`compact` has no Figma
frame**, so choosing it — and choosing which treatment wins in a column — is inventing design
rather than matching it. D67 records the scope: six vocabularies, 34 CSS rules, four panes.

### Captures

| File | State | Frame |
|---|---|---|
| `photos-partial-SYNTHETIC-1440x920.png` | thumbnails only | `31:3704` |
| `photos-permission-SYNTHETIC-1440x920.png` | permission refused | `31:3956` |
| `files-sending-SYNTHETIC-1440x920.png` | a transfer in flight | `31:3175` |
| `files-no-folders-SYNTHETIC-1440x920.png` | nothing shared | `31:2819` |
| `files-couldnt-open-SYNTHETIC-1440x920.png` | `TARGET_STALE`, with Try again | `31:2985` |

All five are **SYNTHETIC** and say so in the filename. The status island and the sidebar read

## Sidekick Batch 7 — D67 approved: one state system, two layouts — 2026-09-21

The owner approved the decision D67 recorded. Two layouts, a fixed tone map, no third card style.
**The component design is unified; the exact Figma pixel comparison remains pending** — the MCP is
still disconnected, so nothing here is Figma-exact and no row says it is.

### The scope was five, not six — and that correction is the first finding

D67 counted six pane-private vocabularies. `call-state` is **not a state card**: it is a call row's
status *text* (`Ringing · WhatsApp`), one CSS rule setting a font size and a colour. The count had
matched a **name pattern** rather than a thing — the lookalike rule, in a measurement written to
enforce a design rule. The real scope:

| Vocabulary | Rules | Layout it took |
|---|---|---|
| `files-state*` | 16 | Compact |
| `apps-banner*` | 6 | Compact |
| `photos-banner*` | 5 | Compact |
| `activity-state*` | 4 | **Full** |
| `files-banner*` | 2 | Compact |

**32 rules, 120 lines of CSS deleted.** Plus a second hand-built copy of the Files card in
`renderTable`, for a directory that would not open — two copies of one vocabulary inside one pane,
which is how six accumulated across an app.

### Three changes that are not merely a re-skin

- **`tone` and `icon` are gone from `FilesPaneView` and `ActivityPaneView`.** One `kind` decides
  the tone, the glyph, the headline's verb and whether an action exists. Files' M2/M4 still differ
  in the four independent ways §3 of the files proposal requires — now *by construction*, so a pane
  cannot restyle a state into agreeing with another one.
- **Activity's A2 is red, not amber** (D70). The approved map puts an actual operation failure in
  red. What amber was carrying — nothing is lost on the phone — is in the body, in words, where it
  does not depend on anybody reading a hue.
- **`partial` is an eighth kind** (D68). *The feature works, and not all of it* is not one of the
  others wearing another name, and the map puts it in amber.

### Verified where it is drawn, not where it is defined

`scripts/state-system-verify.mjs`: **93 state blocks**, twelve routes × two themes × two sizes,
each pane driven into its states through its own public path. Thirteen readings, all OK:

| | |
|---|---|
| exactly two layouts | no block carries a class outside `state-block` / `state-block compact` |
| the tone map | every drawn block matches, and **no lime anywhere** |
| one action maximum | and a `wall` has none |
| keyboard | every action is a real, tabbable, `type="button"` `<button>` — so Enter and Space work with no code |
| layout | no action clipped, no block overflowing, none running off the window, at 1440 × 920 **and** 1100 × 700 |
| shape | one badge and one headline each |
| **coverage** | each migrated pane **drew** the states it was migrated for |

The migrated panes drew: **files** `error` compact, **photos** `permission` + `partial` compact,
**apps** `permission` + `partial` compact, **activity** `error` + `empty` **full**.

### Four instrument faults, and the coverage check found two of them

| | What it reported | What it was |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | every route drawing an `empty` block, Photos drawing `error` | the query read `document.querySelectorAll('.state-block')` — **every hidden pane's blocks, on every route**. `CLAUDE.md`'s own rule, broken in the file written to enforce a design rule: narrow the selector until it can only be the thing |
| 2 | `activity/error` never drawn | `failRequest` is a key on the real bridge and **is not honoured by it** — it belongs to the test double. The driver did nothing while reporting nothing |
| 3 | `photos/permission` never drawn | `shell.onRoute` starts its own `refresh()`; at 220 ms the driver's refusal was installed and rendered, then the route's in-flight fetch resolved over it with `failure = null`. Two callers of one fetch, resolved by order |
| 4 | every later `shot.mjs` refusing with *"the window is zoomed"* | `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` is **per-target**, so the override outlived the session and a clear from a later one did not undo it. An instrument that quietly breaks the next instrument |

**The coverage check is why 2 and 3 were found at all.** Without it the sweep would have reported
thirteen green readings over a run in which two of the four migrated panes never drew a state — a
pass that certifies the panes it did not measure. It names the states each pane must have drawn and
fails when one is missing, which is the denominator rule applied to a *set* rather than a count.
Fault 4 now fails the sweep loudly with the instruction (restart the app) rather than being left to
be rediscovered.

### Real function, after the migration

`scripts/state-real-function.mjs`, on the live phone: Files **2 entries**, Photos **152 albums**,
Apps **128 tiles**, Activity **9 rows**, and **no state card drawn on any of them** — the panes work
and say nothing about themselves, which is the state the component is supposed to leave them in.

## Motion pass close-out — the fix that shipped without taking, and two instruments that called it wrong — 2026-09-21

The motion and brand pass (`baf5664` … `d016bb6`) was finished in this sitting rather than extended.
Nothing new was designed. What it produced is one product defect, two instrument defects, a
fifteenth commit hook, and a set of evidence re-taken end to end against the committed tree — the
mid-pass captures were replaced rather than kept beside the new ones, so no measurement in
`docs/evidence/motion-2026-09-21/` appears twice with two values.

**Conditions, stated because they changed between the mid-pass captures and these.** A phone **was**
linked for every reading here — `Samsung SM-S938B`, `link: connected`, on the third line of each
sweep — where the mid-pass runs were disconnected. That is a coverage difference, not a cosmetic
one: notification rows, call rows and the 128 app tiles only exist with a phone on the other end.

### Where the sitting started, and what "the defect check" turned out to be

The brief named a `defects: 1` result. Nothing in this repo emits that string, and every
defect-related check was green when the sitting opened: `check-defects.sh` (112 rows), all thirteen
hooks, `npm test` at 909, the phone suite `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`. What **was** red was found by running
the one set of suites nothing runs — see defect 131 — and the product defect underneath the brand
work was found by measuring the lockup rather than reading its stylesheet. Both are recorded below.
The original string is unreproduced and is recorded as unreproduced.

### Defect 129 — `.brand-mark` was declared twice and the browser kept the losing rule

| | |
|---|---|
| read | `getComputedStyle(.brand-mark)` in the running app |
| before | `width: 65px`, `object-position: 0% 50%` |
| after | `width: 57px`, `object-position: 50% 50%` |

The stage is 69px and the artwork 57px, so the fix's own comment specifies 6px of ground either
side. What was drawn was **2px left and 10px right**, with the lime half of the halo visible in the
gap. Located in the pixels rather than derived from the CSS, by matching the artwork's own eye
pixels against each capture:

```
before artwork starts 2px into the stage, spans 2..59 of 69 -> bare stage 2px left / 10px right
after  artwork starts 6px into the stage, spans 6..63 of 69 -> bare stage 6px left / 6px right
   [control: 453 of 598 eye pixels matched at the best offset, in both]
```

Both crops are the same frame with the halo's breath pinned to its rest keyframe, so they differ by
the geometry and not by when the shutter fell. `brand-mark-before-dark.png` /
`brand-mark-after-dark.png`. The "before" is reproduced by setting the two losing values inline and
the capture is **gated** on `getComputedStyle` returning exactly the pre-fix pair; the inline styles
are removed afterwards and the restoration asserted.

**The guard that should have caught it passed.** `stylesheets.test.ts` has had a rule against one
selector declared twice in one sheet since the pre-redesign notification block, and its
discriminator is **distance** — far apart is dead, adjacent is a deliberate override you can read in
one screen. Here the new rule was inserted **above** the old one, six lines away, and proximity was
what hid it: the pair reads as a single commented block. A distance is a claim about two things and
either can move. The new assertion has no distance in it — two top-level blocks with one selector in
one sheet may not set one property to two values — and it goes red on the verbatim pair, naming
`width`, `object-position` and both line numbers, while the distance rule stays silent.

### Defect 130 — the sweep called two product states defects

**(a) The mid-FLIP exclusion covered one of the mechanism's two marks.** `overview.ts` adds
`is-arriving` to every arriving row and an inline `transition: none` **only when the row moved**,
clearing both in one `afterNextPaint`. `.recent-row.is-arriving` carries `transition: none` in
`shell.css`. The sweep read the inline half only, so a row that arrived without moving computed
`transition-property: none` and was reported as `snapping: recent-row (12)` — the exact sentence the
exclusion exists to prevent, on the other half of the same mechanism.

Proven at its own layer, because a row arriving with `dy === 0` cannot be demanded: three real
`.recent-row` buttons were given the class with no inline style.

```
constructed: {"rows":4,"marked":3,"inlineOnMarked":["(none)","(none)","(none)"],"computed":["none","none","none"]}
exclusion WITHOUT the is-arriving branch: {"snapped":3,"excluded":0}
exclusion WITH    the is-arriving branch: {"snapped":0,"excluded":3}
page restored, rows still marked: 0
```

A later run met the state in the wild and the fixed exclusion named both marks:
`recent-row/inline (36), recent-row/is-arriving (12)`.

**(b) A settle predicate over three clocks that named two.** `press-down` forces `:active` and
settles when `scaled` and `visible` agree across two force-and-read pairs. It never compared how
many nodes the force **reached** against how many the reader **scored**. Every unreached node
reports its at-rest `--dur-release` 0.16s, which is indistinguishable from a button that does not
shorten its press. The run printed:

```
569 of 697 at 0.1s; others: apps-tile=0.16s …  [forced=573]
```

569 + 128 = 697, and 697 − 573 = 124. Two numbers that must be equal for the reading to exist, side
by side, differing, with the verdict computed from the other one — and the finding written from it
was *"128 apps tiles snap their press"*. `forced === matched` is in the predicate now and a mismatch
is a **NO READING**. Red against the verbatim case by narrowing the force selector by `.apps-tile`:

```
NO READING pressing shortens the transition to --dur-press — the force reached 593 nodes and the
reader matched 721 — the 128 it did not reach report their AT-REST duration, which is
indistinguishable from a button that does not shorten its press
```

**And the sweep now prints its theme and its link state.** A dark run and a light run came back
**byte-identical** — correctly, since no rule in the sweep is about colour — so the two evidence
files could not be told apart and neither said which theme it was taken in. Two indistinguishable
files are one reading and a claim.

### Defect 131 — the fixture suites nothing runs, two of them red

Twenty suites under `scripts/`, about two seconds, run by no hook.
`orphan-tests-none.sh` says so in its own header: *"scripts/\*.test.mjs are counted and reported,
not checked"*.

- **`check-renderer-scripts.test.mjs`** asserted that `index.html` loads `discHue.js` and the scan
  sees it. `discHue.ts` was deleted with its last caller — correctly; the Sidekick system has no
  per-person hue, and `calls.ts` records why. **The guard it belongs to kept passing**, because its
  scope comes from `index.html` and a file no longer listed there is not in scope. The replacement
  control is structural: every name the scan returns must resolve to a real `src/shared/*.ts`. It
  cannot rot on a deletion, and it goes red on the case that matters — index.html and the tree
  disagreeing, which in the browser is a 404 on a `<script>` nobody sees fail. Shown red two ways:
  a deleted file still referenced, and every shared `<script>` stripped (the floor).
- **`adb-count.test.sh`** exports `CONNECTSUITE_ADB` to point at a fake adb. `target-device.sh`
  honours it; `adb-pinned.sh` execed a literal `adb`. So the pin was fakeable and the command was
  not, and the two *must READ* fixtures could only pass with an SM-S938B on the cable — red on any
  machine without one. Its FAIL branch then died under `set -u` on `'$want…'`, because bash takes
  the ellipsis bytes as part of the name, so the first failure it ever reported was a crash with no
  diagnosis. Both fixed; `adb-pinned.sh` resolves `${CONNECTSUITE_ADB:-adb}`, and the refusal
  branches are unchanged (verified against an empty fake bus and against the real one).

The enforcement point is `scripts/check-script-fixtures.mjs` and
`scripts/hooks/script-fixtures-green.sh`, the **fifteenth** hook on this repo's pre-commit path. It
runs rather than reading an artifact, because two seconds is affordable and there is no artifact; it
refuses on a discovery below its floor, because "all fixtures green" over nothing found is the
reading this directory exists to prevent; and it prints the failing suite's **named lines** rather
than a stack tail.

Its own suite is one of the twenty, and its last test asserts the floor sits below the real count —
which recursed until it was killed. The fix is not to exempt this file from discovery: the one suite
the guard refuses to run would be the one guarding the guard, which is the gap it was written to
close, one level in. Discovery is separable from running (`--list`), and every suite stays in scope.

Red-first against the historical case: restoring the `discHue` anchor makes the hook **deny** and
name the assertion.

### The brand lockup, measured

`scripts/brand-lockup-probe.mjs` (the resolved cascade) and `scripts/brand-pixels.py` (the pixels,
classified by the artwork's **own alpha channel** — a brightness threshold cannot separate a dark
wing from the dark ground behind it, which is the whole problem). Both themes, all PASS.

The halo breathes 0.5 → 0.72 over 6s, so the ground is a moving number; the animation is pinned at
each keyframe extreme and the reading is a band.

| dark | wings | ground | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| bare sidebar, no stage | `L=0.0093` | `rgb(14,14,14)` | **1.09:1** |
| on the stage, rest | `L=0.0093` | `L=0.0195` | **1.17:1** |
| on the stage, peak | `L=0.0093` | `L=0.0253` | **1.27:1** |

**That is a very small ratio change and no part of this is a contrast win.** The mask is near-black
by design and lifting a ground *towards* it reduces the difference; 3:1 would need an
`rgb(99,99,99)` slab. **What makes the lockup readable is the stage's edge and the clipped halo
behind the mark — a shape against a gradient.** The ratio is published only so nobody later reads
the screenshot as a number it did not earn.

The control is the **eyes**, in the same frame: **10.24:1** at rest, **9.48:1** at peak. They were
bright all along and are not what changed. A run where the wings and eyes converge is an alignment
wrong for both classes — which is how the first version of this instrument was caught, reporting
**1.28:1** for the eyes because `clip.scale` multiplies on top of the device pixel ratio and returns
a **4x** image that a 2x asset cannot be indexed into.

In **light** the mask never needed help and the stage slightly *lowers* its ratio, which is the
expected direction and is the evidence that light is not over-glowed: **16.55:1** bare, **14.22:1**
and **14.01:1** on the stage. The halo's whole contribution there is a channel spread of 5–6 over
the sidebar's own 3.

**The sidebar takes no tint.** Sampled in the left gutter — 14px of padding every row shares, which
no text enters — beside the lockup and far below it:

| | beside the stage | far below | difference | the stage itself |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dark | `rgb(14,14,14)` | `rgb(14,14,14)` | **0** | `rgb(30,39,37)`, spread 9–13 |
| light | `rgb(249,249,252)` | `rgb(249,249,252)` | **0** | `rgb(229,233,234)`, spread 5–6 |

The stage's spread is the control: something must be tinted eight pixels away or the reading means
nothing. The first version of this band sat to the *right* of the stage and caught the **wordmark** —
`rgb(33,33,34)` against `rgb(14,14,14)`, all three channels moving together. Light text is not a tint.

And from the cascade, both themes: the halo is a **child of the stage** with `overflow: hidden` and
`isolation: isolate`, overflowing by **31px each side** so the clip is load-bearing; the stage is a
`<span>`, no role, `tabIndex -1`, not focusable, `cursor: auto` against the control that a real nav
row in the same sidebar reads `cursor: pointer`; the **wordmark is static** (`animation: none`,
`transform: none`); the breath is `brand-breathe 6s` at rest and **`none`** under `reduce`, with the
control that the emulation moved the halo's animation count 1 → 0; and under `reduce` the halo sits
at **`opacity: 0.5`**, its designed rest value, with no animation attached — it is declared *inside*
`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so there is nothing for the global kill to freeze.

That last row needed its own correction: `getAnimations()` returns CSSAnimation **and**
CSSTransition, and under the emulation the page reports **191 transitions of 0.01ms** — `tokens.css`'s
own reduced-motion kill, created *by* applying the media change. Counted together they read as "191
ambient animations survived reduced motion", the exact reverse. Ambient motion is a keyframe
animation, and that is what the row counts: **1 (`brand-breathe`) → 0**.

### Verification, as run

```
desktop typecheck                tsc --noEmit + tsconfig.test.json         clean
desktop npm test                 911 tests, 911 pass, 0 fail
phone ./gradlew test             BUILD SUCCESSFUL — 450 tests, 0 failures
                                 (core 126, sync-module 212, input-module 52,
                                  mirror-module 49, app 11. A naive sum over the XML
                                  reads 900: debug and release run the same 450 twice)
scripts/check-script-fixtures    20 of 20 fixture suites green (floor 12)
motion-sweep, dark               13 pass, 0 fail, 0 NO READING, 12 of 12 routes
motion-sweep, light              13 pass, 0 fail, 0 NO READING, 12 of 12 routes
check-motion-tokens              74 motion declarations, 20 tokens, no raw literals
brand-lockup-probe, dark/light   ALL READINGS OK
shell-parity-sweep               ALL READINGS OK — 853 of 853 focus rings, 0 at rest
state-system-verify              ALL READINGS OK
card-visibility-sweep            19 cards: 18 visible at rest, 1 reachable, 0 stranded
check-defects                    115 numbered rows, all with records
fifteen pre-commit hooks         all allow
```

Press: **8604 of 8604** enabled buttons, 48 excluded mid-FLIP and named by their mark. Reduced
motion: 168 transforms → 0, 4 keyframe animations → 0, each against its own before-column control.
Reduced transparency: 4 blurred surfaces → 0, and independently in the shell sweep, 5 translucent at
rest with none still blurred or transitioning under `reduce`. Disabled: **1 disabled control on
screen, 0 carrying a press** — a real reading on a denominator of 1.

### What this does not cover

- **No Figma render, and the Figma MCP is not connected on this account.** No value in this pass has
  been compared against a Figma file. Everything is built to the handoff and to the two design
  references in `docs/sidekick-motion-system.md` §0; nothing here is a Figma comparison, and the
  wording in the docs says so rather than implying a comparison that did not happen.
- **Both final sweeps were taken with the window occluded**, which each declares on its own second
  line. That is the better condition rather than a compromise: occlusion stalls `requestAnimationFrame`,
  so the FLIP never clears its marks and the run exercises the mid-FLIP exclusion instead of skipping
  past it. `Page.bringToFront` does not raise an Electron window another application covers, and on
  this machine System Events reports `windows=0` for the process while CDP screenshots it happily.
- **`prefers-contrast: more` is handled nowhere** and is not measured. A colour-and-border question.
- **`.toast` uses `@keyframes`** and restarts rather than retargets. Accepted while toasts do not stack.
- **The `defects: 1` result the brief named was never reproduced.** Every defect-related check was
  green at the start of the sitting and is green now; what was red was found by other means.

## Android UI pass — Slice 1: the design foundation and the Devices overview (2026-09-22)

The brief is `~/Downloads/claude-code-android-full-detailed-prompt.md`; the references are
`Sidekick android ui/*.png`. Screen 01 (Devices overview) is the anchor screen. Evidence:
`docs/evidence/phase-7-android-slice-1/`.

**Where the tokens came from, and why it is not a second reading of the design.** The palette is
ported digit-for-digit from `desktop/src/renderer/tokens.css` — `--canvas #0a0a0a`, `--card
#161616`, `--card-raised #1c1c1c`, `--accent #c6ff33`, `--text-primary #f2f3f5`, `--text-body
#9a9ca8`, `--hairline rgba(255,255,255,.08)`, `--radius-panel 14`, `--warning #ffb547`,
`--destructive #ff5c5c`, plus the `--dur-*`/`--ease-*` scale. Two values are `DERIVED` and say so in
`SidekickColors.kt`: `accentPressed` (the Mac's `--accent-hover` *lightens*, which is wrong for a
finger) and `textDisabled`.

**The change that made any of it visible.** `ConnectSuiteTheme` had `dynamicColor = true`, so on
Android 12+ the OEM wallpaper supplied the palette and the schemes declared in that file had never
once been drawn. Also `isSystemInDarkTheme()`, and `values/themes.xml` inheriting
`Theme.Material.Light.NoActionBar` — a white launch window in front of a `#0A0A0A` app.

### What was measured

| # | Reading | Control | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Nav: the lit tab, by pixel | the other four tabs in the same reading | see below |
| 2 | Folders keeps **Transfers** lit | same probe, same run | PASS |
| 3 | Mac management lights **nothing** | same probe; a `Devices`-lit reading immediately before | PASS |
| 4 | `EXTRA_OPEN_TAB` deep link → Mirror | parked on Devices first, so a pass cannot be "already there" | PASS |
| 5 | Phone unit suites | — | **469 tests, 0 failures**, artifacts 0-1 s old, gradle exit 0 |

**`selected` in a uiautomator dump is not the state of a Compose tab.** The first version of the nav
probe read the XML's `selected` attribute and returned `selected="false"` for all five cells —
*including the one that was visibly lime*. Compose's tab-selection semantics do not reach that
attribute. A probe that reads `false` for the known positive has no reading, so the discriminator
moved to the thing the state actually is: the brightest pixel inside each label's bounds.
`(198,255,51)` is exactly `#C6FF33`; muted is `(154,156,168)` = `#9A9CA8`. **The probe prints the
distance for all five tabs on every row**, so a run where nothing separates says so instead of
naming whichever was marginally closest.

`selectable` replaced `clickable` on the nav cells anyway — not for the probe, which does not use
it, but because the selected state existed *only* as a colour, which is precisely what a screen
reader cannot see.

**Two instrument faults, both caught before they were written down as findings:**

- The first `am start` of a nav run resumed the task **where the previous run left it** — Mac
  management, where no tab is lit — and the probe dutifully reported "0 tabs lit" against an
  expectation of `Devices`. The instrument was right and the premise was stale. Every later run
  establishes the starting state with a tap first.
- The deep-link check used `--es open_tab mirror` and failed. The key is
  `MirrorNotifications.EXTRA_OPEN_TAB = "com.chetan.connectsuite.OPEN_TAB"`. That is
  `CLAUDE.md`'s *a pass criterion naming a string the code does not write* — the string was typed
  from memory; re-run against the constant, it passes.

**And one during the build itself, worth the line because the output looked like progress.** A BSD
`sed` with `\b` silently did nothing, and the recompile's error list — clipped by `tail -40` —
appeared to shrink from 18 to 15. Two instrument faults stacked: a substitution that never ran, and
a bound the instrument imposed and did not report. `grep -c` on the file showed 18 occurrences
untouched.

### What the screen does **not** draw, and why

- **Latency.** References 01 and 10 both show `8 ms`. The phone cannot honestly produce it: RTT is
  measured on the Mac's HUD, and while `MessageType.PING`/`PONG` exist in the contract, nothing on
  this side times them. The chip carries the connected Mac's **address**, which is real
  (`TrustedDeviceEntity.lastAddress`). Wiring a phone-side RTT is a protocol-adjacent change and was
  not made under a UI brief.
- **"See all" on Quick actions and Recent activity.** Both appear in reference 01 and neither has a
  destination — Activity is not a screen on the phone, and Recent activity spans three sources, so
  pointing it at Transfers would be true of a third of it. Omitted rather than drawn as a link that
  goes nowhere.
- **"Open on Mac"** (reference 01's third hero button) is not an action this app has. The slot is
  `Device info`, which reaches Mac management — reference 10's own second button.
- **Battery and Storage cards** (reference 10) are not built. Both are locally available and neither
  is speculative; they belong to whichever slice builds reference 10's variant.

**Recent activity invents nothing.** There is no activity log on the phone. `RecentActivity.of` is a
projection over three stores that already exist: transfer history (`updatedAtMillis`), mirrored
notifications (`postedAtMillis`), and the clipboard's own timestamps — memory-only by design, which
the empty state says out loud rather than leaving the reader to discover.

Red-first, each mutation run with `--rerun-tasks` and a 0 s-old results directory:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `sortedByDescending` → `sortedBy` (the Overview *five oldest* defect, verbatim) | **3 red** |
| `take(limit)` moved before the sort | **1 red** |
| `clip.lastSentAtMs > 0L` → `>= 0L` (a 1970 row) | **4 red** |
| restored | green, exit 0 |

### The screenshots, and what each may be quoted for

- `devices-real-unpaired.png` — **the real app**, real state, no Mac paired. This is the functional
  evidence.
- `devices-harness-connected.png` — the **production** `DevicesSection` and theme, on the device, at
  real density, with a constructed state: `DesignPreviewActivity`, debug source set only. The
  connected state is unobservable on an emulator (the Mac dials *out* to the phone, and pairing needs
  a QR through a camera that does not exist). **It proves layout, palette, type, spacing and insets.
  It proves nothing about wiring** — no ViewModel is attached and every callback is a no-op.

### Fixed after the first run on hardware, not before it

1. **The status-bar inset was applied twice** — Scaffold's default `contentWindowInsets` is
   `systemBars` and with no top app bar it hands that straight to content, on top of each section's
   own `statusBarsPadding()`. ~74 dp of empty canvas above the brand lockup.
2. **Quick-action tiles were as tall as their own copy**, so the row had a ragged bottom edge.
   `IntrinsicSize.Min` + `fillMaxHeight`.
3. **The hero bloom washed two thirds of the card olive** at `alpha 0.55, radius 900`. Now `0.20` at
   `620`, and the reference's card is mostly `#161616` with light entering a corner.
4. **The trailing chevron sat beside the label**, mid-button, with a hand's width of empty pill past
   it. It is `align(CenterEnd)` with the label optically centred.
5. **The phone glyph read as an empty card** when flat. One 3 dp earpiece slit.

### Open

- `Icons.Filled`/`Default` still appear outside the Devices screen; the one-weight sweep finishes as
  each screen is built.
- Grain over the hero bloom is not implemented (needs a tiling noise bitmap or an AGSL shader).
- Recent activity uses squircle badges (reference 10); reference 01 draws circles. One vocabulary
  across the app was preferred; it is a one-line change if the other is wanted.
- **Motion has not been touched.** `find-animation-opportunities` and `improve-animations` come after
  the static layouts are confirmed; `review-animations` needs the user's own invocation.

## Android UI pass — Slice 2: Connect a Mac (2026-09-22)

References `02`-`09`. Evidence: `docs/evidence/phase-7-android-slice-2/`.
Components are Slice 1's; nothing here hand-rolls a card, a button or a state block.

### The finding that shaped the whole slice

**`completePairing` does not connect.** It writes the trust row, arms a token for
`Link.PAIR_TOKEN_TTL_MS`, advertises the pair intent — and returns. The Mac then dials in
(locked decision #2: Android binds, the Mac connects out). So the phone, after a scan,
**listens**. It never searches, never dials, and has no vantage point on a handshake: TLS and the
token check both happen inside `accept()`, and the first thing the phone can publish is a session
that already exists.

Three reference states are therefore **not built**, and this is the unreachable-state rule rather
than a shortcut — a stage nobody can tell from a bug in its neighbour must not be drawn beside
stages that can:

| Reference | Built? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 04 *Searching* — "Looking for your Mac" | **no** | the phone does not look for anything |
| *Verifying* (the un-referenced screen in the brief) | **no** | not observable from this side |
| 05 *Connecting*, with a 3-step stepper | **as one honest state** | the phone observes neither "found" nor "verifying" |

What replaced them is `ConnectStage.Waiting`, which carries the one real quantity a wait has: the
token's remaining life, as a **determinate** bar and a `m:ss` countdown. Both come from
`Link.PAIR_TOKEN_TTL_MS` — the same constant `LinkServer` arms with — so the screen's deadline and
the server's cannot drift. On the emulator it read **4:18** for a 42-second-old scan.

**Reference 07 — "Confirm this Mac", with a fingerprint — is a true screen about the wrong path.**
That is the **v1 Sync** trust-on-first-use dialog (`PairingRequestDialog`, restyled in Slice 1 and
already shipping). In the v2 QR flow the QR **is** the confirmation: the fingerprint is in the
payload and pinned by `LinkTls` before any UI runs. Adding a second confirm step would be a weaker
trust decision bolted onto a stronger one. This is `CLAUDE.md`'s defect 63 exactly — a sentence that
is true of one of two paths, in front of a reader on the other.

**Reference 02's "Enter address manually" points the wrong way.** Manual IP entry is discovery
order #4 and it is the **Mac's** affordance, because the Mac dials. A phone has nothing to type an
address into. The honest inverse is **"Show this phone's address"**, which prints the real endpoint
from `PhoneAddress`. Same journey, and the direction the architecture actually runs.

**Reference 02's third trust column said "No cloud, no account, no data stored".** The last third is
false — Room holds a trust store, a transfer history and mirrored notifications. It ships as
*"No cloud, no account, nothing leaves your network"*, which is true. A privacy claim is the worst
place to round a sentence up.

### What was measured

| # | Reading | Control | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Entry renders with the phone's real address | the string is the emulator's actual `10.0.2.15` | PASS |
| 2 | "Show this phone's address" → real endpoint dialog | dialog text read back: `10.0.2.15:42501` | PASS |
| 3 | "Scan QR code" → the real camera flow | it raised the **real runtime CAMERA prompt** | PASS |
| 4 | QR screen runs the real pipeline | live preview + ML Kit analyzer bound | PASS |
| 5 | "Check Wi-Fi settings" → real destination | resumed `com.android.settings/.Settings$WifiSettingsActivity` | PASS |
| 6 | No-network is **real**, not staged | round trip: address → none → address | PASS |
| 7 | Phone suites | `--rerun-tasks`, artifacts 0-5 s old, exit 0 | **478 tests, 0 failures** |

**Reading 3 is the one worth keeping.** A screenshot of a camera screen proves a composable drew;
the *permission prompt* proves `QrScanScreen` mounted and asked the system for the camera. It is a
line only a running thing can emit, which is the property `CLAUDE.md` demands of a control after the
`Mirror session started` sighting.

**Reading 6, and its limit.** Wi-Fi and data off, then airplane mode: the app showed *No network
connection* both times, and returned to showing the address when they came back — so the reading is
responsive in both directions rather than stuck. **The mechanism is unconfirmed**: `ip -4 addr` still
listed `eth0` at `10.0.2.15` throughout (the AVD's fixed NAT interface), and `ip link show` returns
nothing to the shell user, so *why* that interface stopped qualifying was not established. Recorded
as a correlation, not a cause — the FGS/wake-lock retraction is the precedent.

**The risk that follows from it, stated rather than filed:** if `PhoneAddress.localIpv4()` can
return null for a reason not understood, it can do so on a phone that *is* reachable, and show
"No network connection" over a working setup. `ConnectStage` already puts `Connected` above
`NoNetwork` (tested), so a live session can never be hidden this way — but a reachable-but-not-yet-
connected phone could be. **The stimulus that settles it is one reading on the SM-S938B with Wi-Fi
on**: does the entry card print an address? Not taken; this slice ran on an emulator only.

### Red-first

`ConnectStageTest`, 10 tests. The boundary cases are transitions, which is the half
`LinkWaitStatusTest` structurally could not reach (defect 67):

- the expiry boundary from **both** sides, at `t0 + ttl - 1` and `t0 + ttl`;
- a refusal **after** the scan outranks the wait; one **before** it does not;
- `Connected` outranks `NoNetwork`, because a live session proves the interface read wrong;
- the countdown clamps at 0 rather than going negative.

`ConnectStage.of` composes `LinkWaitStatus.of` rather than restating its precedence — one rule, one
home, per the rule that two expressions eventually disagree.

**One test failed first and the test was wrong, not the code**: *a stale refusal stops outranking the
wait* asserted `Expired` at `t0 + 62 s`, against a **five-minute** token. Two clocks, and the
assertion read the wrong one. It now asserts `Waiting` and carries `assertTrue(late < t0 + ttl)` so
the next reader can see which clock is which.

### Fixed after looking at the device

1. **The art was invisible.** Two outlines at 12% white on `#0A0A0A` read as an illustration that
   had failed to load. A named `artEdge` token at 24% fixed it — a literal would have been the
   thing `check-color-tokens` exists to stop.
2. **The waiting art lit the Mac's screen** while the caption said the Mac had not arrived. Two
   writers on one surface, in pictures. `macLit` is now its own parameter and only a live session
   sets it.
3. **The harness lit a nav tab the real route leaves dark.** The Connect flow lives on `mac`, where
   nothing is selected; `PreviewNav` defaulted to 0 and drew Devices lime. An inaccurate harness is
   worse than none — it is evidence for a state the product never produces.
4. **The connected Mac card carried a server-rack glyph** (`Dns`). It is a Mac; it gets `Laptop`.
5. Two **dead affordances** were removed rather than styled: reference 02's header "?" and
   reference 03's "Having trouble?" row both go nowhere in this app, and the network requirement
   they would have explained is already standing copy on both screens.

### The rename

All user-visible copy now says **Sidekick**. `app_name`, `app_display_name`, the notification-listener
label, the accessibility-service label/summary/description, the pairing notification, and nine
in-app strings. The camera prompt read *"Allow ConnectSuite to take pictures"* before this.

**What deliberately did not change, because it is not copy:** `Download/ConnectSuite` (a real
directory — renaming it orphans every received file), `NsdAdvertiser`'s `serviceName` (**the
discovery protocol**; the Mac matches on it), `O=ConnectSuite` in the certificate subject,
`"ConnectSuite:link"` wake-lock tags, `Theme.ConnectSuite`, `.ConnectSuiteApp`,
`.ConnectSuiteInputService`, and the package. 478 tests green after it.

### Open

- **Not seen on real hardware.** Every reading here is from `sdk_gphone16k_arm64`. Per
  `scripts/target-device.sh`, an emulator is not a hardware reading.
- **`PairRejectReason` never reaches the screen.** `TOKEN_EXPIRED`, `TOKEN_MISMATCH` and
  `TOKEN_MISSING` are decided in `LinkServer`, sent to the Mac as `pair.rejected`, and published
  **nowhere the phone can render**. The phone's own expiry state is derived independently in the UI
  from the same constant, so the common case is covered; a *mismatched* or *missing* token still
  shows as a plain wait until it times out. The fix is one field on `LinkState` and one
  `_state.update` — **not made**, because it is link-layer code and the brief says to ask first.
- **No scan line on the QR screen.** Reference 03 draws a travelling lime line. It is motion, and
  motion has not had its pass.
- Waiting, Connected, Expired and Refused are **harness** captures — the emulator cannot pair with a
  Mac (it dials the phone, and `10.0.2.15` is unreachable from the host without forwarding; pairing
  also needs a QR through a camera that does not exist). Entry, QR scan and No-network are real.

## Android UI pass — Slice 3: Transfers and Folders (2026-09-22)

References `11` and `12`. Evidence: `docs/evidence/phase-7-android-slice-3/`.
Folders is the drill-down from the Transfers header, and Transfers stays lit while it is open —
measured, not assumed (the pixel probe from Slice 1).

### What the data layer actually offers, checked before anything was drawn

| Reference draws | Real? | What shipped |
|---|---|---|
| A **pause button** on every live row | **no** | `TransferStatus.PAUSED` is written by `TransferManager`/`BulkTransfers` when the **connection drops** — the error string is literally `"Connection lost"`. There is no user-initiated pause anywhere in the API. Pausing happens *to* a transfer here. **Cancel** is the one real live action and is what the row carries |
| **"Failed — retry"** as a control | **no** | `resumePausedTransfers` resumes `PAUSED` work; nothing resumes `FAILED`. A failed row shows its real `errorMessage` instead of a button that would not fire |
| A **search field** and a header **overflow** | **no** | neither has anything behind it |
| **"2 min left"** | **yes** | `TransferProgress.etaSeconds`, which was already written to return null when throughput is unknown |
| Per-type **colour** — blue images, red PDFs, purple video, orange archives | **no** | the category-hue system the brief rules out. The *glyph* still varies by type; the colour does not |
| **Downloads** as an addable folder | **no, and it must never be** | Android refuses `Download` to every app — the picker lists it and **disables** confirm. The reference offers it as a row *and* carries a card at the bottom explaining the wall: a row contradicting its own footnote |
| Per-folder **file counts and sizes** | **no** | counting a SAF tree means enumerating it, and `fs.list` over one 16,377-entry directory took **490 s** before the snapshot fix. Per folder, on every open |
| Documents / Pictures / Videos as a fixed **catalogue** | **no** | the model is *grants the user made* (`FolderRow`), not a folder directory |

**The quick picks are two by decision, not by breakage.** `FolderQuickPicks.ALL` offered four;
Documents and Pictures were removed on an explicit product call. Both were safe targets that
`EXTRA_INITIAL_URI` was measured honouring on this handset, and the comment in that file says so —
restoring them is putting two lines back.

### The defect found by writing the feed

`TransfersViewModel` puts `RUNNING` **and** `PENDING` in `active`, and drops from `history` only
rows that are `RUNNING` *and* in the progress map. A **`PENDING` transfer satisfies neither
exclusion and was rendered twice.** Nothing noticed, because two identical file names one above the
other read as two files rather than as a bug. `TransferFeed` de-duplicates, live row wins.

Two more decisions live in `TransferFeed` rather than in the composable, so a test can reach them:
a progress bar is drawn **only where one still means something** (live and paused; not completed,
failed or cancelled — those are over, and a bar invites watching), and the chip counts are computed
over **the same merged list the rows come from**, so a chip cannot claim a total its list does not
contain.

### What was measured

| # | Reading | Control | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Transfers tab → the real, empty Transfers | pixel probe: 4 tabs muted, Transfers at `(198,255,51)` | PASS |
| 2 | "Manage folders" → Folders, **Transfers stays lit** | same probe, same run | PASS |
| 3 | "Add folder" → the real SAF picker | resumed `com.google.android.documentsui/…picker.PickActivity` | PASS |
| 4 | A quick pick → the same picker, aimed | resumed `PickActivity`; degraded to the parent, which showed **"Can't use this folder"** live | PASS |
| 5 | Camera hidden from the picks once granted | harness state with Camera granted: only Screenshots offered | PASS |
| 6 | Phone suites | `--rerun-tasks`, artifacts 0-7 s old, exit 0 | **497 tests, 0 failures** |

**Reading 4 is worth more than a pass.** The aimed pick degraded to internal storage because the
emulator has no `DCIM/Camera`, and DocumentsUI then displayed *"Can't use this folder"* — the exact
refusal string recorded in `docs/evidence/saf-probe-2026-08-31/`. The wall this screen's copy is
built around was observed live, in passing, on this run.

### Red-first, four mutations, each against a 0-1 s old results directory

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| no de-duplication (the `PENDING` row drawn twice, verbatim) | **2 red** |
| history sorted oldest-first (the Overview defect's shape) | **2 red** |
| chip counts computed over the un-deduplicated inputs | **1 red** |
| finished rows carry a progress bar again | **1 red** |

### Two defects the device found that review did not

1. **"0 sec left".** `etaSeconds` is an integer division, so a transfer with under a second of data
   remaining computes to **0** — and *"4.2 MB · Sending to Mac · 0 sec left"* sat on screen beside a
   bar at 68%. The formatter was fine; the caller had to suppress zero. There is now a test for the
   boundary, written after the screenshot rather than before it.
2. **Two controls labelled "Add folder" on one screen** — the empty state's action and the
   persistent row. Found because `tap_named` **refused to guess** between two matching nodes rather
   than picking the first. The empty state now explains and the row acts.

The second is the more interesting one: a probe built to obey the discrimination rule reported an
ambiguity, and the ambiguity was not in the probe.

### Open

- Emulator only. No reading here is a hardware reading.
- **Populated Transfers and Folders are harness captures** — the emulator has no Mac, so it has no
  transfers and no granted trees. Empty Transfers, empty Folders, and both picker destinations are
  real.
- A paused row's subtitle wraps to two lines. It is the one row carrying a real error string plus
  what happens next, and it was left long deliberately.
- No row opens anything. The reference's per-row `⋮` is absent because there is no second action:
  no preview, no reveal, no share. When one exists it gets a menu.
