## Android UI pass — Slice 4: Clip and Feed (2026-09-22)

References `13` and `14`. Evidence: `docs/evidence/phase-7-android-slice-4/`.

### Clip: the reference's main control is the one thing this phone cannot do

Reference 13 shows **"Send what I copy automatically"**, switched on. There is no such setting and
there cannot be. `ClipboardManager.getPrimaryClip` is refused unless the app is **focused** —
Slice 11's measurement, 90 of 90 samples refused with the AccessibilityService bound and 60 of 60
with it disabled, each carrying the platform's own *"application is not in focus nor is it a system
service"*. `OnPrimaryClipChangedListener` never fires backgrounded. Phone → Mac happens in
`ClipFeature.onWindowFocused` and nowhere else.

The real setting is `SettingsStore.clipboardAutoApply` and it points the **other way**: whether an
entry arriving *from* the Mac is written to this clipboard without a tap. So the row reads
**"Apply what arrives automatically"**. Three sentences in the earlier brief were wrong against the
code, and re-reading the implementation rather than trusting the thread is what caught it.

**The direction chips have nothing to filter yet, and that is a real gap rather than a design
choice.** `ClipboardPayloads.History` genuinely holds 20 entries with kind, text, time and source —
duplicates collapsed, `KIND_SENSITIVE` never stored — and it is **private to `ClipFeature`**. It is
served to the Mac as `clip.history` and exposed to this screen only as `historySize`. So the screen
shows the most recent entry **each way**, which *is* exposed, with the held count beneath it.
Wiring the list is the same shape as the `pair.rejected` change and is **not taken here**.

The footer was checked rather than repeated: `onSessionEnded` calls `history.clear()` and resets
`PhoneState()`, and no code path writes the deque to Room or to a file. Memory-only, cleared on
disconnect — accurate.

### Feed: the reference has the direction backwards

Its subtitle is *"Notifications from your phone."* These are not this phone's notifications.
`MirroredNotificationEntity` is keyed `"<peerDeviceId>:<remoteKey>"` and written by
`MirroredNotificationRepository.onPosted` from a packet **another paired device sent**. Had that
gone unchecked, every sentence on the screen would have been wrong in the same direction.

**Reply does not exist on this side, and the check was specific.** Reply is a **Mac → phone** verb:
`notif.reply` arrives and `NotificationFeature.onReply` fires the originating app's own
`PendingIntent`. The phone *executes* replies. `MirroredNotificationEntity` carries no reply action,
no `canReply` and no `RemoteInput` — those live on the outgoing side in `NotificationRelay`. A reply
box here would have nothing to fire, and the "Can reply" filter would have no column to filter on.
There is no Sound setting anywhere in `SettingsStore`.

What is real and is drawn: the sender's own icon (`iconBase64`, downscaled before it crossed the
wire), the app name, title, text, `postedAtMillis`, and **dismiss**, which clears on the other
device too. `isClearable` is honoured — an ongoing call shows **no** dismiss, visible in the
harness capture.

### What was measured

| # | Reading | Control | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Clip tab → the real Clip | pixel probe: 4 muted, Clip at `(198,255,51)` | PASS |
| 2 | Feed tab → the real Feed | same probe | PASS |
| 3 | The auto-apply toggle **persists** | toggled, left to Devices, returned: still `true`; restored to `false` | PASS |
| 4 | Notification-access card appears when access is off | the revoke was **read back** before the screen was read | PASS |
| 5 | "Open notification access" → real destination | resumed `com.android.settings/.Settings$NotificationAccessSettingsActivity` | PASS |
| 6 | Phone suites | `--rerun-tasks`, artifacts 0-5 s old, exit 0 | **497 tests, 0 failures** |

**Reading 3's control is the point.** A switch that flips is not a switch that saves. The round trip
through another tab is what distinguishes `SettingsStore` from a `remember`.

**Reading 4 is the instrument failing four times in a row, caught by one command.**
`settings put secure enabled_notification_listeners ""` **silently does nothing** on this build —
the value read back **unchanged, immediately**. Four separate runs reported "the permission card is
absent" and every one of them was a reading of a stimulus that never happened. The supported route
is `cmd notification disallow_listener <component>`, after which the component really is gone from
the list and the card really does appear.

That is `CLAUDE.md`'s rule about establishing that the thing has been triggered before reading its
absence — and it took four rounds because the absence was *plausible*. The fix is one line and it
is now in the run: **read the setting back after writing it, before reading the screen.**

### Two defects found on the device

1. **The auto-apply switch had no accessible label and the row was not the target.** In the UI dump
   it was a bare `checkable` node with an empty `content-desc`, and tapping the label — which is
   what a person aims at — did nothing. The row is now `toggleable` with `Role.Switch`, full width
   (`[42,366][1038,557]`), and the label taps.
2. **`initialsOf` produced abbreviations, not monograms.** App names reached `AvatarBadge` for the
   first time and "WhatsApp" rendered as **"WH"**, "Gmail" as "GM". One word now gives one letter;
   two words still give two, so `Chetans-MacBook-Pro` is still `CM`.

### Unverified, and the stimulus that would settle each

- **The switch's screen-reader label.** Whichever order `semantics` and `toggleable` are declared
  in, Compose projects them into uiautomator as **two nodes at identical bounds** — one carrying
  `content-desc`, one carrying `checkable`/`checked`. TalkBack reads the merged tree and would
  announce both; a UI dump cannot show that. **Stimulus: TalkBack on hardware**, or a Compose UI
  test asserting `hasContentDescription` — there is no instrumentation source set in this project.
- **Dismiss was never tapped on real data.** The emulator has no paired Android device, so the real
  Feed is empty. `repository.dismiss` and its call site are unchanged. **Stimulus: a second paired
  Android phone.**
- Emulator only, as with every slice so far.

### Layout fixed after looking at it

The two explanatory cards stacked above the entries were **seven lines of prose before any
content**. The clipboard wall moved down beside the memory-only footer — neither is an error,
neither is urgent, and both are things read once. The toggle's sub-line went from four lines to one.

## Android UI pass — Slice 5: Mirror (2026-09-22)

Reference `15`. Evidence: `docs/evidence/phase-7-android-slice-5/`.

### This is the one reference that was already telling the truth

Four slices in, `15` is the outlier: almost everything it draws, the app does. Its best line is one
kept verbatim — *"The power and volume buttons stay out of reach either way. No app can press them,
ours included."* That is the locked platform wall (`INJECT_EVENTS` is signature-level and no
`AccessibilityService` can synthesise a `KeyEvent`) written as a reassurance rather than an apology.

**Its one overreach is the heading.** *"Your Mac can control this phone"* is stated as fact, and the
accessibility service it depends on may never have been granted. `InputOnboardingCard` has always
made that conditional — *"Let your Mac control this phone"* when it is off — and it observes
`Settings.Secure.ENABLED_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES` through a `ContentObserver`, so the card changes
under the user's hand. That stays exactly as it was; only the chrome changed.

### The defect this slice found was mine, from Slice 2

The Sidekick rename changed the accessibility service's label to **"Sidekick Input"**. Two pieces of
copy still told the user to look for **"ConnectSuite Input"**:

- `InputOnboardingCard` — the instruction for granting it;
- **`InputFailure.fixHint`** — the sentence shown *when input fails*, naming a Settings row that no
  longer exists.

Both now read "Sidekick Input". Worth stating plainly: a rename sweep that checks only the strings
it changes will miss every sentence that **names** one of them. The grep that found these is for
copy quoting a system row, not for the old product name — those were already clean.

### What was measured

| # | Reading | Control | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mirror tab → the real Mirror screen | pixel probe: 4 muted, Mirror at `(198,255,51)` | PASS |
| 2 | "Open Accessibility settings" → real destination | resumed `com.android.settings/.Settings$AccessibilitySettingsActivity` | PASS |
| 3 | The heading is conditional on the real grant | service off on this emulator → *"Let your Mac control this phone"*, and the body names **Sidekick Input** | PASS |
| 4 | The disabled Start **gates**, not just greys | tapped it: no activity change, no `MediaProjectionPermissionActivity`, no new mirror line in `link.log` | PASS, with the caveat below |
| 5 | Phone suites | `--rerun-tasks`, artifacts 0-5 s old, exit 0 | **497 tests, 0 failures** |

**Reading 4's caveat, stated rather than buried.** It is an absence with **no known positive**: the
consent prompt cannot be produced on this emulator, because raising it needs a connected Mac. So
what is proven is that nothing happened, not that the thing which would have happened is visible to
this query. The strong half is structural — `enabled` reaches `Modifier.clickable(enabled = …)` in
`ButtonShell`, so the callback is not merely styled away. **Stimulus for the real reading: a
connected Mac, then tap Start and watch `MediaProjectionPermissionActivity` appear.**

### A systematic mismatch, found by comparing and fixed once

Every reference draws a screen's own name at roughly twice the size of a card title. The shared
`SectionHeaderBar` was rendering them at `SidekickType.title` — the **same 21sp as a card heading** —
so the page name and the first card heading had identical weight and nothing on the page said which
was the page. One line in the shared header, and **Transfers, Folders, Clip, Feed and Mirror** all
corrected together. That is the argument for the header being shared, arriving three slices after
the decision.

### Open

- Emulator only.
- **The running mirror state is unseen.** `MirrorPhase.RUNNING`, `AWAITING_FOREGROUND`,
  `REQUESTING_CONSENT` and `STARTING` all have real copy, real tone and real geometry
  (`Capturing W×H at N dpi`) and none was rendered — every one needs a Mac to ask. Unlike the other
  slices, **no harness entry was added for them**: `MirrorStatus` is `MirrorEngine`'s own state, and
  a preview that constructed one would be showing a state machine the preview had written rather
  than one the engine produced.
- Carried from Slice 4, unchanged: the auto-apply toggle's TalkBack label, and dismiss on real
  notification data. Both need hardware or a second device; both are logged for a dedicated
  accessibility pass rather than chased here.

## Android UI pass — Slice 6: Mac management (2026-09-22)

**No reference image.** Built to the structure agreed in the brief and the density the other five
screens established. Evidence: `docs/evidence/phase-7-android-slice-6/`.

### Two things it deliberately does not do

**It does not use `HeroCard`.** There is exactly one gradient surface in this product and it is the
Devices overview's connection card — that rule is in `HeroCard`'s own KDoc and it is the single
thing keeping this app from reading as generated. The brief calls this screen's top card a "hero
card" meaning *prominent*, so prominence is bought with a 64dp badge, the display type and space.
A second gradient would have cost the first one its meaning.

**It offers no per-Mac Disconnect, because there is no such action.** Checked before drawing:
`forgetAndDisconnect` forgets *and* drops the session; `LinkServer.stop` stops the whole server;
`LinkService.stop` is reachable from no UI today and was not given one here. Nothing in the codebase
ends one session while leaving the pairing and the listener alone. A "Disconnect" button would have
had to be one of those two wearing the wrong label — the same test that removed the pause button
from Transfers.

Also absent for the established reason: **latency**. There is no ping on this side.

### The fingerprint rule, measured

Correction #6 says the security fingerprint appears only inside Mac management → Advanced. That is
now a reading rather than an intention:

| | |
|---|---|
| Advanced collapsed | **no** node on screen containing a key-shaped string |
| Advanced expanded | **two** — `A1:B2:C3:D4:E5:F6:07:18` and `30:30:C8:EB:CD:DC:D0:FB` |

Both halves in one run, so the absence has its positive. `DeviceIdentity.shortFingerprint` is the
formatter — the same one the pairing dialog uses, not a second one that happens to agree.

### What was measured

| # | Reading | Control | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Advanced expands and collapses | collapsed reading taken in the same run | PASS |
| 2 | The fingerprint is in Advanced and nowhere else | as above | PASS |
| 3 | No nav tab is lit | `PreviewNav(selected = -1)`, matching the real `mac` route | PASS |
| 4 | The hero card does not repeat the Mac's name | fixed after the first capture — see below | PASS |
| 5 | Phone suites | `--rerun-tasks`, artifacts 0-5 s old | **497 tests, 0 failures** |

### Fixed after the first capture

`LinkWaitStatus.Connected`'s headline is *"Connected to &lt;names&gt;"*, and this card's title is
already that name — so the connected state read **"Chetans-MacBook-Pro / Connected to
Chetans-MacBook-Pro"**. The sentence is now withheld in exactly that one state, where the pill at
the top of the screen already carries it. `LinkWaitStatus` keeps owning the wording for every state
where the name is not the answer; this is a decision about *duplication*, not about copy.

### The extraction, and why it was necessary

`MacManagementSection` is now a function of its inputs — status, link state, paired Macs,
capabilities, own fingerprint, callbacks — with `LinkRoute` passing the live values. Before this it
read `LinkController`, the Room database and `DeviceIdentity` itself, which means it could be
rendered in exactly one situation: the one the device happened to be in. **Every interesting state
on this screen needs a paired Mac**, and the emulator can pair with nothing. Same shape as
`DevicesSection`, `TransfersSection`, `FoldersSection`, `ClipboardSection` and
`NotificationsSection` — this was the last screen still reaching for its own data.

### Open

- **Forget was not exercised.** `onForget` reaches `server.forgetAndDisconnect`, which revokes the
  trust row *and* closes the live session — the distinction defect-era testing established. Firing
  it needs a paired Mac. **Stimulus: a real pairing, then Forget, then confirm the session ends and
  the row is gone** — and per `CLAUDE.md`'s WAL lesson, read the trust store *through the app or
  with the `-wal` file*, never by copying `connectsuite.db` alone.
- **"Pair another Mac" sets the same `scanning = true` flag** whose destination was measured in
  Slice 2 (the real camera flow, proven by the runtime CAMERA prompt). Not re-measured here.
- Harness capture, for the reason above. Emulator only.


## Sidekick feature pass — Feature B: Mac → phone (2026-09-23)

Running report: `docs/sidekick-feature-pass.md`. Destination for every live send below: the phone's
grant-free `downloads:connectsuite` root (*Received files*), which only ever gains files. Every file
sent was a generated sample (`sidekick-pass-*`), no user data.

### What was run, and what each run read

| Run | Instrument | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| 2 files, fresh names | `scripts/sidekick-send-probe.mjs` (card) and the phone's `link.log` | card: `arrived \| Arrived · checksum matched` ×2. Phone: `t-1… verified=true`, `t-2… 6291456 bytes in 168ms … verified=true` |
| the same 2 again | same | card: `Arrived as sidekick-pass-sample (2).txt`, `… -6mb (2).bin`. Phone: 2 refusals (`27 delivered / 1 refused`, `28 / 2`) then both received, `verified=true` — **nothing replaced** |
| 200 MB, Stop mid-way | `scripts/sidekick-stop-probe.mjs` | before Stop: `confirming \| 22 MB of 200 MB on the phone`, bar 0.109. After: `cancelled \| … stopped after 29622272 bytes and can be resumed.` |
| the same 200 MB again | same + phone log | phone: `reusing the pending item … 29622272 bytes already staged — this is the resume path`, `starting at 29622272`, received, `verified=false (nothing was agreed in advance)` — above the 64 MB pre-hash ceiling, reported as such on the card (`not checksummed`) |
| a real drop | `scripts/sidekick-drop-probe.mjs` | `oldPathProp: "undefined"`, `viaWebUtils: "/…/sidekick-pass-sample.txt"`; the card drew `Send 1 file…`; **Cancel pressed, nothing sent** |

Phone tally after the runs: `8 completed / 1 failed since start` — the one failure is the Stop.

### Defect 132 — every drop onto the phone failed on `File.path`

The drop tile read `file.path`, removed from Electron in v32 (this app is 43.4.1). A real Chromium
drop, dispatched at the centre of the named `#files-drop` element measured immediately before, gave
the page a `File` whose `path` read `undefined` — the old code's input — while `webUtils` returned
the real path for the **same** `File` in the same event. The unit double cannot see this defect
(its `pathForFile` reads the fake's own field), which is why the evidence is a live drop.

### Defect 133 — the Mac never read the phone's verdict

`fs.transfer.progress` and `fs.transfer.done` were emitted and dropped. The recorded envelope order
on a 60 MB send, renderer-side:

```
[603,"agreed","t-6-95883"],[674,"fs.transfer.progress",…,262144],[948,…,17825792],
[1184,…,40108032],[1569,…,62914560],[1570,"fs.transfer.done",…,62914560]
```

and a second 60 MB send sampled the drawn card at 866 ms as `confirming` with the batch bar at
**0.304** — the Mac's write had resolved and the phone had 30%. So the Mac's own completion is
bytes queued, and only the phone's `done` may say *arrived*.

### An instrument fault that found a product defect

The first Stop probe settled on `phase === 'sending' && bar > 0.05` and could never settle: by the
time the phone had reported 5%, the Mac's write had resolved and the item was `confirming`. That is
*a predicate over two clocks settling on one* (`CLAUDE.md`). Writing the probe correctly is what
showed the product had the same blind spot — **Stop looked only for a `sending` item**, so a Stop
pressed during `confirming` would never have reached the phone. Fixed in the same sitting, with a
view test that goes red against the old lookup.

### A layout defect found in the first capture

The first capture of the arrived card showed **no file name**: status and name shared a grid row,
and a long status took the `auto` column and squeezed the name to zero width. Now two lines per file,
tone on a glyph rather than on the words. `docs/evidence/sidekick-feature-pass-2026-09-23/b-send-*.png`
are the corrected captures; `b-send-synthetic-states.png` is **synthetic** — the pane's own reducers
fed invented ids, no transfer.

### Suites

Mac `npm test` 926/926, typecheck clean. Phone `ReceivedFilesTest` 5/5 (artifact 12 s old, Gradle
exit 0). The phone's received-file notification is **built and not yet observed on the device** —
the phone build carrying it is installed with Feature F's, once, to limit how often the real link
is interrupted.


## Sidekick feature pass — Feature C: Photos preview quality and video (2026-09-23)

### Root cause, read before anything changed

| Suspect | Finding |
|---|---|
| thumbnail instead of original | **Yes.** The detail preview was the grid's own `media.thumb` at `maxEdge: 256` — the same bytes as the tile |
| CSS scaling / `object-fit` | **Yes.** Drawn into a 4:3 well at `object-fit: cover`: ~1.2–2.5× upscale, and every portrait photo cropped to a landscape strip |
| stale cache | **Latent.** `PhotosClient.thumbsFor` keys its cache by id alone, so asking it for 512 after the grid's 256 would have returned the 256 as a hit. The preview now has its own cache |
| limited preview URL handling | **Yes.** CSP `img-src 'self' data:` — no way to show bytes from disk, so no original and no video was ever possible in the pane |
| decoding limitations | Real for HEIC stills and HEVC video on some Macs; now detected and said, not assumed away |
| the Android source query | No fault: `media.thumb` honours up to 512 and `media.original` streams real bytes |

### What the pane does now

The 512 px preview at once, **labelled as a preview**; images ≤ 40 MB fetch their original after a
350 ms dwell into a private temp cache (`main/mediaPreview.ts`, mode 0700, emptied at start, on
disconnect and at quit, 12 kept at most); videos fetch only on **Play**. A `sidekick-media://` URL
carries an opaque token, never a path, and answers `Range` (`shared/byteRange.ts`) so a video seeks.

### Live, on generated samples only

A 3000 × 4000 portrait JPEG and a 12 s 1280 × 720 H.264 MP4 were made on this Mac, sent to the
phone's Received files with Feature B (both `checksum matched`), and selected **by exact byte size**
— no other photo was opened. `scripts/sidekick-photos-probe.mjs`:

```
photo, original decoded → caption "Original · 3000 × 4000", scheme sidekick-media,
                          natural 3000x4000, drawn 246x329, object-fit contain, frame 3000 / 4000
facts                   → Name sidekick-pass-portrait-3000x4000.jpg · Photo · 680 KB · 3000 × 4000
video before Play       → caption "Video · 0:12 · 4.6 MB", action "Play", <video> elements: 0
video after Play        → "Original video · 1280 × 720", controls true, autoplay false, paused true,
                          duration 12, seekable [0, 12]
seek to 7 s             → currentTime 7, readyState 4, error null
```

**One reading is not reportable and is not claimed:** the 512-preview state before the original
decoded. The 680 KB original decoded inside the probe's first poll, so the instrument gave up on a
transient it could not catch (`stopped=deadline`). The preview caption is covered by
`photos.test.ts` instead.

Viewing wrote nothing to the receive folder: after the run `~/Downloads/Sidekick` held only the
photo that **Save to Mac** was pressed for; the two viewed originals were in the 0700 cache.

**Reveal in Finder** refuses anything outside the receive folder — `/etc/hosts`, a `../` escape
from inside it, and a prefix lookalike (`…/SidekickEvil/x`) all `false` — with the positive control
`true` on the file Save to Mac had just written.

### Observed during the run, not caused by it

At 01:03–01:04 the Mac log shows the app being used by a person while these probes ran: rows
selected in Received files (the pane's existing selection prefetch pulled `inbox-probe.bin`,
`nogrant-probe.bin` and later `sidekick-pass-stop-200mb.bin` into `~/Downloads/Sidekick`), every
Files root opened in turn, and Photos opened twice. No probe in this pass clicks a Files row; the
readings above select their own items by byte size and are not affected.

### Suites

Mac 940/940 (+`byteRange.test.ts` 6, `photos.test.ts` +8 — red on *listing size beats decoded
size*), typecheck clean, colour and contrast guards green with `--media-stage` added as a
theme-fixed token beside `--media-scrim`.


## Sidekick feature pass — Feature D: Files grid, sort and filter (2026-09-23)

`shared/filesListing.ts` owns the rule (`visibleEntries`): natural name order, folders first under
every sort, **unknown dates and types last in both directions**, a case-insensitive filter over the
name and the resolved app label, and the input never reordered in place (it is the pager's cursor).
Sort and filter act on the **loaded** entries only and the footer says so while more is unloaded;
an explicit **Load more** sits in the footer because a filtered list may be too short to scroll.

### Live, on the phone's Received files (13 entries, all test files)

`scripts/sidekick-files-view-probe.mjs`:

```
default order         → inbox-probe.bin, nogrant-probe.bin, sidekick-pass-60mb (2).bin, …  (13)
Size ↓                → 200 MB ×2, 60 MB ×2, 6 MB …; nonIncreasing true, drawn == model true
filter "sidekick-pass"→ 11 rows; footer "11 of 13 items loaded match “sidekick-pass”"
filter to nothing     → "Nothing loaded here matches “zzqqxx-no-such” … Clear filter"
grid                  → portrait JPEG → picture; .bin → BIN, .mp4 → MP4, .txt → TXT
```

**The phone was only read.** In the probe's window the Mac log carries 6 `fs.list` and 1 `fs.thumb`
and **0** `fs.delete` / `fs.mkdir` / `fs.transfer.begin` / pushed / pulled lines — the same pattern
matched `pulled` lines earlier the same night, so the zero is a reading.

### A product defect the probe caught

The first grid read was **NOT REPORTABLE** (empty after 10 s). Inspected: `query` still held the
previous text. Clicking Grid re-rendered inside the filter's 120 ms debounce, and the toolbar wrote
the **old** query back into the field — erasing what had just been typed before the debounce read
it. A person who types and then clicks anything loses the text. Fixed (the field is written back only
when no keystroke is pending); `filesView.test.ts` *a render inside the filter's debounce does not
erase what was just typed* goes red against the old line. The unchanged probe then passed.

### Layout, from the first capture

The toolbar wrapped into three rows and stranded **Send to phone…** alone. Now two: breadcrumb and
Send, then filter (taking the free width), sort, direction and the List | Grid pair. Evidence
`docs/evidence/sidekick-feature-pass-2026-09-23/d-grid.png` (Received files: test files only).

### Suites

Mac 952/952 (`filesListing.test.ts` 8, `filesView.test.ts` +4), typecheck clean.


## Sidekick feature pass — Feature E: Set up Sidekick (2026-09-23)

### Defect 134 — four features no screen could turn on

Read from the code before building anything: the only `ActivityResultContracts` in shipped code are
`SyncRoute`'s file and folder pickers, `QrScanScreen`'s camera, and onboarding's notification
permission. **Nothing requests SMS, Calls, Contacts or Photos**, while onboarding tells the user they
are asked *"from the Sync tab, when you turn them on"*. The SM-S938B's grants agree: `READ_SMS`,
`READ_CALL_LOG` and `READ_CONTACTS` are `granted=true` **without `USER_SET`** — set by `adb`, not by
a person tapping Allow — while `CAMERA`, `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` and `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES`, which do have
UI, carry `USER_SET`.

### What was built

`SetupPlan` (pure, 10 items in three sections — the link, what the Mac can do, staying connected)
and `SetupScreen`. What it deliberately does not ask for: `NEARBY_DEVICES` (defect 69 — the Mac link
was measured not to need it), and the camera (reported only; the scanner asks at the moment it is
needed). Every feature has **Not now**. Status is read from the OS on every resume.

### On the emulator only — the SM-S938B's data was never cleared

`emulator-5554` (Android 16, SDK 37), `pm clear` then a fresh first run, every tap resolved from a
fresh `uiautomator dump` by text or by the permission controller's resource id:

| Step | Reading |
|---|---|
| onboarding → *I'll do this later* | lands on *Set up Sidekick*, **0 of 9 turned on**, camera *Asked when you scan* |
| Texts → Allow → the system's own dialog *"Allow Sidekick to send and view SMS messages?"* → Allow | row **On**, **1 of 9**; `dumpsys package`: `READ_SMS`, `RECEIVE_SMS`, `SEND_SMS` all `granted=true` **with `USER_SET`** |
| Calls → Allow → **two** dialogs (call log, then phone) → Don't allow, twice over | row **Turned off in Settings** (amber), action **Open Settings** — Android's second-round dialog used `permission_deny_and_dont_ask_again_button`, after which it answers without a dialog |
| Show notifications → Open Settings → Back without changing it | Settings opened `NotificationAccessSettingsActivity`; back in the app the row still reads **Off**; `enabled_notification_listeners` lists two other packages and not ours (the control: the query can see the list) |
| Done | lands on Devices (the not-paired outcome) |

Two instrument faults, both caught before a reading: a helper matched only `permission_deny_button`
and missed the second-round id (no tap happened, and the next dump showed the dialog still up); and
a cold start had not drawn onboarding yet, so every tap was **refused** rather than guessed — the
retry waits for the node instead of sleeping.

### A layout fault from the first capture

The title and scrolled content drew under the status bar. The scroll region now starts below it and
ends above the gesture bar (`statusBarsPadding` / `navigationBarsPadding` before `verticalScroll`).
`e-setup-first-run.png` is the corrected capture; `e-setup-texts-on-calls-blocked.png` was taken
before the fix, mid-scroll, and shows the states it is named for.

### Not exercised

The phone half on the SM-S938B: installing there interrupts the real link, and is done once, with
Feature F. Photos' Android 14+ *Select photos* (partial) answer reads as **Off** here, because the
feature itself needs images **and** videos in full; that is the same test `MediaFeature.granted`
applies, so the row and the Mac's `photos` capability cannot disagree.


## Sidekick feature pass — Feature F: the mirror request while the app is backgrounded (2026-09-23)

### The platform rules this is built inside (official Android behaviour, not assumptions)

- **Every MediaProjection session needs fresh consent**, shown by Android; an app cannot answer it.
- **Background activity launches are restricted** (Android 10+): a backgrounded app may not bring
  itself forward. A *notification tap* is the user's gesture that allows it — the route already
  measured on this handset (`MirrorEngine` → `AWAITING_FOREGROUND`).
- **Full-screen intents** (`USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT`) are, since Android 14, granted by default only
  to calling and alarm apps; others must be granted by the user, and Play policy restricts them to
  those uses. Sidekick is neither, and a window thrown over another app asking about screen capture
  is exactly what a spoofed system prompt looks like. **Not used.**

### What changed

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| notification | *"<Mac> wants to mirror your screen" / "Tap to open ConnectSuite and start mirroring."* | *"<Mac> wants to see this phone's screen" / "Tap to review. Android will then ask you to approve screen sharing."*, a named **Approve screen sharing** action, `category=reminder`, and `setTimeoutAfter(30 s)` — gone when the request is |
| tap | the Mirror tab's generic state card and Start button | a **request card**: who asked, what sharing lets them see (including notifications that appear, and control with Sidekick Input on), that Android asks next in its own words, what stays black, a countdown from the real consent timer, **Continue** (then Android's prompt) or **Decline** |
| decline | not possible except by letting it time out | `MirrorFailure.DeclinedOnPhone` through `fail()` — the Mac hears *"Screen sharing was declined on the phone."*, distinct from a refused system prompt |
| copy to the Mac | *Tap "Start now" on the phone.* — a label this Samsung does not show (it reads *Next* then *Share screen*) | *Approve screen sharing on your phone.* No sentence quotes a button (`ConsentCopyTest`, red against the verbatim old sentence). *ConnectSuite* → *Sidekick* in every mirror sentence and in the Mac's three *Sidekick Input* instructions |

## Defect 137 probe — the provider answers an empty cursor (2026-09-23, 10:06)

Owner-approved debug-only `-r` install on the pinned SM-S938B (`RZCY12330DT`), to split the children
query from the row parse. **Not fixed; no grant requested; no file touched.**

**The instrument.** `SafChildrenProbeActivity` (debug manifest only, `Theme.NoDisplay`, finishes at once)
calls `SafTreeStore.probeRootChildren(20)` for each tree from `FsRoots.all`: the same
`buildChildDocumentsUriUsingTree`, projection and resolver as `childrenOf`, the tree **root** only, no
cache, no recursion, at most 20 rows (hard ceiling `PROBE_MAX_ROWS`). Rows are classified by
`parseRow` — the one home `entryOf` now delegates to, so the probe and the listing cannot disagree about
what a rejection is. It logs counts, column names, extras *keys* and exception class names; no name,
document id or extra text.

**Install preserved everything** (read before and after):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| tree grants | DCIM / Documents / Pictures `persisted=0x3`, `persistedCreate` 1788211970787 / 1788259600815 / 1788259570873 | identical |
| notification listener / accessibility entries naming the package | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |
| `granted=true` | 28 | 28 |
| `trusted_devices` (copied **with** `-wal`) | 1 row, `b59f4bbaf2fc…` | 1 row, `b59f4bbaf2fc…` |
| link (`scripts/link-up.sh`, after `am start -n …/MainActivity`) | 3 OK, 1 session | 3 OK, 1 session — the Mac reconnected unaided |

**The reading:**

| tree | cursor | `count` | columns | examined / cap | accepted | rejected | extras | failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Documents | returned | **0** | the 5 requested | 0 / 20 | 0 | — | none | none |
| DCIM | returned | **0** | the 5 requested | 0 / 20 | 0 | — | none | none |
| Pictures | returned | **0** | the 5 requested | 0 / 20 | 0 | — | none | none |

`count` is the cursor's own, taken before the parse loop, so **`entryOf` is ruled out**: there were no rows
to drop. No `EXTRA_LOADING` (not a pending async load), no `EXTRA_ERROR`, no exception.

**What else would produce 0, and why each is ruled out or not:**

- *The folders are empty* — no. `ls -A /sdcard/<dir> | wc -l` through the shell: DCIM **29**, Documents
  **1**, Pictures **229**. DCIM 29 and Documents 1 are the exact counts the app listed before the flip.
  This is a **different client** (shell uid, no SAF), so it proves the directories are populated and
  nothing about what the provider serves us.
- *A stale provider process* — no. `com.android.externalstorage` started 09:05:58, hours after the flip,
  and answers 0.
- *A lost grant* — no. Persisted, unchanged across the install, and `fs.stat` resolves through it.
- *The instrument cannot see a row* — **not controllable here without a new grant**, since every granted
  tree is the thing under test. What bounds it: it is the product's path, which listed DCIM 29 at 00:47:44,
  and the failing value (`count`) is read from the provider's cursor, not produced by our loop.

**Boundary:** `ExternalStorageProvider` returns a well-formed, empty children cursor for these trees to
this uid. Per the brief, the run stopped there — no re-grant, no `MediaStore`/path fallback. (`logcat -c`
was run once before the probe, through the pin, so the probe's lines stood alone; it discarded the
device's logcat buffer, not `link.log`.)
Suites: sync-module 250/250 with the refactor.

### Defect 139 — one photo-access state, on both ends (code; device run blocked)

Per Android's Selected Photos Access guidance for `targetSdk 36`: `READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED` declared and
requested with `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES` and `READ_MEDIA_VIDEO` on 34+ (`MediaAccess.requestFor`), which removes the
compatibility mode measured before the fix. `MediaAccess.of(granted)` is the one state:

| Granted (from the OS) | State | Phone checklist | `capabilities` | `limited` | Mac Photos pane |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| images + video (or storage ≤ 32) | full | On | `photos` | — | no notice |
| selected-photos only | selected | *Some photos allowed* · *Change selection* | `photos` | `photos` + the phone's sentence | *Some photos allowed* + that sentence |
| nothing (or images alone) | none | Off / Not now / Turned off in Settings | — | — (`unavailable` carries the reason) | *Thumbnails only* |

`docs/protocol.md` gained `limited` before either side used it.

**Mutations** (each run: fresh results, exit 1; restored: exit 0):

| | Mutation | Red |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | manifest declaration removed | first **green** — `CapabilityPermissionTest` accepts any one declared alternative. Red after adding *every permission MediaAccess asks for is declared* |
| P2 | selected read as full (the compat-grant defect) | 4 `MediaAccessTest` tests |
| P3 | contract alternatives without the selected grant | *permitted exactly when access is not none* |
| P4 | no limited reason | 2 tests, including *full to selected-only is a change the Mac is sent* |
| P5 | selected-photos permission not requested on 34+ | *Android 14 and later ask for …* |
| P6 | checklist says *On* for selected | 3 `SetupPlanTest` tests |
| M1 | Photos pane ignores `limited` | 1 of 963 |
| M2 | teardown leaves `limited` behind | 2 of 963 (`session.test.ts`) |

**Not reached by any test**, so unproven until a device run:
- `CapabilityDetector.refresh` building `AdvertisedState` with `limited()`, since it needs a `Context`;
- the `limited` JSON the session emits;
- `link.ts` storing it;
- `renderer.ts` handing it to the pane;
- the checklist ordering `Limited` before the refusal check;
- **what Android actually grants for each dialog choice once the permission is declared.**

Owed, on an isolated emulator:
- full access, selected-only, denied, and each after a process restart;
- *Change selection* opening the platform picker;
- the Mac pane's wording against a live `capabilities.changed`.

Blocked: 316 MB free on the Mac after the builds.

### Defect 145 — the Devices screen says Offline while the Mac is connected

Found in the run above. With `link-up.sh` at one session ESTABLISHED and Mac settings reading *Connected*,
Devices read *Offline*, *Paired with Chetans-MacBook-Pro · waiting for it to connect*, *Your Mac: Not
connected*, and drew *Send files* disabled — twice, 5 s apart (`s-07-devices-after.png`).
`DevicesSection` sets `connected = mac?.isConnected`; `DeviceRepository` fills `isConnected` from
`ConnectionManager.connectedDevices`, the v1 Android-to-Android transport. The Mac is on v2 `LinkServer`.
Not fixed; fix direction in the register.

#### Defect 145 — fixed (2026-09-23, 15:10–16:07)

**The trace — every Mac element on Devices and what it read before:**

| Element | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| header pill *Connected / Offline* | `Device.isConnected` (v1 `ConnectionManager`) | `MacLinkView.connected` |
| hero line *Connected to … / Paired with … · waiting* | same | same projection |
| address chip | `Device.address`, shown only if v1-connected | `MacLinkView.address`, shown when connected |
| *Your Mac* card (icon tint, *Connected / Not connected*) | same v1 flag | projection |
| **Send files** | enabled on the v1 flag; tap → `TransferManager.send`, which needs `connections.connectionTo(mac)` — v1, never present for the Mac | **disabled with a reason** on every link state, `MacLinkView.canSendFiles = false` |
| Start mirroring, the reason under it | `link.isConnected` (v2 — already right) | `MacLinkView.connected`, one source |
| Quick actions (Mirror, Files, Clip, Feed) | not gated on the link — navigation only | unchanged |
| Mac settings (pill, badge, name, address) | `state.isConnected` / `state.clients` / the trusted row, inline | the same `MacLinkView` |

`ConnectionManager` is untouched; the v1 device list below the overview still reads it for Android-to-Android.

**Why Send files is not lit on the v2 link.** There is no phone-to-Mac send: `TransferManager.send` is v1-only,
and a phone-initiated transfer to the Mac is Feature A, blocked on a protocol decision. Gating the button on
the live link would move the defect from *says Offline* to *promises a send that fails*. Its reason line:
*"Sending files from this phone to your Mac isn't available yet — send them from the Files pane on your Mac
instead."*

**Tests.** `MacLinkViewTest` (core, 5) drives connect → drop → reconnect through `afterListeningStarted`,
`afterSessionReady` — the connect edge, extracted from an inline `copy()` in `LinkServer.onSessionReady` so
a test can reach it — and `afterSessionEnded`. `DevicesMacSourceTest` (sync-module, 4) holds the wiring, with
a control showing its matcher sees the defect line. Mutations, each reverted:

| | Mutation | Red |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | **the defect verbatim** — Devices takes the Mac from `state.devices` | 2 `DevicesMacSourceTest` |
| M2 | projection reads *paired* as *connected* | 2 `MacLinkViewTest` |
| M3 | `afterSessionReady` writes nothing | 3 `MacLinkViewTest` |
| M4 | Send files gated on the link | 1 `DevicesMacSourceTest` |
| M5 | projection claims a send path | 1 `MacLinkViewTest` |

refused, and the results the harness printed were 76 s old — the previous run's. The age column is what
showed it; it was re-run with a unique anchor and went red at 0 s.

### Feature F — review on the SM-S938B (2026-09-23, 16:34–16:55)

**What F is** (`d9e681e`, mirror-module, the Mac's three mirror sentences, `docs/protocol.md`). **Before it:** a
backgrounded `mirror.start` already posted a notification — *"<Mac> wants to mirror your screen" / "Tap to open
ConnectSuite and start mirroring"*, `CATEGORY_STATUS`, no action, no expiry — and three sentences quoted
*"Start now"*. **F added:** the named action *Approve screen sharing*, `setTimeoutAfter(30 s)`, `CATEGORY_REMINDER`
on the `IMPORTANCE_HIGH` channel `screen_mirror_request`; Sidekick's own request card (who, what is shown, a
countdown from the real timer, Continue / Decline); `MirrorFailure.DeclinedOnPhone`; no quoted button labels. No
full-screen intent (Android 14+ reserves it for calling and alarm apps).

**Method.** The Mac driven by id through `probe.mjs` (`#mirror-start`, `#mirror-stop`, the overlay, the note; control:
the section's button count); the phone read from `dumpsys notification --noredact` (control: Sidekick's other
notifications counted in the same read), `uiautomator` and both logs. Pairing, trust, folders and permissions were
checked before and after (see the accessibility note below). The owner put the phone down on the home screen
before the runs; one run where the phone was in use (16:36) is void.

| Run | What | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Start, Sidekick backgrounded | notification in 3 s: *"Chetans-MacBook-Pro wants to see this phone's screen"* / *"Tap to review. Android will then ask you to approve screen sharing."*, action **Approve screen sharing**, `timeout=PT30S`, importance 4. Mac overlay: *"…Approve screen sharing on your phone — tap the Sidekick notification, or open Sidekick › Mirror."* |
| 1 (cont.) | untouched | **expired at 30.0 s** (16:35:05.404 → 16:35:35.411), notification gone, Mac Start re-enabled — **with the old copy** pointing at the removed notification (fixed, `cfb38d1`) |
| 4, 6 | tap the notification in the shade | **Sidekick → Mirror** in front with the request card, *"This request ends in 21s"*; the notification removed itself |
| 3, 5, 7 | the same tap | **no reading**: the shade closed between `uiautomator`'s dump and the tap, and the tap reached the launcher (`HoneySpace … checkMultiFingerGesture`), which ignored it. Samsung also groups Sidekick's notifications, and a tap in the shade can expand the group rather than fire it. The instrument, not F; runs 4 and 6 are the reading |
| 2, 6 | Continue with the clock nearly out | expired before the tap — **5–7 s per `uiautomator` dump** on this phone; slow instrument, not a product failure |
| 8 | open Sidekick › Mirror during a request → Continue | Android's own `MediaProjectionPermissionActivity`: *"Share your screen with Sidekick?"*, default **Share one app** with **Next**; switched to **Share entire screen**, the button becomes **Share screen** |
| 8 (cont.) | Share screen | a real session: `Encoded +26 frames (13.0/s)` then static-screen ticks; Mac `session: active`, overlay hidden. **Stop from the Mac** → phone `stopped-by-mac`, projection released 4 ms later, `dumpsys media_projection` → `null` |
| 9 | Decline on the card | Mac: *"Screen sharing was declined on the phone. If that was a mistake, start mirroring again from this Mac."* — **the same sentence on the phone's own screen** (fixed to *"your Mac"*, `75f5363`; verified after on both ends) |
| 10 | Stop on the Mac while the phone's request is pending | notification removed within 3 s; phone Mirror tab *"Mirroring was stopped from the Mac."*, no Continue/Decline left. **The phone wrote no log line for it** — noted, not changed (pre-F path) |
| 11 | untouched, then retry | new copy on both ends: *"Screen sharing was not approved within 30 seconds, so the request ended." / "Start mirroring again from your Mac, then approve screen sharing on your phone."*; an immediate retry posted a fresh notification |

**A late approval is dropped, and nothing says so.** After Continue the timer re-arms for Android's prompt; when
it expired with the prompt still up (16:40:38), *Share screen* tapped at 16:41:14 logged *"Screen capture consent
granted"* and started nothing — no projection (`null`), the phone still showing *"Mirroring stopped"* under
Android's dialog (`f-03`). The app cannot dismiss Android's prompt. Not changed: the consent timer predates F.

**Heads-up.** The notification is importance 4 (heads-up eligible) and Samsung drew an edge-lighting window at
post time; a heads-up was **not** seen in a dump taken 6 s later. Whether and how long One UI shows it is the
OEM's, and was not measured.

**Copy fixed** (each its own commit): `cfb38d1` the timeout; `75f5363` the decline hint; `bd4b295` the Mac's note
under Start (*"Waiting for the phone. Approve screen sharing on your phone."*), moved into
`shared/mirrorSession.ts` where a test reaches it. No Mac or phone sentence quotes *"Start now"* or any label of
Android's prompt; `ConsentCopyTest` and `mirrorSession.test.ts` hold it.

**Sidekick Input was switched off at 16:25:46 by a Force stop in Settings, not by this work.**
`dumpsys activity exit-info`: `reason=10 (USER REQUESTED) subreason=21 (FORCE STOP) … from pid 26472
(com.android.settings)`; `dumpsys settings` history: `enabled_accessibility_services` → `null` by `android` at
16:25:46.261 (and once before, 09-19 08:31:56). No command was sent to the phone at that time; every other exit
today is `PACKAGE UPDATED` (the installs) or the 14:55 photo revoke. It was **not** re-enabled from adb — it is
the owner's switch. Everything else in the baseline is unchanged.

### Android motion pass — items 1, 2, 4, 5 of the approved proposal (2026-09-23, 17:05–17:55)

Survey and audit by `find-animation-opportunities` and `improve-animations` (read-only); the Mac's motion is
unchanged, including the brand breath; item 3 of the proposal (the Mac mirror-overlay fade) is held. Every
duration and curve is a shared `Motion` token (`core/ui/SidekickDimens.kt`), the Mac's `--dur-*` / `--ease`
ported. Compose scales them by Android's `animator_duration_scale` — read by ui-android 1.9.1, confirmed in
the jar — which is the setting behind *Remove animations*; the Samsung's was never changed, so reduced motion
was measured on the emulator. Widths below are read per frame from `screenrecord` videos (`ffmpeg`, PIL);
recordings drop unchanged frames, so rows are the frames where something changed.

| Order (proposal #) | Commit | What | Normal motion (measured) | Remove animations (emulator) |
|---|---|---|---|---|

### Defect 146 — the force-stop guard does not run on pinned-wrapper commands

`no-force-stop.sh` is registered with `"if": "Bash(adb *)"`. During motion item 1 a command beginning with a
variable and calling `scripts/adb-pinned.sh emu … am start -S -n com.chetan.connectsuite.debug/…` ran without the
hook firing, and force-stopped Sidekick **on the emulator**. The same command fed to the hook directly is denied —
the matcher is right, the registration is too narrow, and it is narrow in exactly the form this repo requires for
device writes. The Samsung was not touched. Open; fix direction in the register.

#### Defect 146 — fixed (2026-09-23)

`.claude/settings.json`: the `no-force-stop.sh` entry loses `"if": "Bash(adb *)"` (one line). The matcher was
unchanged — it already denied every wrapper form; it was simply never asked about commands that did not start
with `adb`. `scripts/hooks/no-force-stop.test.sh`, text fixtures only:

| Expect | Command shape |
|---|---|

| deny | `scripts/adb-pinned.sh samsung shell am start -S -n com.chetan.connectsuite.debug/…` |
| deny | `adb -s "$(scripts/target-device.sh samsung)" shell am start -S -n com.chetan.connectsuite.debug/…` |

| deny | the verbatim command that reached the emulator (`SP=/x; $SP/e shell am start -S -n …DesignPreviewActivity …`) |
| pass | `scripts/adb-pinned.sh samsung shell am start -n com.chetan.connectsuite.debug/…MainActivity` |

## Feature A — URI grant lifetime, emulator (2026-09-23, evening)

The experiment `docs/phase-7-share-proposal.md` §4 required before any Feature A code. Instrument:
commit `a79efa1` — the debug-only `ShareGrantProbeActivity`, with its rules in `ShareGrantRun`
(12 tests; four rule mutations each turn one red). It reads the shared stream inside the activity
before `finish()` as the control, then reopens the same URI from the same process at +1 s, +30 s and
+120 s after `onDestroy`, recording whether the foreground `LinkService` was running in the process.
It logs the authority and the exception **class**, never the URI, a path, a display name or the
exception message.

**Device: Pixel 10 emulator only.** The results below are the run's results as accepted by the owner;
raw log lines are not reproduced here.

| Source app | Authority | Control (inside the activity) | +1 s | +30 s | +120 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Google Photos | `com.google.android.apps.photos.contentprovider` | read succeeded | `SecurityException` | `SecurityException` | `SecurityException` |
| DocumentsUI | `com.android.externalstorage.documents` | read succeeded | `SecurityException` | `SecurityException` | `SecurityException` |

The foreground `LinkService` was running in the same process. The control succeeding on both rows is
what makes the six failures a reading about the grant rather than about the file or the instrument.

**Consequence:** rev 1's architecture — finish the Share-receiving activity and read the URI later
from `LinkService` — is **rejected**. The proposal is revised to rev 2: the activity copies the file
into private staging (`cacheDir/share-staging/`) before it can finish, computing exact size, SHA-256,
sanitised name and MIME type, and only the staged copy is ever streamed, after the Mac accepts.
Nothing of Feature A is implemented.

**Not yet proven:** the same on the SM-S938B (Samsung Gallery, Samsung My Files). It must be repeated
there before release validation; not run, and not approved yet.

**Left in place on the emulator, untouched:** `/sdcard/Pictures/SidekickShareTest/sidekick-share-test-image.png`,
`/sdcard/Documents/SidekickShareTest/sidekick-share-test-file.bin`, and `/sdcard/window.xml`. None is
deleted without asking.

No build, install, device command, protocol change or `docs/protocol.md` change was made for this
entry.

## Feature A — private-staging proof on the SM-S938B (2026-09-24, 09:12–09:33)

The debug-only staging proof, commit `b3eca15` (`ShareStaging`, `ShareStagingProbeActivity`,
`ShareStagingSweepProvider`). It is not Feature A: no offer, no socket, no Mac, no protocol change.
It copies one shared file into `cacheDir/share-staging/` while the receiving activity still holds the
grant, hashing as it writes. `docs/phase-7-share-proposal.md` rev 2 §5.

**Device and install.** The SM-S938B (`RZCY12330DT`), with every device write through
`scripts/adb-pinned.sh samsung`. The Pixel 10 emulator was attached as well and was not touched. The
built APK and the installed one had the same package id, the same `versionCode`/`versionName`, and
the same signing certificate (SHA-256 `d3a505d2…7d26`, read from the installed `base.apk` with
`apksigner`). After `install -r`, 28 of 28 runtime grants were intact, as were the
notification-listener and accessibility bindings. `LinkService` was started again by name
(`am start -n …/MainActivity`, no `-S`), and the Mac reconnected: 3 ports listening, 1 connection
established on 42501. At the end the same state was measured again, with auto-rotate still `0`.

**Stimuli: synthetic files only**, generated on the Mac and pushed, then left in place:

| Path | Bytes | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `/sdcard/Pictures/SidekickShareTest/sidekick-share-test-image.png` | 230,778 | `1afc71b6e565b83262b3d50089f28e053eca14d3e351c4fe8b771590ff65c84c` |
| `/sdcard/Documents/SidekickShareTest/sidekick-share-test-file.bin` | 100,000 | `b5f989fe09daf7ab2d2f5af458812cd7e417624d40325f6f3d0502c6bb2b6e4d` |

The hashes were computed on the Mac before the push, and again on the phone after it. Gallery was
opened on the image's own MediaStore row (`Filmstrip 1 of 1`), and My Files was opened on the folder
itself (one row). No other media was listed or read.

### Samsung Gallery — authority `media` (a MediaStore URI), provider size not reported

| Stage | Result | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Control read inside the activity | **pass** | the source re-read after the copy: `sourceRereadMatch=true` |
| Copy, count and digest | **pass** | `staged bytes=230778`, the SHA-256 equals the Mac-side hash, `readBackMatch=true`; `run-as sha256sum` on the staged file gives the same digest |
| Preflight with an unknown size | **pass** | `expected=unknown`, `limit=23673573003` (bounded by free space) |
| Staged copy readable after Finish | **pass** | `after-finish +2000ms staged=ok bytes=230778 match=true`, activity records = 0 |
| Source read fails after 32 KiB | **pass** | `SourceReadFailed`, `files left for this attempt: none` |
| Simulated low space | **pass** | refused before any copy: needed 268,435,457 bytes, 134,217,728 free, `limit now 0` |
| Cancel mid-copy | **pass** (third attempt) | control: a 36,864-byte `.part` existed mid-copy; `Cancelled(bytesWritten=40960)`, `filesLeft=none` |
| Recreate mid-copy | **pass for the copy** | recreated 1.5 s into an 8.6 s copy; the copy completed with every digest matching |

**The limit on the Gallery rows:** after Finish the source was **still readable** (`source=ok`). That
is **confounded, not a finding about the grant.** Sidekick holds `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES`
(`granted=true`, user 0) for the Photos feature, so it can open a `content://media/…` URI with no
share grant at all. For the same reason, the successful re-open after recreation says nothing about
whether the grant survives recreation. Gallery does not answer the grant-lifetime question on this
phone unless that permission is revoked, and it was not.

### Samsung My Files — authority `com.sec.android.app.myfiles.FileProvider`, size 100,000 reported

| Stage | Result | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Control read inside the activity | **pass** | `sourceRereadMatch=true` |
| Copy, count and digest | **pass** | `staged bytes=100000`, the SHA-256 equals the Mac-side hash, `readBackMatch=true`; the same via `run-as sha256sum` |
| Preflight with a known size | **pass** | `expected=100000`, `limit=23674574661` |
| Staged copy readable after Finish | **pass** | `after-finish +2000ms staged=ok bytes=100000 match=true` **while the source failed**: `source=failed exception=java.lang.SecurityException` |
| Source read fails after 32 KiB | **pass** | `SourceReadFailed`, nothing left for the attempt |
| Simulated low space | **pass** | refused: needed 268,535,456 (= 100,000 + 256 MiB), 134,317,728 free |
| Cancel mid-copy | **pass** | control: a 36,864-byte `.part`; `Cancelled(bytesWritten=45056)`, `filesLeft=none` |
| Recreate mid-copy | **pass: the grant survived recreation** | `recreation=1 … reopen ok=true bytes=100000`, with the matching digest; the copy completed (`staged` 2.3 s later) |

My Files is the source that separates the grant from Sidekick's own permissions: Sidekick has no other
access to that provider. **Its source read after Finish failed with `SecurityException` while the
staged copy read fine.** That is the rev 2 premise, seen on the Samsung. It is **one reading at
+2 s**, not the full §4 instrument (+1 s/+30 s/+120 s). The recreation re-open succeeding is a real
reading that the grant survives an activity recreation on this phone.

### What was not tested, stated rather than implied

- **Physical rotation was not tested.** Auto-rotate is off on this phone (`accelerometer_rotation=0`)
  and changing it was out of scope. Recreation was driven by the probe's Recreate button
  (`Activity.recreate()`), which relaunches through the same path a configuration change uses.
- **Process-death cleanup is JVM-tested only.** Killing Sidekick was out of scope, so
  `ShareStagingSweepProvider`'s startup sweep never ran on the device against a real orphan. The
  sweep's rules are covered by `ShareStagingTest` (orphans, symlinks, a symlinked directory,
  live/young/unrecognised entries) with seven mutations each red.
- **Zero-byte and space-dropping-mid-copy are JVM-tested only.** There was no zero-byte synthetic
  file on the phone, and the synthetic files are smaller than the 8 MiB re-check interval.

### Instrument faults, recorded so the next run does not repeat them

- **The first two Gallery cancel attempts held no reading.** `uiautomator dump` waits for the UI to go
  idle, and the probe redraws every 150 ms during a slow copy, so the dump before the Cancel tap
  blocked until the copy had finished (measured at **10.68 s** during a copy, against 2.3 s idle).
  Cancel then arrived at a finished copy and correctly did nothing. The passing runs tapped Cancel at
  bounds resolved from a dump taken just before Start, and a `.part` listed mid-copy is the control
  showing the copy was running when Cancel landed.
- **Swipes on Samsung's share sheet closed it**, and the later swipes paged the owner's home screen
  (swipes only, no taps, nothing opened). The owner picked the target by hand once; after that,
  Samsung listed a grouped **"Sidekick"** entry, whose sub-menu names both debug activities, so later
  picks were made by exact label.
- **The probe's 10-minute expiry deleted the first staged Gallery copy** during the run
  (`expired after 600000ms deletedFiles=2`, 09:28:01). That is the bounded-retention rule working as
  designed; its log lines and `sha256sum` had already been captured.

### `scripts/link-up.sh` is unsafe with two devices attached

It calls `adb` without a serial. With the Samsung and the emulator both attached it failed with
*"cannot read …'s uid (device offline, or not debuggable)"*. That is a false failure: the same three
reads run through `scripts/adb-pinned.sh samsung` showed the link up. **Do not use it unqualified
while two devices are attached.** The script is unchanged; fixing it is a separate task.

### Defect 147 — check-suites-run blocks non-commit commands while staged sources are stale

The hook is registered `"if": "Bash(git commit *)"`. During slice 1 (2026-09-24, around 09:40–09:55),
with the slice's `git mv` staged and the phone results older than it, the hook denied these commands.
**None of them was a commit:**

| Command shape | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `python3 - <<'EOF' … EOF` editing a source file | denied |
| the same shape, a second time | denied |
| `t0=$(date +%s) && ./gradlew -q testDebugUnitTest … ${pipestatus[1]} … python3 - <<EOF` | denied |
| `t0=$(date +%s) && ./gradlew … ; python3 script.py $t0` (no heredoc) | denied |
| `date +%s > file && JAVA_HOME=… ./gradlew -q testDebugUnitTest > out 2>&1; echo "gradle exit $?"` | **ran** |
| `for c in …; do … $c …; done` with a stale/red result present | denied |

Every denied command contained `$(…)`, `${…}`, a heredoc or a loop variable, and the plain one ran.
That is a **correlation from about six sightings, not a reading of the harness**: how the `if`
treats a command it cannot fully parse was not examined. The effect was a deadlock: the hook's own
message asks for `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`, and that command, written with substitutions, was
itself denied. Open, and not fixed in slice 1 or 2 by instruction; fix direction in the register.

## Feature A slice 2 — negotiation, offer, decline, cancel; no transfer (2026-09-24, 10:36–10:40)

`docs/protocol.md` → Extensions and Share. Protocol major stays **1**: `ext` on `hello`/`hello.ack`
is optional, `share.offer` goes only to a Mac that negotiated `share.file`, and a Mac of this
revision declines every valid offer with the `not-available` **stub**. That is not a person's
decision: there is no card, no Accept, no transfer and no file saved. **Offers come only from the
debug `ShareOfferProbeActivity`** (synthetic generated bytes); an ordinary share still stops at
*Ready* with Send disabled.

**Automated.** Phone **680/680**, Mac **986/986**, both written by their own runs. New tests:
`ExtensionsTest` (phone) and `extensions.test.ts` (Mac), both reading
`docs/fixtures/ext-negotiation.json`; `ShareOfferTest` (every transition, answer-once, another
session's answer, `accept` refused, expiry never a decline, and every end deleting the staged copy);
`shareOffer.test.ts` (one case per malformation rule, replay, busy, not-negotiated, the skew
boundary); `share.test.ts` (the receiver never sends `accept`, silent mode, tally). **Nine
mutations, all red on fresh results**: P1 another session may answer, P2 an ending keeps the
staged copy, P3 expiry reported as a decline, P4 `ext` value 0 accepted, M1 an unnegotiated offer
judged valid, M2 a replay answered again, M3 `rootId` unchecked, M4 the stub accepts, M5 a string
version accepted. All guards pass; `check-protocol-spec` counts the three `share.*` types as
specified.

**Hardware: SM-S938B (pinned) and the development Mac app**, relaunched from this tree only. Same
signer (`d3a505d2…7d26`). After install: 28/28 grants, listener and accessibility intact. The Mac's
identity files and pairing record were hashed before and after the run and are **unchanged** (same
paired phone, same `pairedAt`); every relaunch reconnected through last-known, with no re-pair.

| # | Pair | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| A | new phone, **real old Mac** (the build running since 2026-09-23, before this slice) | phone: `ext: Mac advertises nothing; negotiated nothing`. Probe: `offer … not made: Chetans-MacBook-Pro did not negotiate share.file — nothing sent, nothing awaited`, `NotNegotiated`; staging 0 entries. The Mac log wrote **0 lines of any kind** in that window, so its silence is no reading; the phone's line is the evidence |
| B | new and new | both sides `negotiated {share.file: 1}`. 100,000-byte offer: Mac `valid` → `decline not-available` → phone `ack … state=declined` → `staged copy deleted, 2 file(s)`, **129 ms** end to end. A **zero-byte** offer (`sha256 e3b0…b855`) the same. Tallies agree on both sides |
| C | Mac with `shareSilent` (debug) | the offer held unanswered with a 20 s life; the staged copy was present at +5 s. At +20 s the phone logged **`expired`** (not declined), sent `share.cancel{expired}` and deleted the copy; the Mac logged *"expired, not declined"*. **Defect found and fixed here:** the Mac counted that one expiry twice, once from its own timer and once from the phone's cancel 57 ms later. It now counts a cancel only for an offer it still held. The test is red with the old line and green with the fix |
| D | Mac quit with an offer live (10 min life) | at 10:39:14.047, within the second of the quit, the phone logged `ended with the session: staged copy deleted, 2 file(s)`, with no message sent |
| E | Mac with `shareOmitExt` (debug old peer) | identical to A: the phone `negotiated nothing`, the offer `not made`, nothing sent; the Mac `negotiated {}` |

The run ends with the Mac relaunched **with no switches**, `share.file` negotiated, the link up
(3 listening, 1 established), staging empty, and the two synthetic source files untouched.

**Not observed on hardware:**
- **`accept`, a Mac-initiated `share.cancel`, a replay, a malformed field, and `busy`.** No Mac of this
  revision sends them. They are covered by `ShareOfferTest`, `shareOffer.test.ts` and `share.test.ts`.
- **An offer from a real user share.** Not wired, by instruction.
- **A process death with an offer live.** Not produced (G15); the startup sweep covers the staged copy.

## Feature A slice 3 review — a read of the committed code before the transfer (2026-09-24)

A read-only review of `29d2ac4`: no edit, build, device command or relaunch. It was made to specify
version 2 (the transfer) from the code rather than from the proposal, and it found that the proposal
had described one rule that does not exist.

| # | Finding | Where | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | A bulk pull is claimed by `transferId` alone; `Pending.sessionId` is read only by `forgetSession`. **The proposal's §8 said a claim from another session is refused "by the existing `Pending.sessionId` rule". There is no such rule.** | `BulkTransfers.kt:339-345`, `serve()` `:380-422` | defect 148; proposal §8 and plan slice 3 corrected in place; the share pull binds the session itself (contract) |
| F2 | `transferId` = `t-<counter>-<millis mod 100000>`, predictable | `BulkTransfers.kt:195` | defect 148; share ids are 128-bit random (contract) |
| F3 | The Mac publishes with `fs.rename` after choosing the name with `freeName`, so a file that appears meanwhile is replaced | `bulk.ts` commit; `files.ts:333`, `photos.ts:269` | defect 150; share publishes exclusively (contract) |
| F4 | `bulk.pull` removes an unrecorded `<name>.part` before a fresh pull, which may be another app's | `bulk.ts` start of pull; `transferFiles.ts:40` | defect 151; share uses `.<offerId>.sidekick-share.part` (contract) |
| F5 | A failed pull keeps its `.part` for resume, and a checksum failure writes a `.failed` sidecar | `bulk.ts` | share deletes its partial on every failure and writes no sidecar (contract) |
| F6 | No idle timeout after the bulk connects (`setTimeout(0)`), and no free-space check on the Mac's receive side | `bulk.ts:151-157` | share: 30 s idle, free space ≥ `size + max(256 MiB, ⌈size/10⌉)` (contract) |
| F7 | A `share:` root on any `fs.*` verb falls through to `ROOT_NOT_GRANTED`, `feature: "files"` | `FsFeature.kt` each `FsRoots.find` | contract: `NOT_FOUND`, `feature: "share"`, one test per verb (3c) |
| F8 | `fs.transfer.cancel` is keyed by `transferId` alone, and a claim for an unknown id is tagged `feature: "photos"` | `FsFeature.onCancel`; `BulkTransfers.kt` `serve()` | defects 148 and 149 |
| F9 | `ShareOfferProbeActivity` and the other adb-driven probes are exported with no permission | `app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml` | defect 152; slice 3b |
| F10 | A version-1 phone answers `accept` with `BAD_REQUEST`, so a transfer-capable Mac must know before accepting | contract | `share.file` 2 means both can transfer; a version-1 peer stays offer/decline-only |

**The owner's decisions (2026-09-24):**
1. **Where hard links are unsupported, the save is refused** (`unsupported-destination`). No
   placeholder-then-rename, no overwrite.
2. **Synthetic transfer tests write only to a dedicated development-only receive folder.** It is
   ignored by packaged builds, never changes the configured receive folder, and is never Downloads or
   any personal folder. Its exact path is shown before the first file is written there.
3. **`share.file` 2 means both peers can transfer.** A version-1 peer stays offer/decline-only, and no
   transfer may start with it.
4. **Test acceptance only through a development-build switch** that accepts identified synthetic probe
   offers. It defaults off, never accepts an ordinary share-sheet offer, and never works in a packaged
   build. No production auto-accept.

`docs/protocol.md` → Share now separates **version 1 (implemented)** from **version 2 (specified, not
implemented)**. `share.saved` is on `check-protocol-spec`'s specified-not-on-the-wire list, with its
reason, until the commit that adds it to `MessageType`.

### Defect 148 — a bulk pull is not bound to its session, and its id is guessable

Read from `BulkTransfers.kt` at `29d2ac4`. `serve()` parses the header and calls
`pending.remove(transferId)` with no reference to `channel.session`. The only reads of
`Pending.sessionId` are in `forgetSession`, which drops a dead session's pulls. `nextId()` is
`"t-${counter.incrementAndGet()}-${System.currentTimeMillis() % 100000}"`. `FsFeature.onCancel`
forwards any `transferId` to `BulkTransfers.cancel`. No device reading; the defect is in the code's
absence of a check, and the review is the record. Only paired, pinned Macs hold a session token, which
bounds the exposure. Open; not fixed in Feature A beyond the share path.

### Defect 149 — a bulk claim for an unknown transfer is always tagged photos

Read from `BulkTransfers.kt` at `29d2ac4`: the unknown-`transferId` branch of `serve()` sends
`NOT_FOUND` with `feature = "photos"`, whatever the pull was for. No device reading. Open.

Read from `desktop/src/main/bulk.ts` and `shared/transferFiles.ts` at `29d2ac4`: `partPathFor(d)` is

### Defect 152 — debug probes are exported with no permission

Read from `app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml` at `29d2ac4`: the adb-driven probes are
`exported="true"` with no `<intent-filter>` and no `android:permission`, among them
`ShareOfferProbeActivity` (offers data to the paired Mac). Any installed app can start an exported

**Correction, made in slice 3b before the fix:** the 3a entry also named `FsProbeActivity` (which can
arm the corruption hook). Enumerating the manifests found that **no manifest declares it**. The debug
manifest declares six activities; the built debug APK lists no `FsProbeActivity`. The classes
`FsProbeActivity`, `ClipProbeActivity` and their siblings exist in `app/src/debug/…/probe/` with no
component, so nothing can start them, adb included. The claim was made from the class list rather
than from the manifest; the manifest is what decides reachability.

#### Defect 152 — fixed (slice 3b, 2026-09-24)

**What is exposed, enumerated from the manifest:**

| Activity | Exported | Filters | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DesignPreviewActivity` | yes | 0 | `DUMP` |
| `PhoneAddressProbe` | yes | 0 | `DUMP` |
| `SafChildrenProbeActivity` | yes | 0 | `DUMP` |
| `ShareOfferProbeActivity` | yes | 0 | `DUMP` |
| `ShareGrantProbeActivity` | yes | SEND | unchanged: the share sheet must reach it; it reads only what is shared with it |
| `ShareStagingProbeActivity` | yes | SEND | unchanged, same reason |

**The gate's premise, read on both devices:** `com.android.shell` holds `android.permission.DUMP` on
the SM-S938B (SDK 36) and on the emulator (SDK 37), and `pm list permissions -f` gives its protection
level as `signature|privileged|development` on both. An app cannot obtain it by installing; only a
person with adb can grant a `development` permission.

**Red first.** `DebugProbeGateTest` (`app/src/test`): every exported, filter-less debug activity
requires `DUMP`; the offer probe specifically; the two share-sheet probes keep their filter and no
permission. Against the old manifest, the first two failed, the first naming all four activities; the
third passed. With the gate, 3/3 pass. Phone suite **683/683**, written this run. `aapt2 dump
xmltree` of the built debug APK shows `DUMP` on exactly the four.

**The gate demonstrated in both directions, on the emulator only**, with two throwaway apps of about
8.6 KB each, built from SDK tools in the scratchpad: `com.sidekick.gatetest.target` exports `Gated`
(`DUMP`, no filter, the same shape as the probes) and `Open` (no permission, the control), and
`com.sidekick.gatetest.caller` requests no permissions. The emulator was used because Samsung installs
were not permitted and the emulator cannot fit Sidekick's 94 MB APK.

| Case | Reading (logcat, tag `GateTest`, 11:15:25–28) |
|---|---|
| caller (uid 10240, `holds DUMP=false`) → `Gated` | **refused**: `SecurityException: Permission Denial: starting Intent { … cmp=com.sidekick.gatetest.target/.Gated } from ProcessRecord{… uid=10240} requires android.permission.DUMP` |
| the same caller → `Open` (control) | **started** (`Open STARTED`), so the refusal is the permission, not a caller that cannot start activities |
| `adb shell am start` → `Gated` | **started** (`Gated STARTED`): the adb path works through the gate |

**What this does not prove:** it proves the platform mechanism with an identical attribute, on SDK 37.
It does not prove Sidekick's own gated APK on the SM-S938B, where no install was permitted. That
reading (`scripts/adb-pinned.sh samsung shell am start` of `ShareOfferProbeActivity` still works) is
owed at the next approved install. The two test apps are still installed on the emulator: they are
the owner's to keep or remove, and they were not removed without asking.

## Feature A slice 3c — the phone half of version 2, built and not advertised (2026-09-24)

`docs/protocol.md` → Share → Version 2, phone side only. **No device command, install or Mac change
was made.** The phone still advertises `share.file: 1` (`Extensions.PHONE`, pinned by
`ExtensionsTest`). Negotiation is `min(mine, theirs)`, so in any live pairing, even with a
version-2 Mac, the phone refuses `accept` and authorises no pull. A test drives exactly that path:
a v2 Mac against this phone negotiates 1, `accept` gets `BAD_REQUEST`, and a pull on the root is
`NOT_FOUND`. Ordinary share-sheet Send stays disabled.

**What was built:**
- `ShareOffer`: accepted → sending → awaiting verdict → saved, or failed → retry from byte 0 → expired.
  **Only `share.saved {ok:true, verified, full size}` reaches Saved**; the phone's own finished send
  reaches *awaiting verdict* and no further, and 60 s without a verdict becomes `failed (unconfirmed)`.
  The Retry window is `min(failedAt + 5 min, expiresAtMs)`. Every end deletes the staged copy, and
  a live pull is stopped first.
- `ShareRoot`: routing. On a `share:` root only a pull `fs.transfer.begin` goes to Share; every other
  `fs.*` verb is refused, `NOT_FOUND`, `feature: "share"`. Share transfer ids are `ts-` + 128 random bits.
- `BulkClaim` and `BulkTransfers.serve()`: a share pull is bound to its session and to offset 0, and a
  wrong claim is refused and the socket closed **without consuming the entry**. Unbound entries (every
  Files and Photos pull) are claimed exactly as before (defect 148 is separate).
- `FsFeature`: every handler is wrapped by the share-root intercept at one point. A
  `fs.transfer.cancel` naming a `ts-` id goes to Share, which answers only the session that owns it.
- `ShareFeature`: `share.saved`, the pull (the staged copy only; a missing or wrong-length copy
  ends the offer as `staging-lost`), and the verdict and Retry timers.
- The capability contract gains `share.saved` and the bulk channel. `share.saved` is in
  `MessageType` and is on `check-protocol-spec`'s phone-only list until the Mac half.
- **The corruption trigger** (owner ruling 1): `ShareFeature.debugArmCorruption(offerId, byte)`,
  scoped to **one offer's next pull**. It refuses unless the build is debuggable, writes an `E` line
  when armed, and its one caller is the `DUMP`-gated debug `ShareOfferProbeActivity` (extra
  `corruptAtByte`, default off). `FsProbeActivity` was read first, not exposed, and is still declared
  in no manifest. It arms a **global** one-shot corruption of the next pull of any kind, and its class
  comment says it appears in the debug merged manifests, which it does not. Both are recorded here and
  it was left alone.

**Contract additions** (for 3d): the offer-time destination check, a Sidekick-owned probe file
hard-linked in the receive folder at the offer and at Accept. Only a completed link counts as
support; anything the check cannot establish declines `folder-unavailable` and fails safe. It is not
a substitute for the exclusive save. `unsupported-destination` joins the decline reasons.

**Automated.** Phone suite **725/725**, written by this run, with the debug APK building. New:
`ShareOfferV2Test` (33 tests) and `ShareRootTest` (9: every `fs.*` verb enumerated from `MessageType`
by reflection, one refusal per verb by name, Files roots untouched, id randomness, and the bulk-claim
rule). Slice 2's `ShareOfferTest` passes unchanged. **Eleven mutations, all red on fresh results
and all compiled:**
- V1 accept at version 1
- V2 the phone's own send counted as Saved (13 tests)
- V3 an unverified save accepted
- V4 a pull or verdict from any session
- V5 any item pulled
- V6 a bulk claim that ignores the session
- V7 `fs.stat` reaching Files on a share root
- V8 a Retry window running past expiry
- V9 no verdict deadline
- V10 predictable share ids
- V11 an ended offer taking a verdict. This one went red through the end-deletes test; the
  duplicate-verdict test did not go red, because a separate check on which states may take a
  verdict also blocks it.

**What the tests do not reach, stated rather than implied:**
- The Android wiring: the `FsFeature` wrapper, `ShareFeature`'s handlers and timers, and
  `BulkTransfers.serve()`'s use of `BulkClaim` (entry kept on a wrong claim, `onEnded` from
  `streamTo`'s `finally`). The rules they call are tested; the calls are not. They run for the first
  time in 3e, with the Mac half.
- **No real transfer has run**, by instruction. The bytes path, the corruption flip reaching a Mac, and
  the verdict round trip are 3e.

**Files and Photos:** unchanged in behaviour. Their related defects are already registered (148
session binding and predictable ids, 149 the `photos` tag, 150 rename-over, 151 stranger `.part`
deletion) and are not fixed here.

**What was built** (`desktop/src/main` unless noted):

Every socket-driven test has a 10 s timeout, so a mutation that removes the idle timer shows up as a
