  2026-09-17 and `Sidekick Safe Storage` created 2026-09-20 — consistent with the development and packaged
  builds sealing under different item names, which is the mechanism of 2026-10-08's overwrite.

#### Defect 208 — a listing race, not only the thumbnail queue

- Mechanism found reading the pane: a root switch while the previous listing is in flight makes the new
  `loadMore` return (`loading` is true); the old page lands in the **new** root's list; the grid then asks the
  new root about old ids — and the new root is never listed. Red: `asked downloads:connectsuite about
  primary:DCIM/Camera/IMG_1.jpg, which belongs to another root`. Main process red: `the old root's queued batches
  were still sent`. Phone red: `expected NotInRoot but was Gone` (results file 0 s old, gradle rc 1).
- **7 mutations red**; the phone ones read from result files 0–1 s old with `failures="1"`, so none is a
  compile failure read as a test failure (`tests/208-mutations.txt`).

Red: `activities that would join Sidekick's task expected [] but was [.SendSelectionActivity]`. The guard now
covers every activity reached by `SEND`, `SEND_MULTIPLE` or `PROCESS_TEXT`; 2 mutations red (an affinity equal
to the package; a neighbour losing its empty affinity).

#### Item 4 — ML Kit replaced by ZXing core 3.5.3

- Licence Apache-2.0 (read from `zxing-parent-3.5.3.pom`); no runtime dependencies; 291 classes, none
  referencing Android, sockets, `URLConnection`, processes or file writes; `java.net` appears only as
  `URI.create`/`URLDecoder.decode` in result parsers the scanner never calls.

  with the app's `QR_OPTIONS`, converted to luminance bytes with `pngjs`, placed in a 640×480 frame with a
  704-byte stride, in four orientations. Red first against a stub (3 of 5). 6 mutations red; 2 equivalent mutants
  (a dead length guard; a catch of a subclass the next clause already caught) removed as dead code.
- **Before → after, release:** runtime classpath Google artifacts **16 → 0**; merged manifest components
  **26 → 20** (ML Kit init provider and discovery service, `GoogleApiActivity`, `datatransport`'s discovery
  service, job service and alarm receiver removed); permission list identical. APK **25 MB → 5.1 MB**.
- **Instrument faults caught here:** a `stat`/`grep` on an empty variable read stdin and hung a shell for
  10 minutes (the Gradle run itself had finished in 32 s); a component diff by regex compared **0 with 0**
  because the tags span lines — re-read with an XML parser; an APK unzip stopped on a case-insensitive filename
  collision and extracted no dex, so every count *including the positive controls* read 0; `strings` could not
  read the dex at all (the manifest-guaranteed `MainActivity` read 0) — replaced by a byte search whose control
  read 1. None of these was written down as a finding.
- **Claim kept and now true:** *"No cloud, no account, nothing leaves your network"* — phone main sources hold
  **0** `http` strings across all six modules (control: 6 socket files found by the same search).

  separate the two conditions.
- **Next:** overnight, phone unplugged and untouched, lock still disabled — the owner's choice — to set against
  the earlier overnight reading taken with the lock held.
- Evidence: `docs/evidence/release-candidate-2026-10-09/205-hour-B/` (ticks, crossings, a batterystats extract
  with other apps' rows left out).

### Instrument faults this run, none written down as a finding

- **The cancel probe's first version read only the single-card layout** of the receive window. With more than
  one offer the window draws a queue (`#sw` reads `queue`, `#sw-one` hidden), so the probe waited while the file
  it existed to cancel saved in full. It now reads both layouts and targets the card that was not on screen when
  it attached (two saved cards of the same name were). Control run: 4 existing cards seen, none touched.
- **Its second version passed at 0 bytes.** `R < N` holds for 0, so a cancel that landed before the bulk socket
  claimed anything read as *mid-transfer*. It now waits for `--at-fraction` of the bytes and labels the case.
- `share-accept-probe.mjs` read the **packaged** profile's log (`sidekick-desktop`) — stale since 207 (b) moved
  the development app to `sidekick-desktop-dev`; caught before use.
- A 12:40 log window for an event at 12:30 returned nothing; a zsh `UID=` assignment failed (read-only in zsh);
  a phone-side glob was expanded by the Mac's shell. Each produced an empty read that was re-run, not recorded.

### What changed on the devices

Phone: debug build `21570962…` installed; re-paired to this Mac; **both 205 debug markers still present**
(overnight); `adb logcat -c` was run once (the logcat buffer, not Sidekick's own log); synthetic files in
`Download/SidekickBeta/` (1 MiB, 300 MiB) and `Pictures/SidekickBeta/` (3 PNGs). Mac: profile
`sidekick-desktop-dev` created by copy; `~/Downloads/Sidekick` gained `sk-b6-collision.bin`,
`sk-b6-collision (2).bin`, `sk-b8-cancel-300mb.bin`, `sk-b8-cancel-300mb (2).bin` (two full saves before the
cancel probe worked), `sk-b7-2.png`, `sk-b7-3.png`, and `sidekick-pass-stop-200mb (9).bin` from B10. Nothing
was deleted.

### Defect 205 — the night without the lock (2026-10-09 17:30 → 2026-10-10 08:36), and the owner's decision

The phone was left unplugged with the lock off (debug marker) and the per-minute ticker on. Evidence:
`docs/evidence/release-candidate-2026-10-09/205-night/`.

- **The Mac slept at 19:01:53** (`pmset -g log`: *Clamshell Sleep*), with maintenance wakes about every 15 min
  all night. The Mac's request probe therefore covers 17:38–18:58 only (17 samples: 8 ok, 9 *not connected*
  17:53–18:33 while the Mac reconnected, then ok); it ended with *unsettled top-level await* — a CDP read that
  never answered once the Mac slept. Recorded as a bound of the instrument, not a link reading.
- **The lock is held only while a Mac is connected** (`LinkService.kt` — `if (state.isConnected) acquireLocks()
  else releaseLocks()`). So with the Mac asleep the normal build would also have held no lock for most of the
  night: this run measured **a mostly disconnected night**, not *lock off* against *lock on*. The 2026-10-07/08
  soak (176 mAh, `ConnectSuite:link` held 8 h 54 min) had a Mac awake and connected.
- What it does show: deep idle from **03:15** (ticks 9–49 min apart, which is the CPU sleeping — the ticker
  cannot run without it); the phone **accepted** the Mac's reconnects at 22:23, 22:56, 00:55 and 01:12 with no
  lock; batterystats since the last charge (~01:20, **7 h 16 min** on battery): CPU awake **31 min** (7.1 %),
  screen on 4 min 42 s, 229 mAh computed = actual, **Sidekick 0.955 mAh**.
- **Not measured:** whether a link survives deep Doze **without** the lock while a Mac stays awake.
- **Owner's decision, 2026-10-10:** keep the lock and state the cost — ≈ 20 mAh per connected hour (≈ 0.4 % of
  5,000 mAh), released when the Mac sleeps or disconnects. Stated in the privacy draft §3 and the tester guide.
  Register: `docs/defects.md` → 205 (accepted, with reopen conditions).
